entries.vision: Make /dashboard/prediction-claims update DAILY, not weekly. User: page not update many day, wants update continue day by day. ROOT CAUSE (router RAW-confirmed + PO-verified live): page + /api/prediction-claims + predictionClaimsHandler are HEALTHY — do NOT touch them. The DATA PRODUCER is starved: prediction_claims has only 9 rows, newest 2026-06-14 (agentId 08-prediction-synthesizer). The synthesis flow (digest-predict/flow/monday.md, P-3..P-5 create_prediction_claim) was DISABLED by Sprint 1949-T5 (Monday prediction synthesis removed — Sunday weekly covers full scope); the Sunday weekly.md flow only READS get_prediction_accuracy, it never calls create_prediction_claim. So NO active flow has produced a claim since 1949-T5 — the 06-14 batch was the last routed run. Live confirm: get_prediction_accuracy(30d)=no results; calibration Brier=0.1379 healthy (product is SOUND, just unfed).
entries.product_decision: Option (a) chosen: re-enable prediction synthesis on a DAILY cadence by routing digest-predict to a daily prediction sub-flow + a new daily cowork slot, WITHOUT disturbing the Sunday weekly calibration report. Daily update = a daily synthesis run that CREATES new high-conviction claims when fresh evidence appears AND lets existing open claims keep accruing toward their multi-day/weekly horizon (e.g. W26). It is NOT a forced 5-claims-every-day spam. GUARDRAILS (designed by architect first): (1) per-DAY cap (small, e.g. 2-3) replacing the monday max_prediction_claims_per_week:5, with a weekly ceiling so cadence cannot inflate claim volume; (2) same-day idempotency marker via task_claim (TTL ~20h) keyed on day+slot so a re-fire never double-creates; (3) NO-OP cleanly when no ticker passes the bullish/bearish>0.6 high-conviction filter (do NOT lower the bar to manufacture daily claims — standing no-fake-data directive); (4) Sunday weekly.md calibration report stays unchanged + un-regressed.
entries.success_metric: LIVE: prediction_claims gains new rows on consecutive (high-conviction) days; /dashboard/prediction-claims generatedAt + rows reflect them day-over-day; daily/weekly caps honored; flat-market day no-ops without fabricating claims; Sunday weekly MARKET calibration dish still fires unchanged. entries.vision: An agent CANNOT persist incomplete or malformed data anywhere in the project. Every agent write surface is schema-validated; a rejected write throws a descriptive error naming exactly which required field is missing/invalid so the agent understands and self-corrects. Stored data is guaranteed-complete and future-proof.

entries.vision: When any frontend data surface goes stale AT REST, the system automatically DECIDES the root cause and ROUTES a remediation: mint a dev FIX task if the fetch/writer CODE is broken, OR call the responsible refresh agent (market-watcher / news-scout / the cron fetchers) to re-run if the data merely wasn't refreshed — with NO alert spam. This is the auto-REMEDIATE layer (conceptually FFT-L6) sitting ON TOP of L4 detection. Detection already exists and emits SLA-breach signals, but today they DEAD-END: alert-commander suppresses freshness-sla-monitor urgent_news every cycle as infra noise (DS-OBS-01-FIX note in freshnessSlaMonitorJob.ts lines 538-548), so a genuine stale-page breach never mints a fix and never re-runs a fetcher — the user's 'many frontend pages show non-updated data' persists because the signal has no remediation consumer.
entries.scope_in: THREE genuinely-new pieces ON TOP of L4: (1) REMEDIATION-TRIAGE decision-layer — for each breaching surface, read its coverage-map .writer + .cadence, probe the writer's live runtime (generalize queryBctcPipelineRuntimeState's queueDepth+serviceActive idle-vs-crash reader across ALL coverage-map surfaces, not just bctc), and CLASSIFY broken-code (writer service down / erroring / never-scheduled) vs not-refreshed (writer healthy+idle, just didn't run) → route to dev FIX vs refresh-agent re-invoke. (2) ANTI-SPAM gating — REUSE apps/alert-engine dedup-key-builder + cooldown-gate primitives (Go) plus the existing sla_breach_audit 60-min cooldown table; key dedup by (surface, breach-class); SUPPRESS repeat signals while a remediation task/signal is already OPEN for that surface; keep the isVnMarketHours() market-hours gate. (3) ORCHESTRATION integration — REDIRECT the breach signal OFF the dead-end alert-commander addressee ONTO the po/dev-team signal_queue drain (the existing anomaly→BACKLOG bridge: emit-audit-signal.sh + po-s* drain-mint jq library) so remediation is AUTO-picked-up, not a dead alert. Detection-completeness input: coverageMapFreshnessChecker.ts currently maps only 5 of 50 surfaces to DB queries (ENDPOINT_DB_QUERY) — the other 45 are silently skipped, so 'many pages' cannot even be detected yet; widening endpoint→DB coverage is an input the architect must scope for the triage layer to be effective.
entries.scope_out: NOT re-building L4 detection (FIX-L4-FRESHNESS-SLA-MONITOR-SELF-POLICING owns verify-live + wire-if-missing of the detector/emitter — stays a separate READY task, do NOT widen it). NOT the frontend badge / auto-revalidate display layer (L3 = FIX-L3-FRONTEND-AUTOREFRESH-FRESHNESS-BADGE + FE-PG-*-FRESH-FIX — that shows staleness to the USER; this ACTS on it). NOT the input-validation sprint (that gates bad writes at input-time; this catches data going stale over time). NOT rebuilding alert-engine dedup/cooldown (REUSE the Go primitives). NOT overlapping system-auditor's two-layer fetch-vs-analysis freshness audit (coordinate, don't duplicate).
entries.success_metric: A forced real breach on a watched surface (a) is CLASSIFIED broken-code-vs-not-refreshed by a live runtime probe (RAW: scheduler log shows the classification), (b) produces EITHER a minted dev FIX task in task_board.backlog (broken-code) OR a re-invoke call to the named refresh agent (not-refreshed) — verified live, not self-report, (c) does NOT re-emit while that remediation is still OPEN (dedup/cooldown proven by a second tick producing no duplicate), (d) the breach signal lands in the po/dev-team signal_queue drain, NOT the suppressed alert-commander path. DoD gate is RAW live evidence per each, not unit-test-only.

L4 stays the 'does the detector fire + emit' gate (READY, dev-mcp-server, about to execute); this sprint owns 'what happens when it fires'. Widening L4 would bloat a verify-live FIX into a multi-week build and risk the health-recheck stale-duplicate footgun. entries.vision: Replace the ENGINEERING ESTIMATE of silent-tick cost with a MEASURED number. The cron preflight scripts shipped by TOKEN-ECONOMY-TICK-PREFLIGHT (2026-07-02) each emit one compact JSON verdict on stdout and then exit — on ~80% of ticks that verdict is SILENT/SKIP and no LLM work follows. Nothing anywhere records that those invocations happened, so the only available answer to 'what does the silent-tick layer cost' is an estimate derived from the script's I/O shape (the router quoted ~250-500 tok/silent cowork tick on 2026-08-12; the user asked for that to become a measurement). This sprint adds per-invocation, append-only, LOCAL-FILE-ONLY usage telemetry at each script's verdict choke point: what verdict, when, how many BYTES of verdict JSON the LLM actually receives, how long it took, what exit code. It records only what is measurable and deliberately does NOT compute a token number inside the script.
entries.scope_in: FOUR rows, sequenced, WU-0 gates the rest. (WU-0) NEW shared lib scripts/agents-flow/lib/tick-telemetry.sh — one log_tick_usage() helper + log destination + size-cap/tail-truncate rotation + its own regression suite; must land and be green before any wiring. (WU-1) wire into scripts/agents-flow/cowork-tick-preflight.sh at its single _emit_verdict() choke point (lines 76-82) — the user's specifically named target, ships first after WU-0. (WU-2) wire into scripts/agents-flow/dev-team-tick-preflight.sh at its single _emit_verdict() choke point (line 200-203) — structurally identical to WU-1, ~1 line after WU-0 exists. (WU-3) wire into scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh — GATED on WU-0/1/2 all green; NOT the same change, see product_decision.

(c) NO est_tokens / estimated-cost field computed inside any script — record measurable bytes, let a later analysis step convert. (d) NOT in scope, deliberately deferred and recorded here so it is not lost: the OTHER THREE members of the same preflight family that share this exact verdict-JSON-on-stdout shape and the same silent-tick economics — scripts/agents-flow/code-janitor-tick-preflight.sh (SKIP-SPAWN|SPAWN), scripts/agents-flow/db-integrity-probe.sh, scripts/agents-flow/orch-sentinel-lite-probe.sh. entries.product_decision:
PO triage 2026-08-12T13:03Z, from a user 'yes' to a router proposal. The router asked 1 WU (cowork only) vs 3 (all preflight scripts). PO read all four scripts at source and both framings are wrong; the answer is 4 rows.

WHY NOT 1: measuring cowork alone answers 'what does a silent cowork tick cost', not 'what does the silent-tick LAYER cost', which is the actual question behind the user's yes. dev-team fires more often than cowork (7/37 min vs 15 min). And once WU-0 exists, WU-2 is approximately one line — refusing it would be false economy.

WHY NOT 3-AS-EQUALS: it is NOT 'the same change 3x'. cowork-tick-preflight.sh and dev-team-tick-preflight.sh each have a SINGLE _emit_verdict() function every verdict routes through — a genuinely mechanical hook. auditor-tier1-probe.sh has NO choke point: it builds verdict JSON inline at >=6 distinct sites (lines 757, 767, 772, 858, 894, 921) AND it is dual-mode — run_tiered_probe() (tier 2/3) internally calls run_probe() and then re-emits its own wrapper verdict with a DIFFERENT field set (checks_verdict ALL_GREEN|FAILURE inner vs verdict SKIP-SPAWN|SPAWN outer). A naive per-call-site hook therefore DOUBLE-LOGS every tier-2/3 tick with two incompatible shapes and silently corrupts the very dataset this sprint exists to produce. Correct instrumentation there requires first extracting a choke point from a 925-line script guarded by a 1323-line suite. That is a different risk class and gets its own gated row, droppable without invalidating the sprint.

WHY WU-0 FIRST: three copies of the same log helper is exactly the debt CLAUDE.md forbids. Precedent for the extraction already exists in this tree — scripts/agents-flow/lib/hook-guard.sh and scripts/agents-flow/lib/notebook-section-direction.sh.

ENGINE: jq, NOT python3. The intake brief suggested reusing a python3 json.dumps() log_json() pattern from another project. Rejected: all four scripts already hard-depend on jq and use `jq -nc --arg` as their quote-safe JSON emitter throughout. Adding a python3 dependency to four cron-critical paths is a new failure mode for zero benefit.

SESSION ID: NOT logged, even hashed, in v1. cowork-tick-preflight.sh's own header (lines 56-57) states CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is 'never echoed/logged by this script beyond its use as a bound task_claim arg'. Writing it to a telemetry file breaks that stated contract. This sprint is about cost, not cross-session correlation.

RATIO: PO checked and the convention ALREADY EXISTS — 4 chars/token, used in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-05-21-token-toolcall-economy.md §W-1 ('At 4 chars/token') and applied in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-12-token-economy-lazyload-audit.md (3,162 chars ~= 790 tokens; 23,994 chars ~= 6k tokens). Do NOT invent a new one, and do NOT bake it into a script.

HONESTY CAVEAT, ACCEPTANCE-BEARING: verdict_bytes is a LOWER BOUND on true per-tick cost, not the cost. The real cost of a silent tick is the cron prompt text the LLM reads + whatever flow-doc lines it loads + the tool_result. The script can only measure the last of those three. Every artifact this sprint produces (script header, lib doc, dev-standards pointer, any later rollup) MUST state that explicitly, so the resulting number is never mis-sold as 'a silent tick costs N tokens'. Shipping a precise-looking number with an unstated denominator would be worse than the estimate it replaces.

VERDICT: NEITHER (a) NOR (b). Traced at source, not inferred:
  - emitPressureStateTool.ts:387 stores `args.calendar_status ?? "unknown"`. calendar_status is CALLER-SUPPLIED. The server never computes it and can never itself emit "closed" — its only self-generated value is "unknown".
  - telemetry.md Step 6.0 L15 passes `"calendar_status": "<CALENDAR_STATUS from Step 4.3>"`.
  - pressure-read.md L65: `CALENDAR_STATUS = PRESSURE_STATE.calendar_status` — read FROM pressure-state.json.
  The dispatcher reads the field out of the very file it then writes back. Closed self-recycling loop, no authoritative producer anywhere in the chain. Whatever literal enters the file once persists forever. This is precisely the "circular" mechanism this row was minted for — so the fix lands in the CALLER + the TOOL BOUNDARY, not in cadence-policy.json.

ENABLER (why an out-of-domain literal survives): the tool's Zod schema is bare `z.string().optional()` (emitPressureStateTool.ts:459) — no enum gate — even though its own describe() text names the 5-value domain 'open'|'weekend'|'holiday'|'half_day'|'unknown'. A coordinator finding this tick proposed attaching a mislabelled-report case here on the theory that this row's "filename heuristic / pattern-guessing" IS the mechanism. PO traced it and IT IS NOT. Do not absorb that case into this row.

THE FILENAME IS NOT GUESSED FROM NOTHING — IT IS RENDERED FROM THE STORED PERIOD KEY. apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:224 calls normaliseFilename(sourceUrl, actionCode, periodYear, periodQuarter), and apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/resolvePdfText.ts:45-61 returns canonical ACTIONCODE_YEAR_QUARTER.pdf unless the source URL's own basename both ends in .pdf and already contains the action code. So the canonical filename is a faithful projection of financial_reports.period_year/period_quarter — the two cannot disagree, and today the filename is the ONLY place a wrong period identity is visible to a human reading a directory listing.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S DELIVERABLE. "Derive the real filename from source metadata instead of pattern-guessing" is a reasonable goal on its own terms, but it decouples the filename from the stored period. If the stored period is wrong, the file would then be named correctly while the DB row remains mislabelled — the corruption becomes invisible instead of fixed. The live case that prompted this: report_id 5b0dad71-3b05-4455-9823-c2072442777d is stored as DPM_2025_Q4.pdf while its refined content is unambiguously Q1-2026 across five independent pages. The filename is what exposed it.

That row adds the period-vs-content validation the ingest boundary has never had (bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:194-201 validates only that the year is 2000..2099 and the quarter is one of Q1..Q4 — shape, never correspondence). Once a wrong period identity cannot be stored, decoupling the filename from it is safe and this row becomes a clean improvement. Until then, this row's change would delete the tripwire.

backlog.note: EVIDENCE ADDENDUM 2026-08-01 (po/triage-auditor-findings-20260801) — A CLAIM AGAINST THIS ROW WAS TESTED AND FALSIFIED; recorded here so it is not re-raised. THE CLAIM (from a 3-tier auditor brief): "a 24-hour window predicate on agent_signals returns far FEWER rows than the table holds, because the bound datetime(now,-24 hours) is space-separated while alert-engine writes ISO-8601-with-T, so the string comparison silently drops most rows", citing 12 of 116 / 15 of 119 / 20 of 124 from three tiers, and asserting this corrupts C-07 own published output. BOTH HALVES ARE WRONG. (a) DIRECTION IS INVERTED. Measured live 2026-08-01T06:14Z: rows matched by the space bound but NOT by a T bound = 2; rows matched by a T bound but NOT by the space bound = 0. The space-separated bound drops ZERO rows. This is the same direction this row title already states ("T (0x54) > (0x20) at position 11 makes every T row sort AFTER every space row within the same date") -- the defect is FALSE INCLUSION, never exclusion, exactly as the original +61%/60-minute measurement found. (b) THE CITED NUMBERS ARE A DENOMINATOR ERROR, NOT A DEFECT. The denominators 116/119/124 are the WHOLE agent_signals table, which is only partially pruned and spans back to 2026-05-18 (live 2026-08-01: 131 rows total; by month 2026-05:28, 2026-06:52, 2026-07:39, 2026-08:12). A 24h window returning ~20% of a 2.5-month table is correct arithmetic. Format-agnostic ground truth via julianday(replace(replace(created_at,T, ),Z,)) >= julianday(now,-24 hours) = 27; the live space-separated predicate also returns 27 -- i.e. on this data the 24h predicate is currently EXACTLY RIGHT, 0 rows in error. (c) WHY, AND WHY IT IS STILL LATENT: this row already says "cross-day windows still work by accident". Confirmed -- all 17 current T-format rows are >= 2026-07-31T14:04:45.672Z, well inside the window, and none fall in the 00:00-to-bound-time band of the boundary date where a T row would be falsely included. The latent hazard is unchanged and the fix is still warranted: mixed formats (live 2026-08-01: 114 space, 17 T; the 106/234=45% figure in this title was 2026-07-31 and has since churned) make ANY string bound unsound on the boundary date in whichever direction the mismatch falls. THIS ADDENDUM DOES NOT LOWER PRIORITY -- it removes a false corroboration so the fix is justified by the real (60-minute, +61% false-inclusion) evidence rather than an arithmetic artifact. ALSO NOTED, SEPARATE DEFECT NOT FIXED HERE: 130 of 131 agent_signals rows have expires_at already in the past yet remain in the table, and the oldest is 2026-05-18 -- cleanExpired() is not pruning to its stated TTL. Any brief describing agent_signals as "a rolling ~2h TTL window" is wrong; count(*) on it is neither window fullness nor a producer rate.

Router proposed: inside the isVnSbvBusinessDay(now) arm, return defaultThresholdMinutes only within the publish window, else minutesSinceLastSbvWindowEnd(now) + OFF_HOURS_GRACE_MINUTES, calling it a ~3-line change because both helpers already exist. backlog.router_accepts_po_correction_20260721T20: ROUTER'S OWN ANALYSIS ON THIS TOPIC WAS WRONG AND PO CORRECTED IT BY MEASUREMENT — the correction stands, router's earlier key does not. backlog.router_shipped_arm_never_worked_20260721: THE SEVERE FINDING NEITHER ROUTER NOR PO HAD BEFORE THIS PASS: THE ALREADY-SHIPPED WEEKEND ARM HAS NEVER WORKED AT REAL CADENCE. Commit d71e3f2e2 closed FIX-SLA-EXEMPT-NEWS-SBVFX with a dedicated passing regression file, and router cited that passing file at 19:35Z as PROOF the capability existed and PO's premise was false. The capability exists; it does not FUNCTION. Per PO's measurement its S-1 fixture asserts '289 min NOT breached' against a 1470 threshold — but 289 was never derived from the source's real cadence, which is ~1854. So the fixture is satisfiable by a broken implementation, and the row closed green while the false positives it existed to stop kept firing. LESSON FOR THE ROW AND FOR ROUTER: a passing regression file is evidence a code path EXISTS, never evidence it WORKS. Router treated the former as the latter. backlog.po_correction_20260730:
PREMISE REFUTED — do NOT build the capability described in the original title; it already shipped.

READ AT SOURCE: process_telegram_report (interface/mcp/tools/briefings/telegramReportTools.ts:160-242) takes resolution: z.enum(["none","fixed","wontfix","duplicate","monitoring"]). "monitoring" IS the dispositioned-but-deferred ack this row asks for; "duplicate" IS the tracked-elsewhere ack. Step 4 calls markProcessed(db,id) UNCONDITIONALLY, setting status=processed. read_telegram_reports filters WHERE status='new' (telegramReportStore.ts:108); listUnresolvedReports filters "resolution NOT IN ('fixed','wontfix','duplicate') AND status != 'processed'" (:391-401). So ANY process_telegram_report call drops the row out of BOTH polls.

PROVEN END-TO-END, not inferred: PO acked report 4039, re-read list_unresolved_reports -> 179 dropped to 178 with 4039 absent; then acked the remaining 178 and both planes returned empty. 179 -> 0 in a single pass. The queue was never unclearable — it was uncleared.

RETARGETED SCOPE (cheap, and this is the actual root cause):
(1) Fix docs/agents/tools/list/process_telegram_report.md — it documents the parameter as `delete_message` (actual: `delete_telegram_message`) and does not mention `resolution` AT ALL. That doc drift is precisely why 179 reports sat at resolution=none: every agent reading the tool doc literally could not see the disposition values.
(2) Wire an explicit ack step into whichever flow reads this queue (dev-team Step 4.1 / the PO report-queue pass) carrying the resolution decision table: fixed = the fix shipped; duplicate = root cause already has a board row; monitoring = real and tracked but not yet fixed; wontfix = detector/actuator mismatch that will never be actioned.

backlog.title: verify-deploy-sha.sh false-positives on doc/orch-state-only commits landing after a build (3rd confirmed occurrence)
backlog.desc: scripts/verify-deploy-sha.sh compares deployed image git_sha label against current HEAD — fails whenever HEAD advances via a doc/notebook/orch-state-only commit made after the build, even though deployed source is byte-identical to HEAD at build time. backlog.fix_spec: Teach the script to PASS when: (deployed SHA is an ancestor of HEAD) AND (git diff <deployed_sha>..HEAD -- apps/<service>/ is empty) — i.e. treat doc-only HEAD advancement post-build as non-drift. backlog.title: An agent-side context-budget limit is written into permanent report state as a data failure — failed_ct is indistinguishable between 'source data is bad' and 'worker could not hold a 1.2MB image'
backlog.mechanism: For the final 4 windows of POW_2026_Q1 the refine agent reported the page-28 image fetch returned ~1.2MB of base64 that 'exceeded context token budget'. That is a limit of the SUBAGENT's context window — not a property of the document and not of the pipeline. Per its error-boundary contract the agent pushed FAILED for those windows and called finalize_bctc_refine, producing refine_status=FAILED with failed_ct=28.
backlog.why_it_matters: The failure reason is now indistinguishable, in stored state, from a genuine data defect. A future remediation pass reading failed_ct=28 cannot tell that some windows failed because a transcription worker could not hold a 1.2MB image rather than because the page is unreadable. Combined with the head-of-line row this is also what makes the head row PERMANENTLY dead: the finalization is sticky.
backlog.fix_direction: Introduce a distinct terminal-ish status (e.g. DEFERRED / RESOURCE_EXCEEDED) that does NOT finalize the report and leaves the window re-attemptable by a worker with a larger budget or via an image-downscale path. Do not class it with text_fetch_failed.
backlog.scoping_caution: The agent FOLLOWED its documented graceful-degradation contract — this is NOT filed as agent misbehaviour. The defect is that the contract has no distinct terminal status for 'worker could not process within its own resource envelope' versus 'source data is bad'. Prior art (the BCTC reingest guard: 56/56 FAILED/empty-markdown, data-loss guard refused to wipe bctc_table_rows) shows the downstream cost of that ambiguity is already being paid elsewhere.
backlog.advisory_do_not_chase: The refine agent recommended 'investigate upstream text extraction (get_bctc_page_text) for POW reports'. That is WRONG-ROOTED as a current root cause and must not become a task: the store reports text_status=COMPLETE, cowork-team called get_bctc_page_text(report_id=78b06684..., page_number=1) — one of the 24 pages said to have failed — and got full Vietnamese OCR text with source='sqlite_ocr', and the agent's own report contradicts itself ('Page 28 text retrieved successfully'). LIMIT ON THIS REFUTATION: it does NOT prove text was retrievable when the 24 units failed on 2026-07-19; text may have been backfilled since. It establishes only that pointing an implementer at get_bctc_page_text TODAY sends them at a component that demonstrably works.
backlog.ordering: Sequenced AFTER the head-of-line fix — that one unblocks the live queue and is the urgent half; this one prevents the next sticky-dead head row. Do not merge them: one is a query predicate, the other a status taxonomy, and they must be verifiable independently.
backlog.acceptance: (1) a worker-resource failure records a status distinct from data failure; (2) that status does NOT finalize the report; (3) the affected windows remain re-attemptable; (4) POW_2026_Q1's existing failed_ct=28 is NOT retroactively reinterpreted — historical rows stay as-is unless a separate explicit decision says otherwise.

backlog.title: 'Write acceptance criteria before editing files' is structurally unverifiable for every agent whose commit zone excludes orch-state.json — move acceptance authorship to the dispatcher
backlog.po_evidence: Surfaced by the FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD-SKILLS supervised sign-off 2026-07-21. agent-father claimed it wrote acceptance onto the row BEFORE editing any file, and the row carries self-reported acceptance_written_at=2026-07-21T19:08:10Z. But the acceptance text's FIRST appearance in git is 304f24edd at 19:14:24Z, AFTER the skills commit 3e4f50d3a at 19:12:13Z — because agent-father's commit zone excludes docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, so a peer cold-evict swept the board and collapsed the acceptance-write and the lane-move into one indistinguishable blob. The claim is UNVERIFIABLE, not disproven. acceptance_written_by/acceptance_written_at are self-reported fields authored by the same agent whose ordering they attest — they are narration, not evidence.
backlog.po_ruling: The dispatcher's framing is correct and generalises: an agent whose commit zone excludes the board can NEVER produce evidence for an ordering claim about the board. Requiring such a claim therefore mandates an unfalsifiable self-report, which is exactly the failure class feedback_agent_selfreport_metalayer_confabulation.md warns about. The requirement is unenforceable across the whole maintenance lane, and the unsatisfiable dispatch instruction was the dispatcher's error, not agent-father's — no fault attaches to the agent. PREFERRED RESOLUTION: acceptance is authored by the DISPATCHER (or PO) at dispatch time, before spawn. The dispatcher's commit zone already includes the board, so ordering becomes provable by construction across two disjoint zones: dispatcher commits acceptance, implementer commits code, and git ordering across the two zones is independently checkable. Rejected alternatives: (a) letting maintenance agents commit the board row themselves — breaks zone separation and re-introduces the peer-sweep class this very sprint just fixed; (b) silently dropping the requirement — loses the real benefit that acceptance predates implementation.

backlog.title: Session-scoped CronCreate loops are invisible and unpersisted across 5 CLI sessions — build the launchd-hosted liveness watchdog that turns 'a session died and its whole loop vanished' from silent into a BUG-channel alert
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 4 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 (cron-registry.json) landing first; this row is that registry's first consumer. See po_design_ruling below: the design call was made, this row implements one third of it.
backlog.problem: CronList in the router session returns 'No scheduled jobs.' Crons live inside 5 separate CLI sessions (dev-team, cowork, system-audit, claude-heler, workflows-fix). No session can see or repair another's crons. When a session dies its whole loop vanishes with zero trace. CronCreate additionally only fires while the REPL is idle, so a session stuck mid-query fires nothing. PO verified there is NO on-disk cron persistence under ~/.claude (no crons dir; ~/.claude/jobs/ holds two stale June background-job state dirs, unrelated).
backlog.po_design_ruling: OPTION (a) BROADER LAUNCHD COVERAGE — SCOPED, plus (c) MONITORING. Option (b), a persistence/registry layer for CronCreate, is REJECTED as a new scheduler. Reasoning: (1) building persistence for CronCreate means re-implementing a scheduler we do not own, inside a surface (the CLI REPL) whose contract can change under us; we already own two durable planes (launchd, and the containerized mcp-server node-cron scheduler with 85 jobs) and a third home-grown one is exactly the 'duplicating cron hosts' that UC-CDC-P5 already names as the thing to avoid. (2) launchd is the ONLY plane that survives session death and it demonstrably works (firer: 815 runs). (3) But WHOLESALE migration to launchd is equally wrong — `claude -p` per tick is expensive and, per FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION, structurally truncates fan-out work. So launchd hosts loop RE-ARM and LIVENESS, not every loop. (4) The REPL-idle constraint is unfixable from our side; that is a second independent argument for making session-plane failures VISIBLE rather than trying to make the session plane reliable. (5) Monitoring alone (option c as a terminal answer) is also rejected: without a registry there is nothing to monitor against.
backlog.three_part_sequence: PART 1 (registry of record) — FOLDED INTO EXISTING UC-SDF-P6, not re-minted: the 5 session-scoped loops must be DECLARED in a repo file so absence becomes detectable. Not a new scheduler; an inventory. PART 2 (this row) — one launchd-hosted watchdog that reads that registry and alerts when a declared loop has produced no evidence-of-life within its cadence. PART 3 (re-arm automation) — EXISTING UC-CDC-P5, sequenced LAST, only after 1+2: re-arming blind is how you get double-hosted crons.
backlog.hard_constraint_evidence_of_life: Evidence-of-life MUST be the loop's own external artifact — its commits, its notebook mtime, its telemetry row — NEVER a self-report or a heartbeat the loop writes about itself. A loop that can assert its own liveness is a loop whose watchdog is self-satisfying (see FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-FRESHNESS-CHECK-RELOCATE-TO-SENTINEL in ready[], same defect class, already ruled).
backlog.acceptance: Kill any one of the 5 sessions and, within one cadence period, a BUG-channel message names the dead loop. Today that event is completely silent.

backlog.title: Three time bases coexist in one scheduling system: server jobs mix timezone UTC and Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, CronCreate fires at MACHINE-LOCAL France time (CEST/CET, DST-sensitive), and the market it serves is fixed UTC+7 — no single place states what any job's real wall-clock is
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 7 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 cron-registry.json. A registry that records each job's declared time base is most of this answer; doing it before the registry means writing the same table twice.
backlog.problem: (1) mcp-server scheduler jobs individually declare timezone:'UTC' or timezone:'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'. (2) CronCreate jobs fire at machine-local France time (CEST=UTC+2 summer / CET=UTC+1 winter) and therefore SHIFT BY AN HOUR twice a year against the market. (3) Vietnam is fixed UTC+7 with no DST. A job authored as '15:00' has three different meanings depending on which plane it lands on, and nothing declares which.
backlog.dst_is_the_sharp_edge: The France planes silently re-time relative to the VN trading session at each DST transition. docs/standards/cron-jobs.md:292 already documents this reasoning for the guaranteed-slot firer (StartInterval chosen over StartCalendarInterval precisely because the latter is DST-sensitive) — the insight exists but is applied in exactly one place. Next transitions to check against: late Oct 2026 (CEST->CET) shifts every session-plane cron one hour LATER relative to UTC/VN.
backlog.folded_item_5b_minute_collision: FOLDED (item 5b, LOW): restartCadenceAlert (server plane) and cron-db-data-integrity (terminal/session plane) both sit on `15,45 * * * *`. PO assessment: these run in different processes and share no resource except SQLite, so this is a same-minute COINCIDENCE, not a contention bug — it is folded here rather than minted separately because a cron-registry with declared time bases is what makes cross-plane minute maps computable at all, instead of discoverable only by hand-audit.

backlog.title: Add StartLimitIntervalSec=0 to systemd units to prevent crash-loop lockout after transient failures
backlog.description: vn-price-fetch, vn-foreign-flow, vn-sbv-fetch crashed ~2026-07-21 03:05-09 UTC and entered systemd failed state due to missing StartLimitIntervalSec=0 hardening. Systemd default StartLimitIntervalSec=10s/StartLimitBurst=5 causes permanent failed state for any Restart=always unit crashing >=5 times in 10s window. Hardening has been proven safe by commit 42e8448ce (applied to vn-news-fetch/vn-reuters-fetch/vn-tradingeconomics-fetch 2026-05-02) — vn-news-fetch rode through the same incident window unaffected, demonstrating the control. This incident was non-recoverable without manual intervention due to inbound SSH/HTTP being blocked to VPS (user-gated restart already escalated via Telegram).
backlog.scope: Add StartLimitIntervalSec=0 to [Unit] section of vps-scripts/vn-price-fetch.service, vps-scripts/vn-foreign-flow.service, vps-scripts/vn-sbv-fetch.service, vps-scripts/vn-bctc-fetch.service; audit vps-scripts/vn-agm-plan.service and vps-scripts/vn-reuters-fetch.service deployment status (both exist in repo but are never scp'd/enabled by scripts/deploy-vinahost.sh — same dead-code class as OHLCV-backfill gap from c023). Identify and fix byte-identical duplicate deploy scripts (scripts/deploy-vinahost.sh and apps/mcp-server/deploy-vinahost.sh) — update both or dedupe and select one for deployment.
backlog.acceptance: Repo hardening complete: all 4 units have StartLimitIntervalSec=0; redundant deploy script verified or deduped; agm-plan and reuters-fetch units disposition determined (deployed-to-vps OR removed-as-dead-code); redeploy via scripts/deploy-vinahost.sh; live systemctl restart on VPS succeeds (user-gated after reachability restored). Post-deploy: all 3 services recover from failed state and resume pushing data; vn-bctc-fetch state verified separately. BACKFILL (added 2026-07-22T22:45Z from po triage of auditor signal sys-20260722T223302-4f8b): recovery must also REPAIR the outage-window gap, which does not self-heal because prices/foreign-flow pushes are live-only. Live-measured at 43h: daily_ohlcv 2026-07-21=416 tickers and 2026-07-22=51 tickers against an 887-984/day baseline (07-13..07-20), and daily_foreign_flow has NO 2026-07-22 row at all (baseline 102/day). Post-restart acceptance: daily_ohlcv coverage for 2026-07-21 and 2026-07-22 restored to >=880 tickers/day and daily_foreign_flow has a populated 2026-07-22 row; if the existing ohlcv_backfill_queue path cannot cover foreign-flow, state that explicitly and raise the follow-on rather than closing with the gap open.
backlog.notes: Root cause from git: commit 42e8448ce (2026-05-02) added StartLimitIntervalSec=0 to vn-news-fetch/vn-reuters-fetch/vn-tradingeconomics-fetch only. Commit message explicitly lists vn-price-fetch/vn-foreign-flow/vn-sbv-fetch/vn-bctc-fetch as "had no burst limit and are unchanged" — this premise is inverted. No explicit override means systemd applies its compiled-in default (StartLimitIntervalSec=10s/StartLimitBurst=5), not "no limit". Incident recon: docs/vps-sources/vps-push-plane-stale-2026-07-22/recon.md

backlog.title: cowork-team parallel fan-out has no producer/consumer ordering — alert-commander read the signal bus before its co-dispatched producers wrote to it, and went silent on a session with real >5% drops
backlog.mechanism: BGFAN-1 mandates run_in_background=true for every dispatcher spawn and spawn-fanout.md issues all matched slots in ONE parallel block, with no dependency ordering. When a tick matches both a PRODUCER (market-watcher -> price_anomaly; news-scout -> urgent_news/chain_catalyst) and a CONSUMER (alert-commander -> gates on those exact signal types), the consumer can complete its bus read before the producers have posted.
backlog.evidence_16_00Z_tick: Dispatched together: news-scout-offhours, market-watcher-offhours, market-watcher-eod, alert-commander-critical. alert-commander ran ~16:10-16:15Z and reported zero verified_chain/chain_catalyst/price_anomaly on the bus, verified by explicit signal_type-filtered calls — its evidence was CLEAN, the bus genuinely WAS empty at read time. market-watcher-offhours then posted price_anomaly 8680 (GAS -6.98%, 2.89 sigma, 4.02x volume) and 8681 (D2D -3.30%, 52-week low) at ~16:17Z, AFTER alert-commander had exited silent.
backlog.why_this_matters_beyond_tidiness: alert-commander's position-danger gate failed at condition 1/3 for want of price signals its SIBLING produced two minutes later, on a session with real >5% drops (GAS -6.98%, BSR -6.49%, GEX -5.16%). The silent exit was CORRECT given what it could see. The dispatch order is what made it blind. This is a market-facing miss, not an internal hygiene issue.
backlog.options_for_architect: (a) order the fan-out into producer-wave then consumer-wave within a tick; (b) have consumers re-read the bus after a bounded wait when co-dispatched producers are known to be in flight; (c) accept and document that consumers lag producers by one tick. PO has NOT pre-selected one — this is a genuine design decision with a latency/complexity tradeoff and it belongs to architect. Note cowork-team correctly refused to self-modify its own dispatch contract.
backlog.second_order_in_scope: R3 (match-slots.md Step 4b: multi-slot collision WARNs but never blocks) spawned market-watcher TWICE the same tick — the EOD slot fired late (~16:08-16:13Z) pushing the 16:09 dispatch into offhours, so TWO market-watcher cycles processed the SAME 08:32 closing prices four minutes apart. R3 is working as written; the written rule is what needs review. Fold into this design pass — same dispatcher, same tick-ordering root.
backlog.important_scoping_do_not_absorb: This does NOT establish that get_alerts(type=price) is broken. alert-commander separately reported get_alerts(type=price) empty; prior art FIX-ALERT-SCAN-REJECT-STUB-BAR-P0 and FIX-ALERT-OPEN-ZERO-PRICE-RACE sit in that neighbourhood and were deliberately NOT re-filed. At least part of this cycle's blindness is dispatcher ordering, not detector failure. BOTH causes may be live — do not let this row absorb the detector question or close it by proxy.
backlog.acceptance: Architecture brief selecting (a), (b) or (c) with the tradeoff stated, plus the decomposition into implementable rows. If (c) is chosen, the documentation must land somewhere a consumer agent actually reads, not only in the brief.
backlog.architect_design_summary: Chose bounded async schedule_task recheck (variant of PO option b, not synchronous wait) over two-phase wave (a, breaks BGFAN-1 fire-and-forget + risks fire-election TTL lapse) or accept-and-document alone (c, row is market-facing). Mechanism: tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7 captures won_slots at dispatch time (last_fired is stamped at spawn not completion, so a consumer re-deriving co-dispatch after the fact would be silently defeated) -> surfaced through the already-shared cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md tick-snapshot read every cowork agent uses (zero spawn-fanout.md prompt-template edit) -> alert-commander schedules ONE schedule_task recheck (~20min, cowork-schedule.json producer_settle_wait_seconds field) only when a co-dispatched gatherer producer is known AND its own read was empty AND this is not already a recheck (bounded, real discriminator, zero cost on quiet ticks). Prerequisite gap found: alert_commander SKILL_MANIFEST does not grant schedule_task today (apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/bootstrap/agentBootstrap.ts:115-139). R3 folded in as root-cause fix: market-watcher/flow/main.md derives sub-flow from wall-clock time and discards the slot= the dispatcher already sends -- a late EOD-slot fire silently loses eod.md own deliverable, not just duplicate compute; match-slots.md Step 4b kept WARN-only (DDD: dispatcher cannot know same-trading-day-close domain fact). digest-daily flowpath/trigger_prompt signal confirmed orthogonal. 8-row PM decomposition T1-T8 in brief section 9.
backlog.po_ruling_deviation_accepted_20260721T18: DEVIATION FROM (a)/(b)/(c) — ACCEPTED. Architect was right to not pick one of my three literals, and the row's own options_for_architect text explicitly said PO had NOT pre-selected one. I verified BOTH brownfield facts the deviation rests on at source rather than accepting them: (F4) docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/last-fired.md:10 states 'AC-P1-7-1: last_fired written after successful spawn' — confirmed, last_fired is stamped at SPAWN, not completion, so any consumer re-deriving co-dispatch from it after the fact would read a slot as fired before its output exists and be silently defeated. That single fact kills the cheap version of (b) and justifies the tick-snapshot won_slots capture instead. (F7) docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/main.md:10-14 routes on wall-clock UTC windows only, and Step 2 ('Read current UTC time. Match the window above') never consumes the slot= the dispatcher already sends — confirmed, the parameter is discarded. Both facts hold. The chosen bounded-async schedule_task recheck is a better option than any of my three: it keeps BGFAN-1's parallel fire-and-forget contract untouched (the real cost of (a), compounded by the fire-election 600s TTL lapse risk during a multi-minute in-session wait), pays zero cost on quiet ticks (the real cost of (b)-as-worded), and does not leave a market-facing miss undefended (the disqualifier for (c)). Brief section 3 states the tradeoffs plainly as the row's acceptance required — including the two I most wanted named: detection latency goes to a bounded ~20min and NOT to zero, and a tick now has two possible verdicts so telemetry readers must check the recheck cycle too. po_clause_d_20260808.headline: (d) effective_next_agent()/effective_owner() DETAIL-FIRST precedence lets a COLD mint-time value silently outrank a lifecycle-flipped HOT board row.
po_clause_d_20260808.mechanism: docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json is a COLD mint-time store. Its ONLY writer (scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh) runs on new-backlog-item write and documents 'existing cold wins' merge semantics — it NEVER re-syncs a cold entry after the hot row is later flipped by the implementing agent. So for EVERY row that moves past BACKLOG, cold .next_agent/.status are systematically stale, and detail-first makes that stale value authoritative over the live hot SSOT.
po_clause_d_20260808.harm_two_sided: Measured live 2026-08-08 (jq via scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq against the live board): 6 review[] rows carried hot next_agent=='qa' but resolved to a stale cold agent. (i) FALSE-NEGATIVE, the bigger harm: scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq selects effective_next_agent=='qa', so all 6 were PERMANENTLY invisible to PRIMARY QA-Drain and could never be signed off — accreting in review[] forever, actively defeating the throughput goal of docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-01-review-lane-drain-throughput-and-secondary-sweep.md. (ii) FALSE-POSITIVE: the same 6 sat in the SECONDARY-Drain pool (selects != 'qa'), which never lane-moves a claimed row, so it re-dispatches the WRONG agent every tick the row is oldest. Materialised twice: FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-REGEX-HEADING-MISMATCH -> 'developer' (2026-08-05T08:15:09Z) and FIX-COWORK-SPAWN-IDENTITY-PREAMBLE-OFFFLOW -> 'agent-father' (2026-08-08T17:26:17Z; agent-father returned 'already implemented, 9/9 tests, correctly parked for QA' — a full wasted dispatch).

Predicate-driven, idempotent, gate-verified. That is a DATA patch for one lane — this clause is the actual fix.
po_clause_d_20260808.do_not_blanket_flip: A blanket board-first flip is a SAFETY REGRESSION and must NOT be shipped. 10 live backlog[] rows also carry a board-vs-cold next_agent conflict (board architect/agent-father/dev-mcp-server/pm/developer vs cold ba/architect) — e.g. FIX-AUDITOR-C06-OFFMARKET-RECALIBRATE, FIX-ORPHAN-ADOPTION-BOARD-STATE-GUARD. Those are NOT lifecycle flips (still status BACKLOG), and there cold-first is the CONSERVATIVE direction: is_non_dev_next_agent_unrouted() currently gates them OUT of BOUNDED-1 unattended pickup. Board-first would make them auto-dispatchable, reopening exactly the class the 2026-07-09..07-16 gate fixes closed. The rule must be LIFECYCLE/STALENESS-aware, not a precedence swap — e.g. hot board wins when the row has moved past BACKLOG/TODO AND its own .next_agent is present-non-empty; cold fills gaps only.
acceptance_criteria: A review[]/qa[]/done[] row whose HOT .next_agent is present-non-empty resolves to that value regardless of any cold .next_agent.

backlog.title: Add a real updated_at audit column to prediction_claims, maintained on every write, surfaced per-row on the Du bao AI page so a reader can tell at a glance whether a prediction was actually refreshed
backlog.root_cause: Direct user demand: 'each prediction need add update at time for easy recheck is update or not'. VERIFIED ABSENT end-to-end. The store row type PredictionClaimRow (predictionClaimStore.ts:60, mapRow ~:110) exposes exactly: id, stock, agent_id, claim_text, direction, target_price, resolution_date, confidence, resolution_outcome, actual_price, brier_score, creation_price, is_excluded, created_at, resolved_at — no updated_at. The serve DTO (predictionClaimsHandler.ts) and the page type (dashboard.prediction-claims.tsx:82-83) carry only createdAt and resolvedAt. PO DECISION — ADD A REAL COLUMN, do not repurpose an existing timestamp. Reasoning: (1) resolvedAt is the closest existing candidate but it is NULL for all 5 pending rows in live data, which is exactly the population the user wants to recheck — surfacing it would answer 'was this updated?' with a blank for every row the question is actually about; (2) createdAt answers a different question (when minted) and by construction never moves; (3) FIX-PREDCLAIM-CREATIONPRICE-UNGATE-ZOD-CONTRACT deliverable (c) and FIX-PREDCLAIM-BACKFILL-NULL-CREATIONPRICE both introduce a genuine THIRD mutation class — post-creation edits to a claim that are neither creation nor resolution — after which no existing timestamp can represent 'last touched' at all; (4) the backfill will rewrite historical rows, and without an audit column there is no way for a reader to distinguish a backfilled row from an untouched one, which is precisely the recheck affordance being asked for.
backlog.deliverable: (a) mcp-server: add updated_at to prediction_claims using the ESTABLISHED idempotent pattern already in schema-system.ts:209-212 (try { db.exec('ALTER TABLE prediction_claims ADD COLUMN updated_at TEXT') } catch {}) — same shape as the creation_price and is_excluded columns added before it. Do not introduce a new migration mechanism for one column. (b) Maintain it on EVERY write path with no exceptions: insertPredictionClaim sets updated_at = created_at; resolveClaim and excludeClaim set it to now; the backfill script sets it; any future partial-update helper sets it. Stamping must live inside the store functions, not at call sites — a call-site convention is exactly the kind of thing the next new call site skips. Use real UTC from the runtime, never a hand-formed string (feedback_hand_typed_iso_timestamps_drift_into_the_future.md). (c) Backfill existing rows: updated_at = COALESCE(resolved_at, created_at), which is truthful for every row under the current two-event lifecycle. (d) Extend the serve DTO in predictionClaimsHandler.ts with updatedAt, passing through as null where genuinely unset — never coerced, matching the existing 'all nullable columns pass through as null' rule in mapClaimRow. (e) frontend: render it per claim on dashboard.prediction-claims.tsx as 'Cap nhat luc', clearly distinct from the creation date, and legible for pending rows. (f) Fold updated_at into the Zod contract from FIX-PREDCLAIM-CREATIONPRICE-UNGATE-ZOD-CONTRACT as a REQUIRED field on write once the column exists.
backlog.acceptance: Every one of the 17 live claims returns a non-null updatedAt through the LIVE served endpoint after backfill. A claim mutated by the backfill script shows an updatedAt strictly later than its createdAt; an untouched historical claim shows updatedAt equal to its resolved_at or created_at. Resolving a pending claim advances its updatedAt within the same tick. The value is visible per row on the rendered page. All timestamps are runtime-generated UTC — no hand-typed ISO strings anywhere in the change.
backlog.note: zone=multi because the change spans apps/mcp-server/ (column + store stamping + DTO) and apps/frontend/ (render) — architect splits per the precedent set by FIX-PRED-CLAIMS-EXCLUDED-SERVE-DISPLAY, which was minted zone=multi (commit c40f90062) and dispatched to dev-mcp-server + dev-frontend in parallel (commit b0a786690). Sequenced P2 behind the three P1 rows: an updated_at on a claim that is still structurally unscoreable would tell the user when a worthless row was last touched. Fix the scoring first, then give the reader the recheck affordance.

backlog.title: system-auditor labelled `pdf-extractor at memory limit 98.87% (2.472/2.5 GiB)` as WARN (rank 2) when its own tier-1 ladder maps `peak >97%` to CRITICAL (rank 3): `--severity` is a hand-authored literal with no binding to the measured value, so the dedup layer's escalation bypass (`new_rank > stored_rank`) is structurally unreachable for magnitude-driven conditions — and three improvised dedup_keys for one condition are currently the ONLY reason the 98.87% alert was not suppressed
backlog.root_cause: PREMISE CORRECTION — THE ESCALATING REPORT'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS REFUTED, AND THE REFUTATION IS THE FINDING. The report to PO asserted: `its BUG Telegram was DEDUP-SKIPPED: dedup_key microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY had already been sent at 2026-07-28T14:30:09Z for the BENIGN 85% state ... the key minted while the condition was 'stable plateau, not a defect' now suppresses notification for '20 MiB from OOM and climbing' for the next 7 days.` PO checked the ledger and the signal rows instead of accepting this. It is wrong on the decisive fact. The 14:30:09Z entry did NOT carry the benign 85% state. Live signal_queue row sys-20260728T143010-6ec2, ts=2026-07-28T14:30:10Z, summary verbatim: `pdf-extractor at memory limit 98.87% (2.472/2.5 GiB) — sustained after OCR workload`. The 14:30:09Z Telegram WAS the near-cap alert, and it WAS sent. What the 14:34:57Z emit hit was a 4-minute-later re-observation of the SAME state (98.84% vs 98.87%) under the SAME key — a textbook intra-cycle duplicate, and the router itself independently classified it as one on the row: `router_dedup_note: INTRA-CYCLE DUPLICATE of sys-20260728T143010-6ec2 (same sweep, same pdf-extractor condition, 98.84 vs 98.87). Triage as ONE.` THE DEDUP GATE BEHAVED CORRECTLY. No escalation was swallowed. Filing the reported bug as reported would have `fixed` the one component in the chain that worked. LEDGER TIMELINE, read from docs/data/auditor-dedup-ledger.json at 2026-07-28T14:44Z, which is what the claim should have been checked against: `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:PDF-MEM-01` ts=2026-07-28T12:49:39Z sev=2 | `mem_pressure:pdf-extractor:A-30-PDF-EXTRACTOR` ts=2026-07-28T13:12:18Z sev=2 (this is the 85.54% plateau — archived signal row sys-20260728T131219-3fca, `pdf-extractor memory 85.54% of 2.5 GiB (2.138 GiB) — stable plateau`) | `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY` ts=2026-07-28T14:30:09Z sev=2 (this is the 98.87%). Three keys, one condition, 101 minutes, all rank 2. DEFECT 1 — SEVERITY IS A HAND-AUTHORED LABEL, NOT A FUNCTION OF THE MEASUREMENT. scripts/emit-audit-signal.sh `_severity_rank()` collapses to `CRITICAL) echo 3 ;; HIGH|WARN) echo 2 ;; MED|INFO) echo 1 ;; *) echo 1`, ranking whatever string the calling agent typed into `--severity`. docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md clause 5 states the policy the label was supposed to follow: `verdict=="ESCALATE", reason contains "OOMKilled=true" -> CRITICAL` / `reason contains "peak >97%" -> CRITICAL` / `reason contains "no reclamation dip" (>93% baseline case) -> WARN`. 98.87% is a `peak >97%` reading; the policy says CRITICAL (rank 3); the emit said WARN (rank 2). That ladder is prose in a markdown file, enforceable only by an LLM remembering to read it, and the tier-2 sweep that produced this emit does not read it at all — there is no tier2 flow file (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/ contains only main.md, tier1-probe.md, page-freshness.md). Nothing in the emit script can detect that `--severity WARN` contradicts a summary reading `98.87% of 2.5 GiB`. CONTROL CASE, SAME AUDITOR, SAME SWEEP, MINUTES APART — this is why the diagnosis is producer-side and not gate-side: sbv_fx DID escalate its label across the identical window, sys-20260728T142957-693e ts=14:29:57Z severity=HIGH `sbv_fx stale 43min (SLA 30min)` then sys-20260728T143455-6a8a ts=14:34:55Z severity=CRITICAL `sbv_fx stale 47min (check B-02-SBV)`. Rank 2 -> rank 3 on the same sweep, which would fire the bypass exactly as designed. One condition varied its label with the measurement; the other did not. The gate is common to both. DEFECT 2 — DEDUP-KEY NAMESPACE DRIFT, and it is currently MASKING defect 1. docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:208 prescribes `"dedup_key":"microservice_degraded:<service_id>:<A-xx>"` with the worked example at :93 `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-20`; the canonical key here is `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30`. The call sites instead improvised `PDF-MEM-01`, `A-30-PDF-EXTRACTOR` under a `mem_pressure:` category prefix that appears in no documented category set, and `A-30-MEMORY`. THE CONSEQUENCE IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE AND IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS ROW: because `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY` was a BRAND-NEW key at 14:30:09Z, `_ledger_prune_and_lookup` found no entry, took the `if [ -z "$LEDGER_ENTRY_TS" ]` branch, and SENT. Had the keys been correctly normalised, the 98.87% emit would have collided with the 13:12:18Z 85.54% entry under one canonical key, compared 2 > 2, evaluated false, and been SKIP-dedup'd — the exact failure the escalating report described, which has not happened yet but WOULD have. Key drift is accidentally load-bearing today. SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT THAT FALLS OUT OF THAT: shipping the key-normalisation half of this row WITHOUT the severity-derivation half MANUFACTURES the reported bug. They must land together, or severity-derivation must land first. DEFECT 3 — PO RE-ESCALATION THRESHOLDS HAVE NO MACHINE-READABLE HOME, which is why PO learned of the crossing by hand. PO's 2026-07-28T13:12Z disposition on sys-20260728T131219-3fca reads `RESOLVED, no mint, MONITOR with a named re-escalation threshold (not a silent file-and-forget) ... RE-ESCALATE, and mint then, if ANY of: crosses 95% of cap, OOMKilled=true, or RestartCount climbs.` That text lives in a `po_disposition_20260728` string field on a signal row that has since been cold-evicted to docs/data/orch/archive/2026-07.json. No detector, no emit path, and no bridge reads that field. When 98.87% was measured at 14:30Z, every participant independently re-derived a severity from scratch and every one of them landed on WARN — the auditor's label, the router's corroboration (`SEVERITY: WARN is right — failure mode is OOM -> docker restart -> recovery, not permanent damage`), and the router's trend note (`No push notification sent — the router already spent one push today on a memory claim it had to retract, and a second for a self-recovering WARN would be noise`). Each judgement is individually defensible. None of them had access to the fact that PO had pre-committed 95%-of-cap as the mint trigger four hours earlier. NOT A DEFECT, CHECKED AND CLEARED — the anomaly-task-bridge did not fail: .claude/skills/anomaly-task-bridge/SKILL.md ATB-1 collects `to == "po"`, `status == "NEW"`, `row.ts < now() - 2h`, so at 14:47Z both rows (17 and 12 minutes old) are correctly grace-window-pending, not dropped; they would surface at ~16:30Z. The 2h gate is a deliberate transient-suppression design and this row does not propose changing it — but note that for a service with ~20 MiB of headroom, a 2h grace and a WARN label compose into a 2h blind spot, which is a further argument for defect 1 rather than for touching the gate.
backlog.deliverable: (a) MAKE SEVERITY DERIVABLE FROM THE MEASUREMENT, not merely assertable. Add a measured-value contract to `emit-audit-signal.sh` (exact shape is the implementer's call — e.g. `--metric-value <n> --metric-warn <n> --metric-critical <n>`, or a required `metric` object inside `--detail-json`) and rank from it when present. The derived rank must WIN over the free-text `--severity` string for bypass purposes. The literal `--severity` passthrough into the E-1/E-3 payloads must remain untouched — the file header marks it a deliberate separate design choice (`NEVER rewrites the literal --severity string passed to E-1/E-3 payloads ... EC-5's category_type passthrough rule is untouched by this`). (b) FAIL LOUD ON SELF-CONTRADICTION — cheap, high-value, and it alone would have caught this incident: when a supplied metric implies a rank strictly higher than the literal `--severity`, that is a call-site bug; surface it rather than silently ranking one of them. (c) NORMALISE OR VALIDATE dedup_key against the documented template `<category>:<service_id>:<check_id>`; on mismatch normalise (preferred, with the normalisation logged) or ABORT loudly. A silently-accepted novel key is indistinguishable from a first-ever alert. **SEQUENCING IS MANDATORY, NOT ADVISORY: (c) MUST NOT SHIP BEFORE (a).** Key drift is what let the 98.87% alert through on 2026-07-28; normalising keys while severity is still flat converts today's near-miss into the real suppression bug (see root_cause defect 2). State in the close-out which order was used and show the interlock. (d) ADD A SAME-RANK MATERIAL-CHANGE BYPASS so a flat label cannot swallow a real deterioration even if (a) is bypassed by some future call site: when a metric is supplied and has moved past a named threshold since the ledger entry was written, send despite `new_rank == stored_rank`, under a distinct grep-able marker (e.g. `OK-threshold-crossing-bypass`) so it is auditable separately from `OK-escalation-bypass`. The ledger entry must persist enough of the metric for the NEXT comparison to be meaningful — a `sev`-only entry cannot express `it got worse at the same label`. (e) GIVE THE MAGNITUDE LADDER A HOME BOTH TIERS PASS THROUGH. The tier-1 clause-5 mapping (`OOMKilled=true` -> CRITICAL, `peak >97%` -> CRITICAL, `no reclamation dip >93%` -> WARN) is real policy currently enforceable only by an LLM reading a markdown file, and the tier-2 path does not read it. Encode it where both tiers pass, or state why not. This is also the natural home for a PO-declared re-escalation threshold (root_cause defect 3) — say explicitly whether that is in scope for this row or a follow-up, and do not leave it implied. (f) RECONCILE THE THREE EXISTING pdf-extractor LEDGER KEYS as part of the data migration, or state explicitly and with a reason why they are left to age out.
backlog.note: PO DECISION 2026-07-28T14:52Z — MINT, on CORRECTED grounds, and PO records that its own first draft of this row (written 14:47Z, before reading the signal rows) repeated the escalating report's framing and asserted that the 14:30:09Z ledger entry carried `the BENIGN ~85%-of-cap state` and that the escalation was `silenced`. Both were false. The row was rewritten in place rather than left standing, because a board row is read later as established fact and a wrong root_cause is worse than no row (memory: feedback_premise_date_error_survives_agent_chain — PO corrected the router's premise and then briefly installed its own). WHAT PO GOT RIGHT BY CHECKING: the escalation report named the right SYMPTOM (a re-escalation threshold crossed without reaching PO through any automated path) and the wrong MECHANISM (dedup suppression). Acting on the reported mechanism would have modified `_check_dedup_and_maybe_send()`, the one link in the chain that is correct, tested, and documented. Recording the shape for reuse: memory feedback_router_blames_detector_when_actuator_or_policy_is_at_fault, needing a third branch — `it detected, it reported, it SENT, and it labelled the report at a rank that could not travel and that no downstream reader would act on`. (1) 98.87%-of-cap emitted as WARN against a written policy that says CRITICAL above 97% — verifiable in two files. That third point is the real prize and would not exist without the false report, so the report earned its keep. WHY P1 AND NOT P0: nothing is unmonitored right now. The underlying pdf-extractor condition is minted as FIX-PDFX-TESSERACT-CONCURRENCY-VIOLATES-SINGLE-WORKER-INVARIANT (P0) on direct PO-captured evidence, and the router reached PO out-of-band. The P1 buys down a structural exposure that is invisible by construction: every `MONITOR with a re-escalation threshold` disposition PO has ever written is enforceable only by whoever happens to remember it, and a threshold that fails to fire leaves no artifact anywhere. WHY NOT FOLD INTO FACTORY-ALERT-dedup-window-config (BACKLOG/P1): different artifact, different plane — that is the alert-engine's 60-minute in-service window in TypeScript; this is the system-auditor's bash-side emit path (scripts/emit-audit-signal.sh) plus docs/data/auditor-dedup-ledger.json. Zero file overlap, and window LENGTH is irrelevant here — the two pdf-extractor emits were 4 minutes apart and correctly deduped by any window. WHY NOT FOLD INTO FIX-AUDITOR-A30-VMHWM-VETO-TAUTOLOGY-FALSE-NEGATIVE (BACKLOG/P1/architect/plan_only, recurring_bug_count=5): adjacent, cross-referenced, deliberately separate. That row is a VETO PREDICATE inside tier-1's A-30 interpretation deciding whether to emit AT ALL; this is what happens to an emit that DID occur, at a layer common to every check. Its scope_out already forbids absorbing adjacent predicates and its note warns that folding confounds its FP evidence. One genuine overlap to hand across: its deliverable (d) SEVERITY CALIBRATION asks the same question as this row's defect 1 from the opposite end — whoever picks up second reads the first's close-out. WHY NOT FOLD INTO FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE (REVIEW, shipped 663fc451b): detector REACH vs emit SEVERITY; also already in review and must not be reopened to carry new scope. backlog.title: A-21 windowed crash detector drops any crash whose predecessor startup falls outside the fixed 8h fetch window - a crash after >8h uptime is structurally uncountable, so the detector is blindest exactly when a crash is most anomalous. Same defect in the mcp-server Telegram alert job it was ported from.
backlog.root_cause: The crash-vs-deploy discriminator classifies a startup by comparing it to its PREDECESSOR startup, but it only ever sees predecessors inside a FIXED lookback of 2x the alert window (8h), while the gap between startups is unbounded. Both implementations share it. (a) docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:119 fetches mcpServerStartup rows >= datetime('now','-8 hours'), :120 sets the 4h alert cutoff, :122 loops `for (let i=1;i<rows.length;i++)` comparing rows[i] to rows[i-1]. The earliest fetched row has no predecessor in the set and is never evaluated. (b) apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/restartCadenceAlertJob.ts is identical in effect: WINDOW_HOURS=4 (:96), fetch bound `-${WINDOW_HOURS * 2} hours` (:179), loop from i=0 (:200) with an explicit `if (i === 0) continue;` at :207 commented 'No predecessor -> cannot classify -> skip (conservative: not a crash)'. (c) The same query appears verbatim in the design brief at docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-23-auditor-a30-reclamation-gate-a21-windowed-restart.md:178-181, so this originates in the SPEC and was ported forward, not introduced by an implementer. THE INTENT WAS EXPLICIT AND THE GUARANTEE IS FALSE: :171-173 of the TS job states the 2x lookback exists 'to capture the startup that preceded the oldest in-window startup (needed to classify the first row)'. A fixed 2x extension only guarantees that predecessor when the inter-startup gap is short. Formally: for an in-window startup T (T >= now-4h) with predecessor P, P is fetched only if P >= now-8h; if the gap T-P exceeds 8h then P < T-8h <= now-8h and P is ALWAYS dropped. So the discriminator can only classify crashes that follow LESS THAN 8h of uptime - i.e. it works during an already-established fast crash loop and fails on the first crash after any stable period. The conservative skip is not conservative: it is a silent false negative on the highest-signal event.

backlog.po_evidence_and_priority_20260729T1140: PRIORITY P3 -> P2 (PO decision 2026-07-29T11:40Z) ON NEW MEASURED EVIDENCE, and this row is now coupled to the memory problem rather than being a tidy-up. MEASURED on the host bind-mount, read-only: data/live/lancedb totals 785 MiB for a corpus of ~11243 rows (index_size measured 05:20Z on RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND). rag_entries.lance/data holds 3137 fragment files totalling 596 MiB — roughly one fragment per 3-4 rows, and each POST /index lands a NEW ~6.7-6.9 KiB fragment (the two newest, 11:29Z, correspond exactly to the two index calls logged at 11:29:50.44 and 11:29:51.09). _versions holds 3091 manifests / 32 MiB and _transactions another 3091 files / 12 MiB, so version metadata alone is 44 MiB and grows one pair per write. _indices is 145 MiB across 745 files. WHY THIS IS NO LONGER COSMETIC: 785 MiB on disk EXCEEDS the 768 MiB memory cap, so no read workload can ever have its working set resident, and every hybrid /search fans out across 3137 fragments plus the index set. Fragment count is therefore a direct multiplier on read cost and on cgroup-charged page cache — the thing that has rag-service pinned at 94-98% of its cap. This row and FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP are the same failure viewed from two ends: the compaction failure-path counter defect that row fixes is WHY 3137 fragments accumulated, and the fragment count is WHY reads are expensive. Neither row currently says that; both should. NOT RAISED FURTHER THAN P2: the corpus is still growing normally, nothing is broken right now, and the P0/P1 ready lane is already saturated. NOT FOLDED into the CLEAN-EXIT row: that row is a ~1-line counter-reset with a tight test plan and folding a compaction/retention redesign into it would destroy a small shippable fix.

That note justified the P3->P2 raise partly on the claim that 786 MiB of on-disk LanceDB exceeding a 768 MiB memory cap means no read workload can have its working set resident, so fragment count drives cgroup pressure. THE MEMORY HALF OF THAT ARGUMENT IS RETRACTED. The cgroup anon/file split measured at the 10:12Z restart reads ~726 MiB anon against at most ~40 MiB file-backed, so the corpus is NOT resident in this cgroup and fragment fan-out is NOT what pins it at 98%. That is the model singleton, owned by FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP and FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY. THE DISK FACTS ARE UNAFFECTED AND STILL CARRY THE RAISE ON THEIR OWN: du -sm data/live/lancedb = 786 MiB for a corpus of ~11243 rows; rag_entries.lance/data holds 3137 fragment files / 596 MiB (roughly one fragment per 3-4 rows, each POST /index landing a fresh ~6.7-6.9 KiB fragment); _versions 3091 manifests / 32 MiB and _transactions 3091 files / 12 MiB, so version metadata alone is 44 MiB and grows one pair per write; _indices 145 MiB / 745 files. Unbounded fragment and version accumulation is a real defect with real disk and real query-planning cost, and this repo has an ENOSPC incident on record. P2 STANDS. The still-true coupling to the sibling row is narrower and worth keeping: the compaction failure-path counter defect is WHY 3137 fragments accumulated, so that row is upstream of this one on cause. It is not upstream on the memory symptom.

backlog.mechanism_correction: The row's recommended_action (add a T4 dedup guard, then flip recoverMissedExecutions:false -> true) is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT and must not be shipped alone. Confirmed at source in node-cron@3.0.3 src/scheduler.js: Scheduler.start() sets lastExecution = timeMatcher.apply(new Date()) and lastCheck = process.hrtime() at start time, and the recovery loop only walks back Math.floor(elapsedMs/1000) seconds since the previous in-process 1s tick. Therefore recoverMissedExecutions:true recovers ONLY event-loop stalls inside a living process — it can NEVER replay a fire that fell during a process restart or downtime window. Any restart spanning 1st-of-month 00:00 UTC still loses the audit with the flag set to true. Real fix must be a startup catch-up: apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/startupHelpers.ts already ships shouldRunCatchup() (task 1430) with a DB-backed 'already ran today' guard, weekdayOnly / requiredUtcDay / utcHour window gating, and fail-safe-on-DB-error semantics. Scope this row as: generalise that helper's dedup window from per-day to per-cadence-period (per-month for this job), enrol monthlySignalQualityAuditJob in it, THEN flip the flag as defence-in-depth.

backlog.root_cause:
PO source-verified 2026-07-30T21:1xZ, BOTH planes read at source, not inferred.

PRODUCER — docs/agents/bctc-analyst/flow/main.md:118-127. guard_key = "esc-deepdive:" + ticker + ":" + quarter + ":" + trigger_id; the ONLY emission gate is task_claim(task_id=guard_key, ttl_seconds=86400). The producer is board-blind BY CONSTRUCTION; its 24h TTL is a rate-limiter, never a known-root suppressor.

GATE-B Tier 1 board_hit matches REFLOW-<ticker>-<quarter>, any id starting REFLOW-<ticker>-, a .related entry, or guard_key appearing in title/status_note/root_cause, over all non-TERMINAL rows. That gate is WORKING: zero deep_dive_result signals exist anywhere on disk or in git since docs/signals/processed/bctc-analyst-20260724T152500Z.json, i.e. no Opus deep-dive has been spawned for FPT ESC-5 since BEFORE the REFLOW row existed. FALSIFIED CLAIM (this is the actual defect, and it is load-bearing on the board): REFLOW-FPT-Q1-2026's own title asserts 'minting it also stops the 24h re-escalation'. It does not, and cannot — GATE-B is downstream of the producer. Minted 2026-07-25T15:28:08Z; re-escalations observed 07-28, 07-29, 07-30 (3 file-sourced signals on disk, all byte-identical payloads: report_id e8ea3df5-3f32-413d-a3eb-c71634c0438d, same 7 low-confidence units unit-0008..unit-0014, same min_confidence 0.45, refined_at unchanged since 2026-05-31). Predecessor PO counted 11 consecutive TRUE cycles (c119..c129) at 2026-07-29T21:3xZ; bctc-analyst's own c133 entry (2026-07-30T21:12:55Z) records a LIVE recheck — get_bctc_refined, 15 units read in full — reconfirming ESC-5=TRUE on the same inputs, so the run now extends to c133.

COST, measured not assumed: 4x/day (cron 15,18,21,00 UTC) bctc-analyst re-reads all 15 refine units to re-derive a conclusion that has not changed in 60 days, plus ~1 signal file/day through drain, plus one PO dedup triage per day. This is the 5th consecutive PO tick spending triage budget on the same finding.
backlog.status_note:
AC — READ THE AMPLIFICATION CAUTION FIRST, IT INVERTS THE OBVIOUS FIX.

(0) DO NOT 'FIX' THE GUARD RELEASE. drain-esc-dispatch.md TERMINAL-EXIT (:116-117) and Step 5 (:140) both call task_release(guard_key) on EVERY exit path, including the GATE-B known-root path. Observation says that release is currently a NO-OP: bctc-analyst c133 found the guard still held at 21:09Z with expiry 21:10:43Z, i.e. it survived its full 86400s TTL from the 07-29T21:10:43Z claim, across ~8 intervening dev-team drain ticks. Candidate mechanism (UNPROVEN, do not assume): the release passes only {task_id}, no owner_agent, while the claim was made by bctc-analyst — the known released:0-orphan class in feedback_task_release_owner_agent_mismatch_orphans_lock. THE POINT: if you 'repair' that release, the guard frees on the very next drain and the loop goes from 1 re-emit/day to 4 re-emits/day. The broken release is currently the ONLY thing bounding this loop. Any fix must make suppression correct BEFORE, or in the same change as, making the release work.

(1) STATE WHICH PLANE YOU ARE FIXING. Two coherent designs, pick one explicitly and say why: (a) CONSUMER-EXTENDS — on a GATE-B Tier 1 known-root hit, re-claim/extend guard_key with a long TTL instead of releasing it, so the producer stays suppressed for as long as the owning board row is open. Cheap, needs no producer change, and works with bctc-analyst's no-Bash constraint. (b) PRODUCER-ASKS — give the producer an MCP-tool-shaped known-root query it CAN call without Bash. More correct, more surface. A third option — widening the producer's TTL — is NOT acceptable: it re-tunes a constant instead of owning the condition, the same anti-pattern called out in FIX-SIGNALQUALITYAUDIT-WRITE-GATE-UNREACHABLE-BY-EMITTER-CONTRACT.

(2) DO NOT SUPPRESS GENUINE CHANGE. Whatever suppresses must re-open when the underlying finding actually changes. Negative control, mandatory: with a known-root row open, an escalation carrying a DIFFERENT refined_at or a DIFFERENT low-confidence unit set must still emit. Suppressing on ticker+trigger_id alone would silently swallow a real regression on the same ticker.

(3) FIX THE FALSIFIED BOARD CLAIM. REFLOW-FPT-Q1-2026's title says minting it stops the 24h re-escalation. Correct it as part of this row, or the next PO re-derives this from scratch for the 6th time.

(4) BIDIRECTIONAL PROOF, on the live signal path, not a fixture. Show (i) zero new docs/signals/bctc-analyst-*.json esc-deep-dive-request for esc-deepdive:FPT:Q1-2026:ESC-5 across at least 2 consecutive bctc-analyst cycles while REFLOW-FPT-Q1-2026 stays open, AND (ii) emission still occurs once that row reaches a TERMINAL_SET status or the finding's inputs change. 'The signal stopped' alone is not proof — it is also what a dead emitter looks like.

(5) Regression test pinning the chosen design, so this cannot revert to board-blind re-emission.

backlog.desc: FOUND WHILE TRIAGING telegram reports #4236/#4237 (both RESOLVED as stale pre-deploy false alarms — see status_note). checkStalledResolutionLiveness() (signalOutcomeResolutionJob.ts:80-114) is the ONLY liveness detector on the signal-outcome calibration pipeline. It asks exactly one question: 'how many rows have checked_at IS NULL and created_at older than 72h (and a 3-letter ticker code)?'. That predicate is monotone in ROW EXISTENCE — it can only be non-zero if rows are actually being created. LIVE STATE read from the running container 2026-07-31T15:5xZ (docker exec vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1, readonly bun:sqlite on /app/data/market.db): 105 rows total, 103 resolved, the 2 unresolved are the known-structural MACRO (2026-06-06) + MULTI (2026-06-25) pseudo-codes, MAX(checked_at) = 2026-07-26 00:17:00, and ZERO rows created in the 5 days since. So the guard now returns 0 and reports HEALTHY at the precise moment the pipeline is deadest — the classic passive-health / dead-detector shape (feedback_passive_health_masks_dead_data, feedback_composite_score_masks_dead_detector_pruned_table). Note this is a SECOND-ORDER consequence of the correct fix 314e70718 (FIX-SIGNAL-OUTCOMES-LIVENESS-GUARD-COUNTS-STRUCTURALLY-UNRESOLVABLE-ROWS, now in review[]): before it, the MACRO/MULTI rows kept the count at 2, which by accident made the guard fire daily and kept the subsystem visible. Excluding them was right, but it removed the last thing making noise, so nothing is left to notice that record_signal_outcome has stopped emitting entirely. The PRODUCER-side defect is already tracked as FIX-ALERT-CASCADE-OUTCOME-DEAD (this triage repaired its null zone -> apps/mcp-server/ and raised P3 -> P1 on the live evidence above); THIS row is the distinct DETECTOR-side gap and must not be deduped into it — fixing the producer without fixing the detector leaves the next stall equally invisible.

AC-2: the new assertion must be provably non-vacuous — a unit test that seeds an EMPTY / stale-only signal_outcomes table and asserts the guard alerts, RED before the fix and GREEN after (the existing FIX-SIGNAL-OUTCOMES-RESOLUTION-STALLED.test.ts only covers the checked_at-NULL branch and passes today against a dead pipeline). AC-3: keep the 314e70718 GLOB '[A-Z][A-Z][A-Z]' non-ticker exclusion intact — do NOT re-introduce MACRO/MULTI counting to restore noise. AC-4: preserve the existing at-most-one-BUG-alert-per-UTC-day dedup on the new branch too. Smallest and highest-ROI of the 4 SPIKE follow-ups: one dead weekly pipeline restored by one composition fix. Serve-layer for this table was already repaired separately by DS-DEGRADE-01-FIX (2026-07-23, b1d2f0582); this is the writer side.

backlog.desc: SPIKE INVESTIGATE-EMPTY-DATA-TABLES (2026-07-31, d4569c5b8) found two INDEPENDENT stacked causes; dev-team RAW-reverified both, specifically confirming the catchup-vs-dedup guard distinction. June 1 and July 1 were both silently missed — no error row, nothing. Same root-cause CLASS already fixed for 6 sibling jobs this sprint (FIX-CRON-SUNDAY-STARTUP-CATCHUP x4, FIX-CRON-SSCCHECKERJOB-DEAD-87D, FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD): node-cron Scheduler.start() re-seeds lastCheck from new Date() on every container (re)construction, so a job with one narrow firing window per period loses the whole period if the process is not alive at that instant. davPharmacyCheckJob was never swept — it has shouldSkipRecoveryReplay (a DEDUP guard, prevents re-running) but NO shouldRunCatchup (a CATCHUP guard, makes a missed window run). Sequence (b) before or with (a) — (a) alone yields no data. AC-COMMON: a test asserts a simulated missed monthly window triggers exactly one catchup run (not zero, not two). ROOT CAUSE, single call site: the only production caller of recordHit is runImpactChain.ts:220, which calls recordHit(db, rule.key, rule.matchedKeyword, rule.sector) — FOUR arguments. cascadeHitStore.recordHit's signature is (db, ruleKey, matchedText, sector?, stocks?, sourceRagId?, confidence?), so the 5th `stocks` parameter is undefined on every single hit and the column is written NULL.
