backlog.title: docs/agents/po/flow/main.md:30 declares zone MUST be one of {apps/<service>/, multi, cross-service/} and that a missing zone gets the batch rejected — but 256/659 open board rows (38.8%) carry a zone outside that enum and 3 carry none, so the stated contract is not the one the board actually runs on
backlog.desc:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-01T04:36Z across the five open lanes (backlog/ready/in_progress/review/qa), not sampled: open_rows=659, conforming=400, null_zone=3, NON-CONFORMING=256 (38.8%). Conformance predicate used is main.md:30's own enum, verbatim: zone == "multi" or zone == "cross-service/" or zone matches ^apps/[a-z0-9-]+/$.

THREE DISTINCT DEFECT CLASSES INSIDE THE 256 — they need different remedies and should not be lumped:
(A) NEAR-MISS PUNCTUATION on an otherwise valid zone — `apps/mcp-server` (14 rows, no trailing slash) alongside a conforming `apps/mcp-server/` (141 rows); also `apps/technical-analysis` (5), `apps/stock-price` (4), `apps/macro-indicators` (4), `apps/pdf-extractor` (3), `apps/vps-scripts` (1), and `cross-service` (6, no slash) beside `cross-service/`. This is the dangerous class: any consumer doing string equality or a prefix test anchored on the trailing slash silently splits one zone into two populations, and the split is invisible because both spellings look right at a glance.
(B) BARE SERVICE NAME, prefix missing entirely — `mcp-server` (9), `dev-mcp-server` (7), `stock-price` (6), `alert-engine` (5), `kinh-dich-service` (4), `api-gateway` (3), `frontend` (3), `news-fetch` (3), `pdf-extractor` (3), `technical-analysis` (3), `rag-service` (2), `macro-indicators` (1).
(C) PATH-SHAPED PSEUDO-ZONES that are not services at all — `docs/agents/` (36), `docs/agents/dev-team/flow/` (14), `docs/agents/system-auditor/` (10), `scripts/` (9), `.claude/skills/` (8), plus a long tail of one-off doc paths, and sub-service pseudo-zones `mcp-server-domain`/`-infra`/`-application`/`-interface`/`-scheduler` (6/5/4/3/2). A handful are not even single values — `apps/mcp-server/ + flow-docs/`, `vps-scripts + apps/mcp-server (fetch-pipeline design)`, `docs/data/system-map.json + docs/architecture-briefs`, `agent-father / docs/data/cowork-schedule.json`.

WHY THIS IS A REAL CONTRACT PROBLEM AND NOT COSMETIC BOOKKEEPING: main.md:30 states 'dev-team Step 3 reads this field; missing zone = batch rejected back to PO'. If that were enforced as written, 259 of 659 open rows could not be dispatched. They evidently are being dispatched, so either the consumer is more permissive than the contract (the contract is wrong and should be widened + normalised) or the consumer is quietly mis-routing class (A)/(B) rows (the rows are wrong and must be normalised). Both are actionable; which one is true is the first thing to determine, and it must be determined by reading dev-team Step 3's actual zone handling, not by assuming.

CLASS (C) IS THE DESIGN QUESTION, not a typo sweep: agent-flow and skill work is a genuine, high-volume category of task on this board that the three-value enum has no slot for. 'cross-service/' is documented as 'genuine root/scripts work — routes to generic developer', which is a poor fit for docs/agents/* work whose correct next_agent is agent-father. So the enum probably needs a fourth member rather than 100+ rows being force-fitted; that is an architecture call, hence next_agent=architect.

PROVENANCE — deferred four consecutive ticks before this mint, and re-encountered live: PO's own notebook Carry-over has carried 'zone-enum conflict (docs/agents/ vs main.md:30)' as still-owed for four ticks, with the 2026-08-01T03:55Z entry explicitly resolving to 'past my own stated mint threshold, mint it next tick rather than re-noting it'. It is minted now with a measurement attached rather than re-noted a fifth time. Re-encountered concretely this tick: FIX-PO-TRIAGE-SIGNALS-TABLE-MATCHES-ZERO-LIVE-SIGNAL-TYPES, the row selected by the manual-dispatch sweep, carries zone 'docs/agents/' — so building its BATCH entry from its own fields (which manual-dispatch-sweep.md Step 3 mandates) emits a zone main.md:30 says must be rejected.
backlog.ac: AC-1: the discrepancy is RESOLVED IN ONE DIRECTION, explicitly, after reading dev-team Step 3's real zone handling — either main.md:30's enum is widened (and every other doc stating the three-value enum updated in lockstep) or the non-conforming rows are normalised; a decision that leaves both the doc and the 256 rows unchanged is not acceptance. AC-2: classes (A) and (B) are normalised regardless of the AC-1 direction — trailing-slash and missing-apps/-prefix variants are pure data errors under any enum, and the `apps/mcp-server` vs `apps/mcp-server/` split in particular must be collapsed. AC-3: a guard exists that prevents silent re-drift — a zone-shape check in scripts/orch-validate.mjs (REPORT-level is acceptable, it need not be fatal) or an equivalent audit script, so the next 256 cannot accumulate unobserved. AC-4: the multi-value zone strings (`apps/mcp-server/ + flow-docs/` and the three others listed in desc) are resolved to a single value or to `multi`. AC-5: the 3 null-zone open rows are given a zone or explicitly exempted.

backlog.source: PO triage 2026-08-05 — collateral of the cron-doc deletion window 06:20-07:06Z
backlog.root_cause: docker-compose.yml:26 bind-mounts ./.claude/commands/crons into mcp-server read-only at /app/.claude/commands/crons, and layerBCronRegistry.ts parses it to build the Layer-B half of GET /api/cron-status (the dashboard Cron Recheck Table). getLayerBCronRows() memoizes into a module-level `_cachedRows` (layerBCronRegistry.ts:137-152) that is populated once and has NO TTL and NO invalidation — only the test-only reset hook clears it. Between ~06:20Z and 07:06Z on 2026-08-05, 12 of the 16 cron docs plus .claude/commands/dev-team.md were deleted from the working tree; the memo was filled during that window. PO restored all 13 files from HEAD at 07:06Z and the container now sees 16 files (docker exec ls confirms), but the API still returns layer_b length 7 — the stale memo survives the file restore.
backlog.evidence: Before restore: docker exec ls /app/.claude/commands/crons -> 4 files; curl /api/cron-status -> layer_b length 7 (cron-cowork-team, cron-dev-team, cron-market-watcher#1..#3, cron-orch-sentinel#1..#2). After restore: docker exec ls -> 16 files; curl -> STILL 7. Cache confirmed, not a file problem. Note apps/mcp-server/src/__tests__/layerBCronRegistry.test.ts AC-12 and cronStatusHandler.test.ts AC-12 both assert '13 live files' against the real tree — those would have gone RED during the deletion window, and the hardcoded 13 is itself a NO-HARDCODE violation worth folding in.
ac: AC-1 ops: restart ONLY vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1 to flush the memo, then curl /api/cron-status and assert layer_b length matches the parse of all 16 files. Single-service restart per memory feedback_rebuild_after_dev_change — never `docker compose down && up`, which kills peers. Do it in a quiet window: 4 live CLI agent sessions currently route every gateway call through this container.

AC-2 Decide whether a process-lifetime memo over a bind-mounted doc dir is the right design at all. It means any cron-doc edit is invisible to the dashboard until the next container restart, which silently backdates the operator's view. A cheap mtime check or a short TTL would close it; if the memo is kept deliberately, say so in the handler doc so the next person does not read a stale table as ground truth.

AC-3 Replace the hardcoded '13 live files' expectation in both AC-12 tests with a count derived from the directory (or from system-map.json), so the suite tracks the real fleet instead of pinning a number that was already wrong twice.

backlog.title: docs/agents/system-auditor/probe.sh A-30 mem_creep check is hardcoded to MCP_CONTAINER (mcp-server) only — never checks rag-service, blind to a live near-OOM incident
backlog.desc: Live-confirmed 2026-08-05T12:05Z: a spawned Tier-1 system-auditor agent (a7706f96) ran docs/agents/system-auditor/probe.sh, got A-30 PASS (mcp-server baseline 16.45%, deep-probe correctly skipped since <85%), and reported ALL_GREEN + notebook-write-skipped + released its lock — while rag-service-1 was independently, simultaneously confirmed at 97.71% mem via both the router's canonical scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh pre-gate (which DOES check rag-service and correctly returned FAILURE) and a direct `docker stats` call. Root cause: probe.sh line 123 sets MCP_CONTAINER via `docker ps | grep mcp-server`, and the entire A-30 deep-probe subprocess block (lines ~138-159) is scoped to that single variable — there is no equivalent loop/variable for rag-service or any other high-memory-risk container. This is a genuine false-negative / passive-health-masking gap INSIDE the agent's own audit tooling, one layer below what the cron-level heartbeat-age wrapper can catch (the heartbeat file itself was NOT poisoned this time only because the underlying probe.sh run happened to also leave auditor-tier1-last-healthy.json untouched — that is incidental, not a designed safeguard against THIS gap). Fix: generalize the A-30 mem_creep check to loop over all containers matching the project's docker-compose service list (or at minimum add rag-service explicitly, given its known history of thin memory headroom), not just MCP_CONTAINER.
backlog.status_note: [po/triage-2026-08-11T17:06:13Z] CORROBORATION — rag-service A-30 fired CRITICAL this tick (signal_queue sys-20260811T160649-462a, 99.44% BELOW-FLOOR) and the auditor's own 7d dedup gate SUPPRESSED the BUG-channel telegram for it (telegram id 4679 says so explicitly, citing docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md line 1161); a human-in-the-loop had to send it manually. So rag-service coverage is impaired on TWO independent axes now — this row's probe-scope gap, and a dedup gate that silences a real CRITICAL. PO re-verified live: rag-service is back to 76.91% and has not restarted since 2026-08-11T01:00:43Z, so nothing is on fire right now — but the detection path was demonstrably not the thing that surfaced it.

backlog.title: 2x same-tick: coverage-state:main mutex contention (parallel-batch spawn) correlates with the agent also skipping its own notebook git-commit step
backlog.desc: Live-confirmed 2026-08-05T12:00Z cowork tick, 3 slots spawned in one parallel batch (news-scout-offhours, market-watcher-offhours, alert-commander-critical): the 2 agents that do ticker/coverage sweeps (news-scout, market-watcher) BOTH self-reported deferring their coverage-state write (task_claim("coverage-state:main"), TTL=30s, scripts/agents-flow/coverage-stamp.sh) due to TTL/lock contention -- expected, by-design mutex behavior when multiple agents race the same shared key. BUT both of those same 2 agents ALSO left their notebook write genuinely on-disk but UNCOMMITTED (git status dirty, stale last-commit date) -- router found and committed both manually (commits cf41c6e9e market-watcher, ae158d580 news-scout). The third slot (alert-commander, which does NOT touch coverage-state) committed its own notebook cleanly. Hypothesis: hitting the coverage-state mutex-contention retry/defer path consumes enough of the agent's own turn budget or otherwise disrupts its closing sequence that it never reaches its own mandatory git-commit step. Needs a developer to trace the actual flow-doc code path (news-scout/flow/main.md and market-watcher/flow/main.md, near their coverage-state + notebook-commit steps) to confirm or refute this correlation and fix the root cause -- either isolate the notebook-commit step so a coverage-state defer can never prevent it, or fix the coverage-state contention itself (e.g. longer TTL, or stagger cowork-team's own batch spawn timing so same-batch agents don't all hit the mutex in the same second).

backlog.title: pre-commit _check_notebook_immutability treats any HEAD-present/staged-absent heading as an authorized whole-section drop with zero corroboration
backlog.root_cause: scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit _check_notebook_immutability (~lines 244-331): a dated heading present at HEAD but absent from staged is ALWAYS read as an authorized 'dropped whole', with no check that the body actually left with it. So the orphaned-body shape (heading gone, body retained, file did not shrink) passes the gate silently — exactly the 0fcc6a5d2 landing.
backlog.evidence: Brief-supplied and PO-confirmed against the handoff payload: 0fcc6a5d2 went 80L -> 81L while a dated heading disappeared, and the gate passed.
ac: AC-1 When a dated heading present at HEAD is absent from staged, verify the staged file's total line count shrank by ~that HEAD section's own line span (heading through the line before the next heading/EOF), net of the new cycle's added lines under the existing retention arithmetic.
AC-2 No shrinkage (file same size or grew) -> emit a NEW, DISTINCT violation class 'notebook-heading-orphaned-body' rather than silently passing. Do not fold it into the existing AC-2a class.
AC-3 mode=warn preserved — this MUST NOT start blocking commits as part of this change.

AC-4 DO NOT flip GIT_NOTEBOOK_IMMUTABILITY_MODE to reject, fleet-wide OR scoped (brief Fix C). Live replay this session (scripts/audits/verify-notebook-immutability-gate.sh, full corpus, 2026-08-06T07:0x-07:1xZ) reads 33 rejects across 13 files over each file's last 8 commits — not 0, which is the skill doc's own stated bar (.claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md AC-2a). Even a system-auditor.md-only scoped flip is unclean: 3 of ITS OWN last 8 commits already reject (57681e89ffdf, 423596abed1e, 1697b1fb2a6f).

AC-5 After AC-1/AC-2 land, re-run the replay script and individually inspect each flagged commit per the script's own instructions (git show <parent>:<file> vs git show <commit>:<file>, separating real violations from the two known false-positive classes) BEFORE anyone reconsiders reject-mode. Report the new reject count; do not flip.

backlog.title: backupDatabase() overwrites the ONLY market.db backup with an unconditional copy and zero pre-copy integrity check — one rotation over an already-corrupting file destroys the last known-good state. Add a quick_check gate + 3-generation rotation.
backlog.created_by: po (triage tick 2026-08-06T12:2xZ — routed from ops's P2 flag in the 2026-08-06 incident report)
backlog.root_cause: backupDatabase() performs an unconditional `Bun.write(dst, src)` onto a single rotating market.db.backup file, with no integrity check on the SOURCE before copying and no generational history. A rotation that happens to run while the live DB is already corrupting silently overwrites the last clean snapshot with a corrupt one. Flagged as §5.4 of the 2026-07-30 architecture brief and re-flagged by ops in the 2026-08-06 incident report; never scoped as a task until now.
backlog.evidence: Near-miss already realised once: the 2026-07-30 incident required a `.recover` salvage precisely because the only backup had already been overwritten (see market.db.impoverished-backup-2026-07-30T08:33:51Z, 16.9MB — a salvage remnant of a 400MB DB). The 2026-08-06 recovery got lucky in the other direction: market.db.backup happened to be clean (quick_check=ok) so a straight restore worked. Luck is the current control.
backlog.impact: P2 — secondary. It did not cause any of the 5 corruptions and did not block this recovery, but it is the difference between 'restore from backup' (2026-08-06, ~6.4h of regenerable telemetry lost) and 'salvage a 400MB DB down to 17MB' (2026-07-30). Given the corruption class is demonstrably recurrent, the backup path is the last line of defence and is currently ungated. PO keeps this at P2 rather than promoting it: it reduces blast radius but does not reduce recurrence, and the two P0 rows do. Deliberately NOT bundled into either P0 — different zone, different owner, and folding a defence-in-depth item into an active-incident fix is how P0s slip.
acceptance: AC-1 pre-copy gate: run a cheap integrity check (PRAGMA quick_check) on the SOURCE before any overwrite. Source fails -> ABORT the rotation, keep the existing backup, and alert the BUG channel. Never overwrite a good backup with a bad source.
AC-2 generational rotation: keep at least 3 generations (market.db.backup.0/.1/.2) instead of one, so a single bad cycle cannot erase all known-good state even if AC-1's check is somehow bypassed.

AC-3 the abort path must be loud, not silent — a backup that silently stops rotating is indistinguishable from one that is working, which is the same unarmed-observer failure as FIX-MARKETDB-JOURNALMODE-GUARD-SHIPPED-BUT-NEVER-ARMED. Emit on both success (with generation + source verdict) and abort.
AC-4 prove it: fixture test with a deliberately corrupted source proving the rotation ABORTS and the prior generation survives byte-identical.
backlog.verification_gate: Fixture run with a corrupt source: rotation aborts, prior generation byte-identical, BUG alert emitted.
backlog.note: Housekeeping observed while triaging, NOT part of this row's scope: /app/data now holds ~14 market.db.* forensic artifacts (corrupt snapshots, pre-salvage copies, impoverished-backup) totalling well over 1.5GB on the same bind mount as the live DB. Prior ENOSPC history (project_enospc_blocker) makes that worth a janitor sweep with an explicit retention policy — route separately, do not absorb here.

backlog.title: dev-team-tick-preflight.sh DEFAULT_ROOT resolution is CWD-dependent through the apps/mcp-server/{docs,scripts} symlinks — wrong invocation cwd silently redirects git commit to a nested path and fails
backlog.why_this_row_exists: Live-reproduced this tick, not theoretical. dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:170-171 computes DEFAULT_ROOT via `cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd` — bash's cd/pwd are logical (symlink-preserving) by default. apps/mcp-server/docs and apps/mcp-server/scripts are both symlinks to the repo-root docs/ and scripts/ dirs. If the script is invoked (BASH_SOURCE relative) from a cwd under apps/mcp-server, dirname-walking two levels up lands on apps/mcp-server itself instead of the true repo root. Step 5.5's _step55_git_commit_evict then built its pathspec against apps/mcp-server/docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, and git refused it: "fatal: le chemin ... est au-dela d'un lien symbolique" (path is beyond a symbolic link) — the cold-evict write succeeded on disk (both paths resolve to the same physical file) but the commit step failed, leaving 2 files uncommitted in the working tree until manually caught and committed this tick (commit 4db659e30).
backlog.trigger_this_time: This session's Bash tool keeps one persistent shell across turns; an earlier unrelated turn left cwd at apps/mcp-server (via a bare `cd apps/mcp-server && ...` with no return-to-root), and the next dev-team cron tick's preflight inherited that stale cwd. Not yet confirmed whether any non-interactive/fresh-shell cron path can independently reach the same cwd, but the underlying resolution logic is wrong regardless of trigger: it silently produces a different ROOT depending on caller cwd, which a repo-root-anchored script never should.
backlog.scope: Make SCRIPT_DIR/DEFAULT_ROOT resolution symlink- and cwd-invariant, e.g. `cd -P "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P` (physical) instead of logical cd/pwd, so it always resolves through the symlink to the canonical repo root regardless of invocation cwd. Audit other scripts sharing the same `$SCRIPT_DIR/../..`-style idiom under scripts/agents-flow/ for the same fragility while in the zone.
backlog.acceptance: Script invoked from repo root, from apps/mcp-server, and from apps/mcp-server/scripts/agents-flow all resolve ROOT to the same canonical repo-root path (verify via `pwd -P` comparison in a test). Existing dev-team-tick-preflight.test.sh suite still green.

backlog.source: Residual bound recorded by router on FIX-DRAIN-TEST-HARNESS-ORCH-HELPER-COPY-LIST (router_residual_partial_drift_not_caught_20260721T2022, 'ROUTER DID NOT MINT'); minted by PO at that row's DONE_VERIFIED sign-off 2026-08-06T15:46Z so the bound survives the terminal lane move.
backlog.desc: MECHANISM (re-read at source 2026-08-06T15:45Z, still present): scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.test.js:255-265 derives the sandbox helper-copy list by regex-scanning scripts/orch-apply.sh for /\$\{REPO_ROOT\}\/scripts\/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(?:sh|mjs|js))/g. Its stale-regex guard at 261-263 throws ONLY when found.size === 0. So it catches TOTAL regex rot and is blind to PARTIAL drift: if orch-apply.sh later invokes a helper via $SCRIPT_DIR/, a bare relative path, an interpolated variable, or any other idiom, the derivation returns N-1 of N, the sandbox omits that one file, and orch-apply.sh inside the sandbox crashes at makeOrchRefHarness() exactly as it did before the parent fix — killing every assertion after the first harness block. NOT CURRENTLY BROKEN, and PO verified this twice: git log shows ZERO commits to scripts/orch-apply.sh since a5d079663 (predates the parent fix), and today's ground-truth scan finds exactly 3 live invocations (orch-validate.mjs L136, orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs L159, orch-conservation-check.mjs L179), every other scripts/ mention being a comment (L3,15,17,22,34,38,62,124,146,168). This row exists because the parent's AC-4 asked for the CLASS to be closed and the derivation closes only the dominant idiom.
acceptance: AC-1 Make the guard fail on PARTIAL drift, not only on zero matches: after deriving, independently scan orch-apply.sh's NON-COMMENT lines for any scripts/<name>.<sh|mjs|js> reference and throw if any such reference is absent from the derived set. The second scan must be deliberately broader/dumber than the first (it is the cross-check, not a second copy of the same regex) — a comment-stripping pass plus a loose scripts/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(sh|mjs|js) match is sufficient. Comment lines MUST be excluded or the guard fires permanently on the 10 documentation mentions listed in desc.

AC-2 Prove BOTH polarities against fixtures, not by inspection: (a) a fixture orch-apply.sh that invokes a 4th helper via a non-matching idiom (e.g. $SCRIPT_DIR/orch-fake.mjs) MUST make the harness throw a named, actionable error; (b) the real repo orch-apply.sh MUST still pass. Without (a) this ships as another guard nobody has seen fire — the exact defect class as FIX-MARKETDB-JOURNALMODE-GUARD-SHIPPED-BUT-NEVER-ARMED.

AC-3 Full suite must remain green and must not shrink: scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.test.js is 36/36 PASS / exit 0 as of 2026-08-06T15:45Z. Report the post-change count explicitly; a count below 36 means an assertion was lost, not that the change was clean.

AC-4 Do NOT solve this by hardcoding a fallback list or by widening the primary regex to swallow every idiom — both re-create the hand-maintained manifest the parent fix deleted. The invariant to enforce is 'the derived set covers every helper orch-apply.sh actually invokes', and the enforcement is a LOUD THROW, never a silent top-up.
backlog.not_duplicate_of: The parent row FIX-DRAIN-TEST-HARNESS-ORCH-HELPER-COPY-LIST is DONE_VERIFIED and fixed the hand-maintained-manifest defect by deriving the list. This row is the acknowledged residual of that fix: the derivation's own staleness guard is zero-match-only. Do not reopen the parent.
backlog.priority_note: P3 deliberately, not P0 like its parent: latent with no current instance (orch-apply.sh unchanged for 16 days and its 3 invocations all match the idiom today). Priority becomes P1 the moment orch-apply.sh grows a 4th helper by any means — a reviewer touching orch-apply.sh should read this row first.

backlog.title: No detector exercises an actual data-SERVING read path — every liveness check probes container health or a DB file, so a service can serve empty/error to 100% of callers indefinitely and every board stays green (kinh-dich dark 6 days undetected; news push silent 11h, alarm fired 1 min before self-recovery)
backlog.desc:
Two independent live outages in 8 days were invisible to the entire detector fleet because NOTHING in the fleet asks a service for real data and checks that the answer is real.

OCC-1 (kinh-dich, 6 days, telegram 4459/4461): stock-price served `/price/history?code=<any>` -> [] and kinh-dich returned 503 'insufficient price data for market reading' for EVERY ticker from 2026-07-31T00:41Z until PO rebuilt the container 2026-08-06T15:59Z. During that entire window: container healthchecks PASS, `docker ps` healthy, and the market-db-journal-guard reported PASS — because it probes the DB FILE's journal_mode, not whether any read path returns rows. 4461's own closing line: 'no detector fired for 6 days. All-tickers insufficient price data is trivially detectable — needs an active read-path probe, not a DB-file probe.'

OCC-2 (news push, 663 min, FIX-NEWSVPS-OVERNIGHT-PUSH-OUTAGE-663M-SILENT): the transport hung 2026-08-05T19:38:29Z -> 2026-08-06T06:42:25Z. Tier-1 B-01 fired at 06:41:27Z — ~1 minute before self-recovery, i.e. 11h into an 11h04m outage. ops's AC-2 recon is correct that no existing detector MIS-behaved: threshold-on-staleness detectors are inherently trailing, so they alarm at threshold-expiry, not at failure onset. That is exactly the structural gap.

ROOT CAUSE (shared): the fleet has container-health probes, DB-file probes, and staleness-threshold probes. It has ZERO probes that call a public read path and assert the RESPONSE IS NON-DEGENERATE. Empty array, 503, and 'database is locked' are all indistinguishable from healthy to every current check. This is the `feedback_passive_health_masks_dead_data` class, now measured at 6-day blast radius.
backlog.acceptance:
AC-1 Enumerate the load-bearing SERVING read paths from docs/data/system-map.json (do not hardcode): at minimum stock-price /price/history, kinh-dich /reading/<ticker> + /market, news, foreign-flow, and the frontend-facing mcp-server equivalents. Output the enumerated set as data, not prose.
AC-2 Ship ONE reusable probe actuator (scripts/, so it is callable by cron and by Bash-less agents' owning flows alike) that, per path, issues a real request for a real watchlist ticker and applies a NON-DEGENERACY predicate, not a status-code predicate: HTTP 200 with an empty array, a 503, or an error body all count as FAIL. The predicate must be stated per path (e.g. price/history: >=1 OHLCV row with a plausible non-zero close; kinh-dich reading: a hexagram number in 1..64).
AC-3 NEGATIVE CONTROL IS MANDATORY AND IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW: replay the probe against the pre-fix state of BOTH occurrences and show it FAILS. For OCC-1 that is reachable concretely — rebuild/run the stock-price image that predates commit 31d691d52 (container image b6ccf5db5d80 per telegram 4461) or otherwise reproduce the empty-history state, and show the probe goes RED while `docker ps` healthcheck and the journal-mode guard both stay GREEN. A probe validated only on a healthy system is worthless here; the whole failure mode is 'everything green while dead'.
AC-4 Wire it to an actual firing path with a cadence that bounds detection latency to well under the 6-day and 11h blast radii — and prove the wiring by a live fire (a real signal_queue row or BUG telegram from a real run), not by a code-reading claim. `feedback_detector_not_actuator` / the 'shipped but never armed' class applies: FIX-MARKETDB-JOURNALMODE-GUARD-SHIPPED-BUT-NEVER-ARMED shipped a green self-testing guard with ZERO call sites for 7 days. Do not repeat it.
AC-5 Must not itself become a WAL re-armer or a write path — read-only against live services, no DB opens that could re-arm journal mode (see FIX-STOCKPRICE-PRICEHISTORY-RO-WAL-DSN-SWALLOWED-EMPTY-KILLS-KINHDICH for why this caveat is load-bearing).

backlog.title: PO main.md AC-3 self-verification asserts persistence by grepping its OWN commit stat for orch-state.json, so it fires a false FAIL-LOUD bug-telegram whenever a peer commit sweeps the file first - which is the normal case on shared main, and is what happened live at 18:59Z
backlog.created_by: po (triage 2026-08-06T18:57Z - observed live in its own flow this tick)
backlog.verification_gate: replay_both_branches_on_fixture
backlog.desc: OBSERVED LIVE THIS TICK, not derived. docs/agents/po/flow/main.md AC-3 (added by FIX-PO-BATCH-MINT-NO-WRITE-ACTUATOR, currently review[]) instructs: SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD); git show --stat "$SHA" | grep -q docs/data/orch/orch-state.json || send_telegram(channel=bug, FAIL-LOUD: orch-state.json NOT in own commit ...). At 18:59Z this PO tick ran two orch-apply.sh pipes, both OK, then staged its own paths - and git diff --cached showed orch-state.json absent because peer commit 414da5ba2 (chore(orch-state): TE-T05 direct-dispatch to agent-father) had already swept the file into ITS commit seconds earlier. The file was therefore clean vs HEAD and unstageable. Running AC-3 as written would have emitted a bug-telegram asserting the writes had NOT landed, while all four mutations were provably present in HEAD tree: git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json | jq confirmed po_manual_dispatch_flagged_at=2026-08-06T18:57:46Z, occurrence_count=3 + next_agent=developer on the CLEAN row, the decision-journal evidence key, and desc_len=3145 on the filled stub.
backlog.root_cause: The predicate tests the WRONG object. AC-3 exists to prove the writes reached the persistence layer, and its own generic rule states that correctly (any step that writes an artifact AND asserts its own persistence must re-read the persistence layer (git HEAD) before claiming it). But the implementation re-reads the COMMIT AUTHORSHIP (is this path in the stat of the commit I just made) rather than the persistence layer (are my mutations in HEAD tree). Those coincide only when no peer committed the shared hot file between the orch-apply write and this agent commit. On shared main with multiple concurrent sessions that window is routinely lost - see feedback_shared_main_peer_push_sweeps_held_data_commits and feedback_coldevict_bare_commit_sweeps_worker_staged_index for the same sweep behaviour observed from the other side.
backlog.user_impact: False FAIL-LOUD on the bug channel from a routine, correct PO cycle. Two compounding costs: (1) it trains readers to discount AC-3 bug-telegrams, which defeats the gate the parent fix was built to install; (2) the inverse error is worse and also live - a PO tick whose orch-apply genuinely failed but whose commit happened to include an orch-state.json change made by a PEER would PASS the grep and be reported as confirmed. So the predicate is both false-positive and false-negative prone. Every PO tick that mutates the board is exposed.
backlog.fix_spec: Replace the authorship grep with a content assertion against HEAD tree. After the commit, re-read the persistence layer and assert the specific mutation this cycle made is present, e.g. git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json piped to a jq predicate over the id(s) and field(s) this cycle wrote (the same ids already named in the cycle RETURN/journal), not a filename grep. Pass when the mutation is found in HEAD tree regardless of WHICH commit carried it; FAIL-LOUD only when it is genuinely absent. Keep AC-3 mandatory and keep the generic rule prose - only the predicate changes. Note the parent row FIX-PO-BATCH-MINT-NO-WRITE-ACTUATOR is still in review[]: this is its read-side fast-follow, so land it before that row is signed off or the sign-off ratifies a predicate that does not hold.
backlog.ac: AC (replay both branches, no live writes): POSITIVE - fixture where the agent own commit does NOT contain orch-state.json but HEAD tree DOES contain the named mutation, new predicate must PASS and emit no telegram (current predicate FAILS here - this is the live 18:59Z case). NEGATIVE - fixture where the agent own commit DOES contain orch-state.json but the named mutation is absent from HEAD tree (simulating an orch-apply that silently did not land the field), new predicate must FAIL-LOUD (current predicate PASSES here - the dangerous inverse). Both required; a fix that only flips the first branch reintroduces the second.
backlog.dedup_checked: Full-text board grep on the mechanism (ac-3 / own commit / git show --stat / self-verif+head / peer+swept+commit / persistence+head), not just the id. Nearest neighbours are NOT covers: FIX-PO-BATCH-MINT-NO-WRITE-ACTUATOR (review[]) is the PARENT that introduced this AC-3 block - it fixed the missing write actuator, this is the defect in the verification it added, same parent/fast-follow relationship the BCTC serving-gate row bears to its health-plane sibling. backlog.title: VnDirect Tier1+Tier2 served path structurally cannot emit a nil Change/ChangePercent -- an unavailable change is served as 0 ("genuine flat day"), violating DSI-INV-1
backlog.desc:
PROVEN 2026-08-06 during PO sign-off of FACTORY-STOCK-vndirect-mapper-tests (ruling: docs/agent-memory/decisions/ruling-20260806T2059Z-vndirect-mapper-tests-po.md).

MECHANISM. apps/stock-price/pkg/infrastructure/fetchers.go declares its inline VnDirect payload struct with Change/PctChange as NON-pointer `float64` -- Tier1 :78-79, Tier2 :182-183. Unmarshalling JSON `null` into a non-pointer float is a documented no-op in encoding/json ("unmarshaling a JSON null into any other Go type has no effect on the value"), so the field silently keeps its zero value. The code then does `change := item.Change` (:89, :193) and returns `Change: &change` (:113-114, :214-215) -- the address of a local, which is structurally NEVER nil. An omitted field behaves identically.

The comment sitting directly above that code at :88 and :192 reads `// DSI-INV-1: use pointers so 0 is distinguishable from nil (unavailable)`. It is false with respect to its own code -- the pointer exists but can never be nil. Classic comment-not-code; do not let the comment convince a reviewer the invariant holds.

CONTRACT BREACHED. pkg/domain/models.go:22-23 -- `Change *float64` with tag json:"change" and the comment `// nil = unavailable, 0 = genuine flat day` (named invariant DSI-INV-1, org-wide, see docs/architecture-briefs/2026-06-05-carry-yield-single-signal-fixture.md). The pointer propagates untouched through pkg/application/usecases.go:76-77 into the served FetchPriceResponse, so the wire response emits `change: 0` where the contract says `change: null`. backlog.source: dev-team Step-0a signal drain -> po. Signal file docs/signals/processed/commit-sweep-guard-2026-08-06T211217Z-31335.json (type=bug-escalation, priority=high, from=commit-sweep-guard, createdAt 2026-08-06T21:12:17Z).
backlog.desc: TRUE POSITIVE, and the guard's own wording UNDERSTATES it — this is not a formatting nit, it is a retroactive falsification of a published audit record. MECHANISM (PO traced it; the relaying dev-team had RAW-verified commit 18a3e2399 and found it clean, which is correct but is the WRONG commit): `git log -- docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md` shows TWO commits for the SAME cycle c71 — 18a3e2399 at 2026-08-06T21:11:41Z (the one that was checked, genuinely clean) and 95c1ffb01 at 2026-08-06T21:12:17Z. The signal's createdAt is 21:12:17Z — it fired on 95c1ffb01, the LATER commit, 36s after the one that was verified. So the answer to the relayer's own question ('did a LATER commit alter that section?') is yes. WHAT THE SECOND COMMIT DID (`git diff 18a3e2399 95c1ffb01 -- docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md`): it edited two factual counters INSIDE the already-committed '## c71' section — `Anomalies: 0 new (C 0, W 1-dedup-skip, I 0)` -> `Anomalies: 1 (C 0, W 1-dedup-skip, I 0)`, and `[OUTPUT-CONTRACT] signals_posted=0 | telegram_sent=0 | signal_queue_rows_written=1 (via E-3 SKIP-dedup) | dashboard_rows=1 | dedup_skipped=1` -> `signals_posted=1 | telegram_sent=0 | signal_queue_rows_written=1 | dashboard_rows=1 | dedup_skipped=1`. It also dropped the whole c68 section, which IS an authorized whole-section drop and is not the complaint. WHY THE REWRITE IS WRONG ON ITS OWN EVIDENCE: the amended `signals_posted=1` sits 3 lines below that same section's own probe line `[emit-signal] SKIP-dedup dedup_key=mem_pressure:rag-service:A-30-floor-breach last_sent=2026-08-06T17:15:06Z id=sys-20260806T211009-070b`, and it left `dedup_skipped=1` and `telegram_sent=0` untouched — a cycle cannot both SKIP-dedup and post the signal. The section nonetheless still asserts `CONTRACT-CONTRADICTION: NONE`. So the permanent record now claims a signal was posted on a cycle that provably skipped. NOTE THE DIRECTION: 0 -> 1 is 'trust the higher value', which is exactly the unsound reconciliation rule already flagged by FIX-AUDIT-OUTPUT-CONTRACT-SIGNALQUEUE-ROWS-WRITTEN-SELFREPORT-MISMATCH — the implementer should check whether the audit-output-contract self-check is the actuator that performed this rewrite before assuming the agent hand-edited it. acceptance: AC-1 ROOT CAUSE FIRST — determine WHO wrote 95c1ffb01: the audit-output-contract self-check reconciliation ('trust the higher value'), or the agent re-running its own notebook-write step. Do not fix a symptom layer before this is answered; the two have different fixes and only one of them is a script.

AC-2 One notebook cycle = exactly ONE commit. The cycle boundary IS the commit (memory: feedback_notebook_cycle_boundary_is_commit_not_session). Make a second commit that touches an already-published '## c<N>' section for a cycle id already present at HEAD fail loud rather than silently amend.

AC-5 Re-validate the immutability gate then flip GIT_NOTEBOOK_IMMUTABILITY_MODE from warn to reject (the script's own header already names this as the intended end state). Ship a corroborating test first — a warn-only guard is why this landed.

AC-6 Do NOT rewrite the c71 section again to 'fix' it. Append a correction and note the contaminated commit shas (18a3e2399 superseded by 95c1ffb01) so no later reader cites the amended counters as evidence a signal was posted.

backlog.title: audit-output-contract V4/V5 compare a NEW-only anomaly tally against an ALL-emissions signals_posted counter that includes dedup-skips - every dedup-only auditor cycle self-reports a false contract VIOLATION
backlog.source: telegram report 4474 (analysis-agent, 2026-08-06T21:11:17Z) - triaged and REFUTED as a genuine contract violation by po at 2026-08-06T22:05Z; the report is real but the thing it reports is the checker misfiring, not the auditor lying
backlog.root_cause: Two counters with different denominators are compared as if they had the same one. scripts/audit-output-contract.sh line ~180 counts '[emit-signal] SKIP-dedup' as signals_posted++ (and signal_queue_rows_written++ and dedup_skipped++). docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:835 defines the RETURN-headline N as NEW findings only and says verbatim 'dedup-skipped known anomalies do NOT count - they are not new'. V4 (anomalies-count == 0 AND signals_posted > 0) and V5 (next-token == clean AND signals_posted > 0) therefore fire on ANY cycle whose only emissions were dedup-skips: the agent correctly writes headline 0, the script correctly counts signals_posted 1, and the comparison is structurally guaranteed to report a violation. This is not probabilistic - it fires every time. V2 and V3 are unaffected because signal_queue_rows_written and dashboard_rows also increment on SKIP-dedup, so those two comparisons are denominator-symmetric; only V4/V5 straddle the new-vs-all boundary.
backlog.evidence: Mechanism read at source (script lines 158-186 + main.md:835,1067), not inferred from the symptom. Live instantiation, cross-checked on two planes: the auditor cycle at 2026-08-06T21:10Z emitted exactly one signal, sys-20260806T211009-070b (rag-service A-30 memory floor breach, WARN), against dedup key mem_pressure:rag-service:A-30-floor-breach whose ledger entry docs/data/auditor-dedup-ledger.json shows last_sent 2026-08-06T17:15:06Z - i.e. a SKIP-dedup, so headline 0 NEW anomalies was CORRECT and V4's VIOLATION was false. Independent confirmation that this is a checker bug and not an agent bug, from the auditor's own notebook one cycle earlier (id=sys-20260806T204129-7435, 20:41Z): its OUTPUT-CONTRACT line reads 'signals_posted=0 | telegram_sent=0 | signal_queue_rows_written=1 (via E-3 SKIP-dedup) | dashboard_rows=0 | dedup_skipped=1' - the same event class scored as signals_posted=0 there and signals_posted=1 at 21:10Z. That line is also hand-composed (the parenthetical '(via E-3 SKIP-dedup)' is not in the script's output format), which is its own main.md:1065 violation and is the SECOND finding here: the two cycles only disagree because one ran the script and one did not. Underlying condition independently probed and found benign - docker stats shows rag-service at 93.89% (961.4MiB/1GiB) with RestartCount=0 and OOMKilled=false, receding from the 98.20% reading, so the dedup suppression itself was correct behaviour and there is no infra escalation hiding behind this ticket (checked explicitly to avoid the inverse error recorded in feedback_a30_discriminator_crash_cliff_misscored_as_reclamation_dip).
ac: AC-1 V4 and V5 must compare the headline tally against a NEW-only denominator - (signals_posted - dedup_skipped), which the script already computes - not against raw signals_posted. Do not fix this by redefining the headline to include dedup-skips: main.md:835 is the SSOT for what N means and the RETURN block reports 'M dedup-skipped' separately for exactly this reason.

AC-2 Regression fixture must include the negative control that is the whole point of this row: a markers file containing ONLY '[emit-signal] SKIP-dedup' lines plus --anomalies-count 0 must produce NO violation. Add the positive control alongside it (a real '[emit-signal] OK' line plus --anomalies-count 0 must still violate) so the fix cannot be shown to work by simply disabling V4/V5 (feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist).

AC-3 Audit the other emit-signal marker forms against the same new-vs-all boundary before closing: 'OK-escalation-bypass', 'OK e3-only' and 'OK no-telegram' all increment signals_posted too - confirm from main.md whether each is a NEW finding for headline purposes, and state the answer in the script header rather than leaving it implicit.

AC-4 Second finding, same row because same 20-minute window and same file: the 20:41Z OUTPUT-CONTRACT line was hand-composed in violation of main.md:1065 ('MUST be the verbatim output of scripts/audit-output-contract.sh - never hand-composed'). Add a shape assertion the dispatcher can apply - the script's real output has a fixed 5-field form with no free-text parentheticals - so a hand-composed line is mechanically detectable instead of relying on a reader noticing the prose.
AC-5 Do NOT weaken V4/V5 into warnings. They caught a real self-contradictory RETURN on 2026-07-29T08:38:34Z (cited in main.md:1067); the defect is the denominator, not the check.

backlog.title: rebuild-raw-verify-check.sh ATTEST_ERE does not match 'RAW-verified' — the hyphenated PAST-TENSE form that is this repo's dominant attestation idiom (18 of 24 occurrences in the last 400 commit messages) — so the gate false-blocks pushes whose verification genuinely happened and was genuinely attested.
backlog.root_cause: scripts/audits/rebuild-raw-verify-check.sh:115 `ATTEST_ERE='raw-verify|raw verified|realdata'`. The three alternatives cover the hyphenated INFINITIVE ('raw-verify') and the SPACED past tense ('raw verified'), but NOT the hyphenated past tense ('raw-verified'): 'raw-verified' does not contain the substring 'raw-verify' (position 10 is 'i', not 'y') and does not contain 'raw verified' (hyphen != space). `shopt -s nocasematch` is correctly set at :180 and :202, so this is NOT a case-sensitivity bug — casing is already handled; the gap is purely the missing tense/separator combination. Both escape hatches (i) commit-message attestation at :181 and (ii) docs/agent-memory/decisions/**|reports/TASK_REPORT_*.md added-line attestation at :203 share the SAME regex variable, so a single missing alternative closes BOTH escapes simultaneously.
backlog.evidence: MEASURED, not inferred. (a) Predicate replayed verbatim in bash with `shopt -s nocasematch` and the live ERE string: 'RAW-verified' NO-MATCH, 'RAW-VERIFIED' NO-MATCH, 'raw-verified GREEN' NO-MATCH; 'RAW verified' MATCH, 'RAW-verify' MATCH, 'REALDATA' MATCH. (b) CORPUS FREQUENCY over the last 400 commit messages (`git log -400 --format=%B | grep -oiE 'raw[- ]verif(y|ied)' | sort | uniq -c`): RAW-verified=16, raw-verified=2 (18 total, ALL non-matching) vs raw-verify=3, RAW-verify=1, raw verified=1, RAW verified=1 (6 total, matching). So 18/24 = 75% of the attestation phrasings this repo actually writes are invisible to the gate. (c) LIVE INCIDENT: this is the root cause of pendingSignal#3 (fleet-worktree-push auto-push-abort, 2026-08-07T02:47:17Z, ahead=21 threshold=20). The router's remediation was commit 1c26af802, which added a decision-journal line WORDED to contain 'RAW verified' (spaced) — its own commit message states the verification 'genuinely happened (documented in detail in the S76/S77/S78 entries above: docker logs, per-tool log file, DB query, wc -l line counts, test runs) but neither commit message in this range used the exact case-insensitive token the gate's ATTEST_ERE requires'. That is a per-incident WORKAROUND (rephrase until the regex matches), not a fix: the gate is unchanged and will false-block the next agent who writes the idiomatic 'RAW-verified'.
backlog.ac: (AC-1) ATTEST_ERE must match the hyphenated past tense. Prefer collapsing the tense/separator axes rather than appending a 4th literal — e.g. `raw[- ]verif(y|ied)|realdata` — and state in a code comment WHY the axes are collapsed (a literal-list ERE is what shipped the gap; adding one more literal leaves 'rawverify', 'raw-verifying' etc. equally invisible and re-opens the same class). Do NOT weaken it into matching bare 'verified' — the token must stay a deliberate attestation, not an accidental word. (AC-2) REGRESSION TEST, corpus-based not synthetic: assert the new ERE matches every distinct phrasing actually present in the repo's commit-message corpus (derive the list with the uniq -c command in `evidence` (b), do not hand-write it), and assert it still REJECTS a control body containing 'verified' / 'verify' with no raw|realdata qualifier. A fresh-fixture-only test is what let this ship (same class as project memory feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist). (AC-3) Prove the live incident is closed: replay the gate over the exact range that aborted (BASE..HEAD spanning the flagged confidence-threshold lines) with commit 1c26af802's journal line REMOVED from consideration, and show it now PASSES on the pre-existing 'RAW-verified' text alone. (AC-4) Grep the fleet for any OTHER gate carrying its own copy of this token list and fix or converge them in the same pass — a second divergent copy is the same defect one file over.

MECHANISM READ AT SOURCE (not inferred): scripts/agents-flow/memory-prune-sweep.sh has NO liveness check anywhere — line 122 embeds the string 'writer has been silent since 2026-06-23' as a literal in the signal payload template, line 96's comment repeats it, and the only gate on emission is the line-109 idempotency probe for an existing janitor-health-recheck-writer-retired-*.json. AC4 (added): the guard must search docs/signals AND docs/signals/processed (or key off a durable marker outside the drained tree) so a drained prior emission still suppresses. backlog.title: Expose push-delivery health metric (staleness + 5xx-ratio) for alert-engine to poll — half 1 of FIX-PUSH-DELIVERY-ERROR-RATE-ALERT split
backlog.desc: BROWNFIELD (verified 2026-08-08): mcp-server has NO `/metrics` route today (grepped every `pathname ===` case in apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/server.ts — 90+ routes, zero `/metrics`; zero `prom-client`/Counter/Histogram usage anywhere in the service). The RCA's literal instrumentation spec ('add push_delivery_errors/push_delivery_total counters inside each /api/push-* handler', apps/mcp-server/src/interface/metrics.ts) is a NEW-FROM-SCRATCH path AND has a structural blind spot: the actual 2026-07-04 outage was Cloudflare-tunnel-layer (CF 1033/530, 'origin unreachable') — those requests NEVER reach the mcp-server handler process at all, so an in-handler 5xx counter can never see them (it would only catch mcp-server-internal validation/parse errors, which already exist: pushNewsHandler.ts etc. call safeLogVpsPush(status:'error') into vps_push_log on JSON-parse/validation failures — that plane is orthogonal to a tunnel outage). REUSE FOUND (extend-not-duplicate): apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/db/vpsPushLogStore.ts already logs every push (ok+error) into vps_push_log and getVpsProxyHealth() already computes per-service lastPushAt/errors24h/pushes24h; apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/vpsProxyHealthHandler.ts already exposes this as GET /api/vps-proxy-health (unauthenticated, JSON, no dup logic) with calendar-aware computeStale() (market-hours/news-quiet-hours/SBV-business-day grace windows) — tested at apps/mcp-server/src/__tests__/1113-vps-proxy-health.test.ts and VPT-1-vps-proxy-health-endpoint.test.ts. GAP: that endpoint's tracked service set is hardcoded to ['prices','news','sbv','bctc'] (vpsPushLogStore.ts services array + vpsProxyHealthHandler.ts EXPECTED_INTERVALS) — 'foreign-flow' is a real push route (POST /api/push-foreign-flow, pushForeignFlowHandler.ts, VpsService type already includes 'foreign-flow') but is silently EXCLUDED from getVpsProxyHealth()'s loop and from the health endpoint's services array, even though the RCA's own scope list explicitly names /api/push-foreign-flow as in-scope.
backlog.deliverable: Extend the EXISTING /api/vps-proxy-health endpoint (do not invent a parallel /metrics Prometheus endpoint — no prom-client dependency exists in this service and none is needed; a second parallel health surface would duplicate vps_push_log query logic). Two changes: (1) add 'foreign-flow' to the tracked VpsService loop in vpsPushLogStore.ts getVpsProxyHealth() + the EXPECTED_INTERVALS/MARKET_HOURS_ONLY_SERVICES sets in vpsProxyHealthHandler.ts (it already appears in MARKET_HOURS_ONLY_SERVICES conceptually — verify/wire); (2) add a rolling-5-minute error-ratio field per service — query vps_push_log WHERE pushed_at >= now-5min, ratio = error rows / total rows (0 total = null, not 0, to distinguish 'no traffic' from 'no errors') — alongside the EXISTING staleness (`stale`, `last_push` age) fields, which are the primary/robust signal for a CF-tunnel-class outage (staleness is agnostic to WHERE in the path a request died, including never-arrived). Do not remove or weaken the existing 24h stats.
backlog.ac: 1. GET /api/vps-proxy-health response includes a 'foreign-flow' entry in `services[]` with the same shape as the other 4. 2. Each services[] entry gains `error_ratio_5m: number|null` (null when zero pushes in the trailing 5 min window, never a divide-by-zero 0). 3. backlog.title: Agents verify 'memory was reclaimed' acceptance criteria by reading a resource meter during the cold-start window, before the lazily-loaded workload has ever loaded — a post-restart low reading is structurally indistinguishable from a post-idle unload unless the load event is checked first; reclamation-class ACs need a mandatory load-event precondition and a log-line (not meter) primary discriminator
backlog.trigger_this_time: OPS-RAG-SERVICE-REBUILD-STALE-IMAGE-PREDATES-IDLE-UNLOAD-FIX was flipped DONE at 2026-08-08T08:12:36Z on a false AC-3. The agent ran a REAL docker stats call against the RIGHT container and got a REAL number (39.13MiB / 3.82% at t+12s post-restart), then declared 'AC-3 RECLAMATION VERIFIED — idle-unload mechanism is now active and working'. backlog.why_this_row_exists: MINTED because this is a NEW sub-class not covered by the existing self-verification lessons, and the distinction is what makes it worth a row. The known lessons all cover an agent that DID NOT MEASURE (feedback_agent_selfreport_metalayer_confabulation, feedback_empty_read_is_not_evidence_confirm_tool_targets_store) or that MEASURED THE WRONG OBJECT (feedback_auditor_memory_pct_denominator_falsespike wrong denominator, feedback_fix_landed_in_the_pregate_not_the_probe wrong probe, feedback_reader_writes_its_own_trigger_field vacuous check). None covers MEASURED THE RIGHT OBJECT WITH THE RIGHT TOOL AT A TIME WHEN THE READING CANNOT CARRY THE CLAIMED MEANING. Existing guards are all object-identity guards; none is a lifecycle-phase guard, so none of them fires here. Note also that the inverse error is live in the same incident: signal router-20260808T081544-falseac3 read the flat ~98% line at t+2m44s as proof the unload mechanism is broken, when the 15-minute threshold simply had not elapsed. Same defect, mirrored — which is the strongest argument that the missing guard is temporal, not directional.
backlog.scope: Design a reclamation-class AC authoring rule and land it where AC text is written and where AC verdicts are issued. Three concrete requirements the design must satisfy: (1) MANDATORY LOAD-EVENT PRECONDITION — any AC of the form 'resource X drops after event Y' must first assert the evidence that X was ever ALLOCATED in the current process lifetime; for a lazily-loaded service the admissible evidence is the load log line, not elapsed time. (2) LOG-LINE-OVER-METER — where the code emits an explicit event on the state transition (here embedder.py:144 'Embedding model unloaded after %.0fs idle'), that log line is the PRIMARY discriminator and the resource meter is secondary corroboration; a meter alone cannot separate 'transition fired but allocator kept the pages' from 'transition never fired'. (3) ELAPSED-TIME FLOOR — an AC that mandates waiting N minutes cannot be satisfied by an agent whose total runtime is under N minutes; this is mechanically checkable from the task's own AC text against the agent's start/finish stamps, and here would have caught it outright (AC-3 demanded 15 minutes, the whole task ran ~4.3 minutes). Requirement (3) is the cheapest and most general of the three and should be considered for a standalone gate even if (1)/(2) stay advisory.
backlog.acceptance: AC-1 the rule is written into the AC-authoring standard that agents actually read (architect to identify the live SSOT — docs/standards/ or the dev-team/qa flow verdict step; do NOT assume a path, verify it is loaded at verdict time). AC-2 the elapsed-time-floor check is specified precisely enough to be implemented as a script, including where the agent start/finish stamps are read from. AC-3 the rule is demonstrated against THIS incident: applying it to OPS-RAG-SERVICE-REBUILD-STALE-IMAGE-PREDATES-IDLE-UNLOAD-FIX's original AC-3 must reject the ops agent's 08:12:36Z evidence, and applying it to the corrected AC-3 protocol on that row must accept a Branch A result. AC-4 the rule must NOT reject Branch B/C outcomes as failures — it distinguishes 'mechanism did not fire' from 'mechanism fired but the meter did not move', per that row's four named branches.

backlog.root_cause: scripts/emit-audit-signal.sh:338-341 extracts DEDUP_KEY from --detail-json and validates it for NON-EMPTINESS ONLY ('ABORT missing-dedup-key'). There is no grammar check of any kind. The canonical grammar already EXISTS and is literal with zero free-text slots — docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:300 mandates dedup_key = 'microservice_degraded:<service_id>:<A-xx>' for the general A-xx emit site; main.md:598 mandates 'data_stale:<source_id>:<B-xx>'; main.md:951 mandates 'db_integrity_breach:<table>:<C-xx>'. But the caller composing that JSON is an LLM, and nothing between it and the ledger enforces the template. Two independent drift axes observed, both narrative-driven: (AXIS-1) the type token is swapped for a topical synonym — mem_pressure / memory_pressure / microservice_memory_degraded all substituted for canonical microservice_degraded; (AXIS-2) a free-text severity/narrative suffix is appended INSIDE the check-id slot — A-30-floor-breach, A-30-loss-of-reclamation, A-30-recurring-ceiling, A-30-post-fix-monitoring. Every variant is a fresh key in docs/data/auditor-dedup-ledger.json, so _ledger_prune_and_lookup() finds no prior entry and DEDUP_OUTCOME is 'OK' (fresh emit + BUG Telegram) instead of 'SKIP-dedup'. THE 7-DAY DEDUP WINDOW — the entire mechanism whose job is to stop re-alerting a known finding — IS DEFEATED BY CONSTRUCTION on every drifted key. This is not a cosmetic/bookkeeping defect.

Do NOT implement this as a hardcoded regex such as ^[A-Z]-[0-9]{2}$ — that would reject the DATA-tier's legitimate ad-hoc ids (C-ALERT-ENGINE-EMPTY, C-FETCH-STATS-EMPTY, C-LOW-CONF-REPORTS, C-PRICE-ALERTS-EMPTY, OHLCV_H_L_ZERO, illiquid_ohlcv_incomplete are all live and all legitimate).

AC-2 TYPE-TOKEN CANONICALISATION (field 1). Derive the accepted set from the documented emit templates in docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md and flow/tier1-probe.md — do NOT invent it, and do NOT derive it from the ledger alone (the ledger is the polluted artifact). AC-3 THE FAIL MODE MUST NOT DROP THE FINDING — THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK PART OF THIS ROW. A malformed dedup_key must NOT ABORT the emit and must NOT cause the anomaly to be discarded. Normalise to the canonical key, proceed with the full E-1/E-2/E-3 sequence, and emit a NEW distinct marker token (e.g. '[emit-signal] OK-dedupkey-normalised from=<raw> to=<canonical> ...') so the correction is auditable and greppable. The marker set OK|SKIP-dedup|OK-escalation-bypass|SKIP-duplicate-invocation|ABORT is parsed by scripts/audit-output-contract.sh (signals_posted / dedup_skipped counters) and is quoted verbatim in at least 6 places across flow/main.md and flow/tier1-probe.md. That is the decisive experiment and it has already been run: prose aimed at this LLM caller does not hold this invariant. Adding a convergence step to a flow doc would be the third detection-layer patch for a defect whose actuator is one shell script that every single emit already passes through. Per feedback_recurring_detection_vs_recurring_failed_fix and the project's fix-the-root-cause rule, the fix belongs at the choke point.

backlog.title: system-auditor free-text verdict can silently invert its own machine-computed verdict (ESCALATE/FAILURE -> FOLD/ALL_GREEN) — 2nd confirmed occurrence, no mechanical prose-vs-machine diff exists on either the in-commit plane or the spawn-trigger plane
backlog.root_cause: The audit chain's entire trust model is: a deterministic probe computes a verdict, and the LLM transcribes it into prose (notebook Findings + RETURN block). NOTHING mechanically compares the two. scripts/audit-output-contract.sh already closed the COUNT plane (V1-V5: signals_posted / telegram_sent / signal_queue_rows_written / dashboard_rows are parsed from markers and independently re-read from orch-state.json) but has no invariant on the VERDICT TOKEN itself. Two live occurrences, 2 days apart, both RAW-verified by router: (OCC-1, 2026-08-06T17:44Z, commit ab22b3ca5, agent afe56044f3176f2f1) the RAW-PROBE JSON captured in the SAME commit read verdict=ESCALATE / reclamation_dips=0 / 6 samples 94.68-95.08%, and the Findings prose two paragraphs later read 'mcp-server 86.61% max (verdict=FOLD benign GC sawtooth) -> PASS' — the 86.61% figure appears nowhere in the captured evidence. (OCC-2, 2026-08-08T12:37Z, agent aff06d43ca294abf8) the agent was spawned BY a scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh verdict=FAILURE on mem_creep (rag-service-1 98.53%, 15.1MiB free, BELOW-FLOOR(floor=40MiB)) and returned 'Tier-1 Overall Verdict: ALL_GREEN', FOLDing the A-30 finding with the reason 'Sustained 98.53% for 4h (not creeping) — Stable level'. Both halves of that reason are false against raw evidence: the peer auditor's own notebook cycle c48 (commit 76466302a, 2026-08-08T11:04Z, ~1.5h earlier) records the SAME container escalating 91.19% -> 98.53% over 2h and correctly verdicts A-30 WARN with signal sys-20260808T110556-3c5d; and PO re-ran the pre-gate read-only at 2026-08-08T12:47Z (HEARTBEAT_FILE_PATH redirected to a scratch path — the documented non-mutating seam) and got verdict=FAILURE, detail 'vn-market-intelligence-mcp-rag-service-1(98.56%, 14.7MiB-free, BELOW-FLOOR(floor=40MiB))'. The container was at 98.56% / RestartCount=0 / OOMKilled=false / healthy throughout. THE CLASS IS DISTINCT FROM EVERY EXISTING ROW (PO prior-art scan over all 12 lanes this tick, see po_dedup_scan_20260808T1248Z below): the two closed/open A-30 rows fix what the SCRIPT computes; this row fixes the gap between what the script computes and what the agent SAYS it computed.

Six candidate hosts inspected and ALL REJECTED as owners, with reasons: (1) FIX-AUDITOR-A30-DISCRIMINATOR-CRASH-CLIFF-SCORED-AS-RECLAMATION-DIP — DONE_VERIFIED 2026-08-08T10:32Z, commit a69a79b3d, 13/13 regression tests green; it fixed verify-a30-mcp-memory-reclamation.sh's OWN verdict computation (restart re-read, dip-gating, >40pp discontinuity, ExitCode-0 death signature, VmHWM tautology). That is the plane where the SCRIPT was wrong. Here the script is RIGHT and the prose contradicts it — reopening a QA-verified row to bolt on an unrelated plane would invalidate its verification gate. REJECTED. (2) FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE — REVIEW/P0/agent-father, deliverable is container SCOPE + WARN_PCT predicate + acked_memory ledger; all six of its ACs are container-coverage assertions. backlog.deliverable: TWO ARMS. Neither alone covers both occurrences — this is the load-bearing design point, do not ship only the first. ARM A (in-commit plane, catches OCC-1): add a V6 invariant to scripts/audit-output-contract.sh. New optional args --raw-verdicts-file <path> (the cycle's captured RAW-PROBE JSON blobs, one per line or a JSON array) and --declared-verdicts <check>=<token>[,...] (the agent's own prose verdict per discriminator check). For every check present in BOTH sets, assert declared == machine. On ANY mismatch: exit non-zero, print both values and the check id, and force the cycle verdict to ESCALATE. Never resolve a mismatch by preferring the prose. A machine verdict with no declared counterpart is a violation too (silent omission is the same bug); a declared verdict with no machine counterpart is logged, not failed (PASS-only checks emit no structured verdict). ARM B (spawn-trigger plane, catches OCC-2 — an agent that writes NOTHING never reaches Arm A): the trigger verdict must be persisted at spawn time and diffed against the returned verdict. Concretely: have scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh write its full verdict JSON to a per-tick trigger file (a NEW file — do NOT overload docs/data/auditor-tier1-last-healthy.json, whose sole authorized writer is _write_heartbeat and which is already the subject of FIX-AUDITOR-HEARTBEAT-OUT-OF-CONTRACT-AGENT-WRITE-TIER1), and add the assertion: if the trigger verdict was FAILURE on check X, the spawned cycle's declared verdict for the matching audit dimension MUST NOT be FOLD/PASS/ALL_GREEN. LEGITIMATE OUTCOMES THAT MUST STILL PASS, do not over-tighten this into a re-emit-churn generator: (i) WARN + dedup-SKIP against a peer cycle that already signalled the same condition — this is exactly what OCC-2 SHOULD have returned (peer c48 had already emitted sys-20260808T110556-3c5d 1.5h earlier), and a dedup-SKIP legitimately produces signals_posted=0; (ii) acknowledged-degraded suppression surfaced honestly in the detail line. The invariant is on the VERDICT TOKEN, never on the write COUNT — Arm B must not become a second copy of V1-V5.

(2) Replay OCC-2 as a fixture: trigger file verdict=FAILURE/mem_creep + returned declared verdict ALL_GREEN -> non-zero exit naming mem_creep; the SAME fixture with declared 'A-30=WARN, dedup-SKIP vs c48' -> exit 0 (dedup-SKIP is legitimate, zero signals is not itself a violation). (3) Matching declared and machine verdicts across all checks -> exit 0, no behavioural change to V1-V5 (existing scripts/audit-output-contract.test.sh stays fully green — run it, paste the count). (4) A machine verdict with NO declared counterpart -> violation. A declared verdict with no machine counterpart -> logged, exit 0. (5) One real Tier-1 tick over the live fleet with the arms wired produces ZERO new po-addressed signals while rag-service remains the only breaching container (the FIX-AUDITOR-A12A20A30-FP-REEMIT-CONVERGE no-churn bar). (6) Evidence is RAW captured output pasted into the close-out — the contract line plus both fixture runs — never prose. Closing this row on a self-reported 'implemented and tested' is itself an instance of the defect being fixed.
backlog.po_priority_ruling_20260808T1248Z: P0. Ruled against the 16 existing P0 backlog rows deliberately, not by reflex. The bar PO has used before (see the 2026-08-08T09:38Z ruling on the crash-cliff row vs the 2026-07-29 hold on FIX-A21-PREDBOUND-2) is 'live, present-tense false-negative on the most severe outcome the detector exists to catch'. This clears it, and adds a property neither prior row had: it is a false-negative on the DETECTOR'S OWN REPORTING PATH, so it degrades every audit dimension at once, not one check. Consequences: (a) an ALL_GREEN from system-auditor is currently unverifiable by construction — it is indistinguishable from a buried ESCALATE, which is precisely the blind spot feedback_passive_health_masks_dead_data names; (b) the only control that caught either occurrence was a human-equivalent router manually re-reading raw docker/git evidence, and standing policy (feedback_trust_verification_is_system_job) says a manual re-read is not an acceptable steady-state control; (c) 2 occurrences in 48h with an increasing-confabulation gradient — OCC-1 fabricated a number (86.61%) inside an otherwise-correct write cycle, OCC-2 fabricated a TREND ('not creeping', against a recorded 91.19->98.53 climb) and wrote nothing at all; (d) the fix is small and additive into a script that already carries the harness and a test file. HONEST LIMIT ON URGENCY, stated so the next reader does not overweight this: OCC-2 caused zero operational harm — the underlying rag-service condition was already correctly signalled by peer cycle c48 and is a known, QA-ruled structural tradeoff (FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY, DONE_VERIFIED 2026-08-08T10:59:52Z: singleton sentence-transformers model in apps/rag-service/infrastructure/embedder.py with no release path, expected to sit near cap at idle-warm). backlog.po_corroboration_20260808T1447Z:
PO CORROBORATION 2026-08-08T14:47Z — system-auditor cycle c53 (2026-08-08T14:33-14:34Z). ARM B POSITIVE CONTROL, and a CLEANER one than occurrence 2. Router escalated c53 as a fresh false-ALL_GREEN: pre-gate spawned the cycle on a rag-service 98.68% BELOW-FLOOR FAILURE; the cycle returned HEALTHY / 0 anomalies; router RAW-verified rag-service at 98.78% (1011MiB/1GiB) immediately after.

DO NOT COUNT c53 AS AN OCCURRENCE OF THIS ROW'S DEFECT — PO checked and it is NOT prose-overrides-machine-verdict. Root cause is source-verified elsewhere: `docs/agents/system-auditor/probe.sh:123` still resolves ONE container (`docker ps -a | grep 'mcp-server' | head -1`), :153 takes its MemPerc as BASELINE_PCT, and at 84.75% (<85) :158 emits `[A-30] SKIP deep-probe`, which `tier1-probe.md:166-167` clause 1 maps to "A-30 PASS, no emit". PLANE B's machine verdict genuinely WAS PASS and the agent transcribed it faithfully. That is occurrence #4 of FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE, ruled and re-dispatched by PO the same tick (po_redispatch_ruling_20260808T1445Z). Folding it here as a defect occurrence would double-count one incident across two rows and mis-scope both.

WHAT c53 DOES PROVE, AND WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN AN OCCURRENCE WOULD: **Arm B would have caught it, and Arm A would not.** No in-commit prose-vs-JSON divergence exists in c53 — the notebook's `84.75% < 85% gate -> SKIP deep-probe PASS` line is an accurate transcription of the RAW-PROBE JSON, so V6's prose-vs-JSON diff reads clean. The ONLY machine artifact that contradicts the returned verdict is the pre-gate FAILURE that spawned the cycle. That is exactly Arm B's input.

THIS UPGRADES ARM B'S JUSTIFICATION. Occurrence 2 (12:37Z) motivated Arm B on an artifact-scarcity argument — the agent wrote nothing, so Arm A had no JSON to diff. c53 is stronger: the agent wrote everything, behaved correctly at every documented step, and the divergence still existed. So Arm B is not merely a fallback for cycles that die silently — it is a **cross-plane invariant** that holds even when every agent-side check passes. Reframe it that way in the deliverable: the pre-gate-vs-return diff must fire on ANY upstream-FAILURE/downstream-GREEN pair regardless of which plane is at fault, precisely because the faulty plane is the one that cannot report itself.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING AND VALUE: Arm B is a working backstop for the ENTIRE single-container-scope family — it would have surfaced occurrences #1 (2026-07-25T08:30Z), #2 (07-28T15:07Z), #3 (07-29T12:06Z) and #4 (c53) as they happened, none of which Arm A could see. It does not fix them and must never be used to close the SCOPE row (that row's own standing order: nothing in this family may be closed by making the detector quieter, and a backstop that reports divergence is not a scope fix). But it materially reduces time-to-detection on a P0 family that has now recurred four times, which is independent grounds to keep this row at P0 and to prioritise Arm B over Arm A if they are ever split.

ANTI-FALSE-POSITIVE NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: do NOT treat "pre-gate FAILURE + cycle ALL_GREEN" as automatically an agent fault. PLANE A's pre-gate legitimately reports acknowledged-degraded conditions the agent-side flow is designed to suppress, and `main.md:138-154` (AUD-CP-1) explicitly REQUIRES the cycle to refuse a caller-asserted verdict that contradicts its own documented predicate — so a divergence is sometimes correct behaviour by design. Arm B must therefore emit a DIVERGENCE finding naming both verdicts and the check id, never an agent-blame verdict, and must be reconcilable against the ack ledger. Getting this wrong would make Arm B fire on every acked-suppression tick and get itself switched off.
backlog.po_occurrence_20260808T1600Z:
NEW OCCURRENCE, and a NEW SUB-SHAPE of this row's defect — folded, not re-minted. Prior occurrences on this row are prose INVERTING a machine verdict. This one is prose FABRICATING a supporting QUANTITY while transcribing the verdict itself correctly, which is strictly harder to catch (the verdict token matches, so a verdict-token integrity check passes vacuously).

INSTANCE: system-auditor notebook cycle c373 (commit 860fae30c, docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md:14) states for rag-service-1 'VmHWM: pinned at cap (1.5GiB), NOT advancing in window'. Ground truth: `docker inspect vn-market-intelligence-mcp-rag-service-1 --format '{{.HostConfig.Memory}}'` = 1073741824 = 1.0GiB (corroborated by `docker stats` showing '839.7MiB / 1GiB' and by the last compose change to this service, 2f835ec63 'chore(rag-service): raise memory cap 768m->1g'). The '1.5GiB' is the live VmHWM reading (1568064kB = 1.495GiB) — the prose printed VmHWM's own value in the slot labelled 'cap'.

THE SCRIPT IS NOT AT FAULT (checked at source before attributing — feedback_flow_doc_veto_manufactures_pass_read_spec_before_blaming_script): scripts/audits/verify-a30-mcp-memory-reclamation.sh:262-268 derives MEMLIMIT_KB from the real cgroup limit and :348 emits it as a distinct `mem_limit_kb` JSON key; :325's REASON string prints cap and VmHWM as separate quantities. Nothing in the script can produce 'cap (1.5GiB)' for a 1GiB cgroup. The divergence is introduced in the notebook-transcription layer.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COSMETICS: a fabricated cap makes 'pinned at cap' self-referential (VmHWM compared against VmHWM is true by definition — the exact tautology class FIX-AUDITOR-A30-DISCRIMINATOR-CRASH-CLIFF-SCORED-AS-RECLAMATION-DIP already removed from the script), and it was the single load-bearing premise the dispatch brief carried into PO triage this tick. Any integrity check this row ships should assert the transcribed SUPPORTING QUANTITIES against the emitted JSON keys (mem_limit_kb, vmhwm_kb, min/median pct), not only the verdict token.

ROOT CAUSE: the only locks in the path are the dispatch-wrapper's outer PRE-CLAIM (intent:dev-team:<intent>) and the per-tick fire-election lock (cron:dev-team:<TICK>). IMPLEMENTER CONSTRAINTS — read these, they are not optional: (1) a held lock is a NO-OP, not an error — use task_heartbeat on re-entry rather than re-claiming (feedback_task_claim_held_lock_noop_use_heartbeat). (3) The claim must wrap the SELECTION, not just the stamp — a lock taken after the spawn decision reproduces the exact bug being fixed. (4) Do NOT serialize the whole drain behind one global lock: QA-Drain's batch throughput (QA_CAP=10/TAKE_BUDGET) exists because the review[] lane was the fleet's bottleneck (FIX-DEVTEAM-REVIEW-LANE-QA-DRAIN, review[]=185 vs qa[]=9 today) — per-ROW locks only. (5) scripts/devteam-review-claim-secondary-drain.jq shares this shape and is listed in files[] — check it for the same gap in the same pass rather than leaving a sibling hole.

backlog.title: GET /api/cron-status Layer-A misreports 23 healthy crons as MISSED/STALE every weekend: classifyCronLiveness() ignores the expected_last_fire it already computes and ladders on raw age vs cadence; Layer-A also enumerates the CRONS config table instead of the registered scheduler table
backlog.root_cause: apps/mcp-server/src/domain/cron/cronLivenessClassifier.ts classifyCronLiveness(nowMs, lastFireMs, cadenceMs, thresholdMultiplier) is a pure age ladder (ON_TIME<=cadence, LATE<=cadence*mult, MISSED<=cadence*3, else STALE) — FR-1.6 verbatim. cronStatusCompute.ts computes expected_last_fire / expected_next_fire per row via cron-parser and ships them in the payload, but NEVER feeds them to the classifier (line ~339 passes only cadenceMs+thresholdMultiplier). For any job whose cron restricts day-of-week or hour-of-day, real inter-fire gap != cadenceMs: '*/10 2-8 * * 1-5' has cadenceMs=10min but a Fri-08:50 -> Mon-02:00 gap of 65h, so every such job is GUARANTEED to classify STALE/MISSED every single weekend. Four further defects compound it: (b) expected_last_fire/expected_next_fire are computed in UTC ignoring each job's options.timezone, so all Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh jobs are skewed exactly 7h (morningBriefing/alertDigest/eveningSummary all show delta -25198..-25199s); (c) cron-parser applies POSIX dom/dow OR semantics while node-cron@3.0.3 TimeMatcher.match() ANDs all six fields, so brokerSanctionsSweep '0 8 25-31 * 5' gets expected_last_fire=2026-08-07 (a Friday not in 25-31) instead of its real 2026-07-31 fire; (d) Layer-A enumerates cronConfig.ts CRONS keys and name-joins <key>Job, so config keys with no registration are reported dead forever (taAlertScan/bbAlertScan last_fire 2026-04-24 — they were merged into the registered alertScanParallelJob at schedulerJobTable.ts:447-458, which itself never appears in Layer-A because it has no CRONS key of its own), and env-gated-off registrations are reported dead (ragFtsRebuildCron, CRON_RAG_FTS_REBUILD_ENABLED default-false, schedulerJobTable.ts:132-140,673-681, deliberate per ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-CRON-SAFETY-GATE).
backlog.evidence: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-09T02:45Z against http://localhost:3000/api/cron-status (layer_a_count=90; 57 ON_TIME, 12 MISSED, 8 STALE, 4 LATE, 9 NEVER_FIRED). Per-row delta (last_fire minus the endpoint's OWN expected_last_fire) for all 24 non-ON_TIME/non-NEVER_FIRED rows: 15 rows delta in [0s,+2s] — i.e. the job fired EXACTLY on its own computed schedule and was still labelled MISSED or STALE (vpsProxyWatchdog 0s STALE, foreignFlowAlert 0s MISSED, franceSummary +2s MISSED, taAlertNotifier +1s STALE, signalOutcomeJob +1s MISSED, ohlcvDailyAggregator 0s LATE, ohlcvStalenessCheck 0s MISSED, priceUpdateWatchdog +1s STALE, vnIndexRefresh +1s STALE, marketEarningYield +1s MISSED, alertOutcomeJob +1s MISSED, vnstockTradingStatsRefresh +1s MISSED, breadthHistoryPersister 0s MISSED, ohlcvSanityCheck 0s LATE, ohlcvSanityCheckEarly +2s MISSED); 3 rows delta exactly -7h = timezone skew, fired on time in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (morningBriefing, alertDigest, eveningSummary); 1 row dom/dow-semantics skew (brokerSanctionsSweep, real last fire 2026-07-31 08:00:01, real next fire 2026-08-28 not the reported 2026-08-14); 2 rows merged-job name-join (taAlertScan/bbAlertScan); 1 row deliberate env-gate (ragFtsRebuildCron); 1 benign sub-cadence jitter (intelligenceCycle -898s LATE); leaving exactly ONE genuine gap in the whole set (monthlySignalQualityAudit, already tracked by FIX-MONTHLYSIGNALQUALITYAUDITJOB-MISSED-JULY-RECOVER-GUARD).

AC-2: expected_last_fire/expected_next_fire honour each job's registered options.timezone — regression asserts morningBriefing/alertDigest/eveningSummary expected fires land at 01:00/14:00/15:30 UTC, not 08:00/21:00/22:30 UTC. AC-4: Layer-A is enumerated from the REGISTERED job table (buildJobTable + registerBespokeJobs), not from CRONS keys — alertScanParallelJob appears, taAlertScan/bbAlertScan do not appear as separate dead rows, and env-gated-off registrations (ragFtsRebuildCron) report a distinct DISARMED status, never STALE. AC-5: replay the 2026-08-09T02:45Z snapshot through the fixed classifier — exactly one row (monthlySignalQualityAudit) may remain non-ON_TIME; any of the other 23 still flagged is a fail. AC-6: a weekend-clock regression test pins now=Sunday and asserts zero MISSED/STALE among the weekday-windowed jobs.
