backlog.title: orch-apply.sh advertises dup-key validation but does not check duplicate task ids in task_board lane arrays — 2 ids live, one duplicated INSIDE ready[] with divergent priority + next_agent (SSOT split, first-match consumers non-deterministic)
backlog.desc:
CLAUDE.md and docs/policies/dev-standards.md CANONICAL:SSOT-W1-ORCH-APPLY-WRAPPER both advertise that scripts/orch-apply.sh "Validates (Zod + dup-key)". Live counter-example found by PO triage 2026-08-11: the dup-key check does not cover duplicate task ids inside or across .task_board lane arrays, so two ids are currently duplicated on the hot board and every orch-apply pipe run over them (including this tick's own three) validated PASS.

EVIDENCE (jq over docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, group_by(.id) on every lane array):
  (1) FIX-ACTIVE-READPATH-LIVENESS-PROBE-NO-DETECTOR — 2 rows, CROSS-lane:
      backlog: status=BACKLOG priority=P1 next_agent=developer created_at=2026-08-06T17:39:33Z
      ready:   status=READY   priority=P1 next_agent=(absent) created_at=2026-08-06T00:00:00Z
  (2) FIX-NEWSVPS-OVERNIGHT-PUSH-OUTAGE-663M-SILENT — 2 rows, BOTH INSIDE ready[] (worse case):
      ready[a]: status=READY priority=P2 next_agent=(absent)        created_at=2026-08-06T00:00:00Z updated_at=2026-08-06T17:58:36Z
      ready[b]: status=READY priority=P1 next_agent=dev-mcp-server  created_at=2026-08-06T08:24:43Z updated_at=2026-08-06T17:39:34Z

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: case (2) is an SSOT split, not a harmless copy — the two rows disagree on priority AND on next_agent. Every board consumer in this repo resolves an id with a first-match idiom (`map(select(.id == $tid)) | first`, used verbatim in docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md WF-2, docs/agents/po/flow/supervised-goahead.md Step 1, and scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq's callers), so which of the two rows a gate sees is decided by array position — i.e. by whichever writer last appended. A supervised/plan_only/po_goahead stamp written onto one copy is invisible to a reader that resolves the other, which is the exact vacuous-gate shape those flows exist to prevent. Case (1) additionally means one id is simultaneously BACKLOG and READY, so the same task can be promoted twice.

FIX DIRECTION (not a spec, the implementer decides): extend the existing validator stage in scripts/orch-apply.sh (or orchStateSchema.ts, wherever the dup-key stage lives) with a lane-row identity check — collect .task_board[<array lanes>][].id, fail loud on any id with count > 1, both within a single lane and across lanes. Precedent for the shape already exists in the same script: the conservation-check stage already prints `signal_row_identity=clean`, i.e. row-identity checking is an established pattern here for .signal_queue.rows[] but was never extended to task rows.

SEQUENCING: land the guard FIRST, then de-duplicate the 2 live ids — de-duplicating first leaves the hole open and the board will silently re-acquire duplicates.

AC: (1) a synthetic fixture with a duplicated id inside one lane is REJECTED by orch-apply.sh with a non-zero exit and a message naming the id and both lane paths; (2) same for an id duplicated across two lanes; (3) a clean board still PASSes (negative control); (4) the 2 live duplicates above are resolved to one row each, with the surviving row's priority/next_agent chosen explicitly and recorded, not silently; (5) regression test lives beside the existing orch-apply validator tests, run in the standard suite.

backlog.desc:

backlog.status_note:
[po/triage 2026-08-12T15:36:32Z] ROOT CAUSE MEASURED — this row's scope is NARROWER than the live defect; widen it. Trigger: telegram 4736 (2026-08-12T09:09:16Z) 'macro-indicators /liquidity-state unreachable (deadline) — sbv_omo_daily did NOT accrue today. Check macro-indicators service / VPS.'

PO probed the live endpoint directly at 2026-08-12T15:36:32Z: GET http://localhost:5004/liquidity-state -> HTTP 405 (route IS registered, method not allowed); POST http://localhost:5004/liquidity-state -> HTTP 200, 1241 bytes, time_total = 9.66 SECONDS; GET http://localhost:5004/health -> {status: ok, service: macro-indicators, port: 5004}; container Up 13 days (healthy).

So the service is UP, the route is REGISTERED and the handler RETURNS 200 — it is simply ~10s slow. The failure mode is A DEADLINE SHORTER THAN THE ENDPOINT'S REAL LATENCY, not unreachability. Two consequences: (1) the alert's own remediation advice ('Check macro-indicators service / VPS') routes every responder to the wrong layer and has done so on every fire; (2) sbv_omo_daily genuinely does not accrue, so this is a REAL DATA GAP, not merely a message-quality nit.

Fix scope should therefore be BOTH: split the conflated error string (this row's original scope) AND raise the cron deadline above the measured ~10s handler latency (or make the handler fast). Priority raised P3 -> P2 on the strength of the accrual gap.

Secondary observation from the same 200 response, deliberately NOT ticketed: policy_rates carries source='sbv_rates DB fallback (HTML parse failed)' with is_estimate=true, and sjc_gold_gap reports sjc_price_mn_vnd=0 with note 'SJC price absent from DB (no SJC crawler row)'. Degraded but HONESTLY LABELLED (is_estimate=true), which is the correct behaviour per feedback_usdvnd_frozen_value_labelled_tier1_not_estimate — recorded so a later reader does not mistake it for a new falsification bug.

backlog.title: COWORK SIGNAL/SYNTHESIS filenames are date-keyed (bctc: ticker+date+mode; chef synthesis: date_vn+dish_type; tnb notebook) not cycle_id -> intra-day cycles collide on ONE path; a between-drains write silently destroys the prior cycle's UNROUTED signal = a dropped escalation with no error anywhere. 3rd instance of one root class same day; CONFIRMED clobber today: processed/bctc_signal_FPT_20260715_routine.json signal 9240 overwritten by 8120.
backlog.note:
MINTED 2026-07-15 by po from signal cow-20260715T212838 (data-integrity, MED). ROOT CAUSE: signal/synthesis filenames carry ticker+date+mode (or date_vn+dish_type) with NO cycle discriminator; bctc-analyst runs 4x/day (cron 0 15,18,21,0 UTC) so all 4 cycles collide on the same path (39 such filenames in processed/). HARM (the real one, not the lost artifact): the drain READS these files to route signals; if cycle N writes the same filename as cycle N-1 between drains, N silently destroys N-1's UNROUTED signal and it is never triaged. Today the hourly drain interleaved so nothing was lost -- luck, not a guard; a late/missed drain loses a signal silently. 3 INSTANCES SAME CLASS SAME DAY: (1) chef synthesis date_vn+dish_type -> run2 clobbered run1 (Write, silent); (2) tnb notebook same collision, caught ONLY by the Edit tool stale-read check; (3) bctc signals ticker+date+mode -> 9240 overwritten by 8120. feedback_recurring_bug_escalation (2+ -> block) qualifies. SAME ONE-LINE FIX EACH TIME: key the filename by cycle_id (bctc already carries one; chef's is already in metadata). SCOPE (ba/architect own HOW): the docs/signals/*.json writers (bctc-analyst, chef/unified-agent, tnb) + docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-<DATE>-<SLOT>.json + the Signal Bus naming contract docs/standards/mcp-tools.md (Naming Contract) + the drain reader that consumes filenames. DISTINCT-FROM (checked, none cover this): FU-CTG-DISCOVERY-FILENAME-FILTER (VPS HNX discovery CV_CBTT filename detection), FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES (backfill real-filename heuristic), FIX-COWORK-SCHEDULE-STALE-BASE-CLOBBER. OBSERVATION folded (mechanism UNPROVEN -- do NOT diagnose, NOT a blocker): signal_id regressed 9240->8120 over 20h same file/tool/sequence; parsimonious candidate = SQLite INTEGER PRIMARY KEY WITHOUT AUTOINCREMENT reuses max(rowid)+1 after the drain prunes highest rows; NOT probed because the LIVE DB is a named volume, not docs/signals/signals.db (feedback_live_db_is_named_volume_not_host_data); cheap check for the implementer = does the SERVING schema use AUTOINCREMENT. If ids ARE reused, any cross-time signal_id reference can silently re-bind to an unrelated later signal (worse than an orphan FK -- looks resolved). AC: (1) two same-day cycles for the same ticker/mode never share a signal/synthesis path; (2) a between-drains double-write of the same ticker+date+mode cannot silently destroy an unrouted signal; (3) the drain-reader change (if any) preserves routing of both cycles' signals.

backlog.po_measurement_20260730T2148: MEASURED CORROBORATION + a second, worse symptom than filename collision. (A) FREQUENCY: the identical 8-file set bctc_signal_{BID,FPT,FRT,GEX,HPG,MWG,VCB,VIX}_20260730_routine.json was drained and routed-to-po FOUR times on 2026-07-30 alone - commits c0cbb756f, 236310900 (18:07Z), 23aeea6ed (21:07Z), 072541471 (21:37Z) - i.e. 32 PO-triage routing events for 8 distinct facts, plus a 5th earlier drain (4737c562d 01:17Z) on a different ticker set. Date-only keying is the mechanism: the filename carries no time/cycle component, so every cycle rewrites the same path. (B) THE WORSE SYMPTOM, not previously on this row: the re-written files are NOT byte-identical re-emissions - they are DIFFERENT ANALYSES WITH A DIFFERENT FIELD SCHEMA overwriting each other at the same path. `git diff 236310900 23aeea6ed -- docs/signals/processed/bctc_signal_HPG_20260730_routine.json` shows the 18:07Z revision carrying esc3_guard_held/esc4_result/esc5_result/e3_cache/trick_summary/trick_confidence/kd_reading/cycle_id/generated_at and the 21:07Z revision carrying NONE of them (different prose, different keys, only esc3_status survives); the BID pair shows the same instability (quarantine/kd_durability replaced by roe_pct/pe/valuation_verdict/kinhdich{}/report_overdue/cycle_tick_utc/slot). Any downstream consumer parsing these fields breaks non-deterministically depending on which cycle last wrote the file, and the prior cycle's analysis survives only in git. Fix scope should therefore cover the emitter's field CONTRACT (a stable schema) alongside the filename keying - cycle-id keying alone preserves every revision but leaves consumers unable to parse them. next_agent=ba is still right.

backlog.desc: RAW-verified live by PO on 2026-08-12 against two real occurrences. The detector's verdict is `detected = all_zero OR contract==arithmetic-violation OR contract==plane-mismatch` (scripts/audits/detect-analysis-only-exit.sh:421-424). Both contract_status values that can force DETECTED on a non-zero-diff cycle are computed from `_plane_output_contract_claims()`, which extracts the `[OUTPUT-CONTRACT]` line via `git log -p -- "$notebook_path"`. When the MISSING artifact is the notebook write itself, there is no committed notebook entry in-window, so `claims` is empty, `contract_status="absent"`, and neither violation branch can ever fire. Any other non-zero plane (a real signal_queue row, a real dedup-ledger key) then defeats `all_zero`, and the detector returns PASS/rc=0 on a genuinely defective cycle. The blind spot is self-referential: the detector looks for the agent's self-published claim inside the very artifact whose absence is the defect.
backlog.scope: Verdict logic + claim-sourcing only. Does NOT re-open the exogenous spawner-side invocation question — that remains FIX-COWORK-DELIVERY-PROOF-GATE-ONLY-CATCHES-ROUTERLATCH-NARRATION (architect). This row assumes the detector IS invoked and fixes what it concludes when it is.

If the log path derives from that same root, the existing suites write into the fixture automatically and never touch live data. An explicit override var is still required as a second seam.

RECORD PER INVOCATION (measurable only — no computed token field): ts (UTC ISO-8601, real wallclock via date -u, never hand-typed — memory feedback_hand_typed_iso_timestamps_drift_into_the_future), script, verdict, tick where the script has one, verdict_bytes = byte length of the exact JSON line written to stdout, elapsed_ms, exit_code. NOT session id (scope_out f).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA the REQ must formalize — each needs a named test, and each of the negative controls needs a real fault-injection case, not an assertion that the happy path still works:
  AC-1 One log line per invocation, on EVERY verdict path of every wired script (cowork SILENT/WORK/LOST_ELECTION/DEFER/ERROR/TOMBSTONED; dev-team RUN/RUN-IDLE/SKIP/SKIP-WIDENED/ERROR; auditor ALL_GREEN/FAILURE plus the tier-2/3 SKIP-SPAWN/SPAWN wrapper). Not one path may be silently uninstrumented.
  AC-2 Logged verdict string == the verdict on stdout, and logged verdict_bytes == the real byte length of that stdout line. Assert against actual captured stdout, not against a re-derivation.
  AC-3 Zero semantic change: verdict token, JSON field set, exit code, lock claim/release sequence and MCP call sequence all byte-identical before and after. The mcp_call stub already counts calls — assert the SILENT-path count is unchanged.
  AC-4 NEGATIVE CONTROL, exit code: the logger must not alter the caller's return status. _emit_verdict is frequently the last statement before an explicit return, and cowork's _step8_silent_release propagates via return $?. Inject a logger that fails and assert every verdict path's exit code is unchanged.
  AC-5 NEGATIVE CONTROL, unwritable destination: read-only / missing / full log dir produces an unchanged verdict on stdout, an unchanged exit code, and nothing on stdout from the logger. The tick must never fail because telemetry failed.
  AC-6 stdout purity: the verdict line stays the FIRST and ONLY thing on stdout. Memory feedback_tick_preflight_verdict_is_first_json_key_tail_always_drops_it — a stray logger byte on stdout breaks every downstream reader. Logger writes to the file and to nothing else.
  AC-7 No new tool call, MCP call, git operation or network I/O on the silent/skip path. Local file append only.
  AC-8 Rotation: size cap enforced, last-N lines preserved, truncate is atomic (tmp+mv, never in-place) so a concurrent appender cannot read a half-truncated file. State plainly whether an append racing a rotation can be lost, and if so that it is accepted — do not leave it unstated.
  AC-9 Concurrency: appends are single-write O_APPEND of one line, never read-modify-write. cowork (15 min) and dev-team (7/37 min) overlap, possibly from different sessions.
  AC-10 All pre-existing suites green at or above their pre-sprint counts. The intake brief quoted 20/20, 37/37, 32/32 — treat those as UNVERIFIED; QA establishes the real pre-sprint baseline by running them before any edit.
  AC-11 Every artifact states the honesty caveat: verdict_bytes is a LOWER BOUND on true per-tick cost (it excludes the cron prompt text and the flow-doc lines the LLM loads). See product_decision — this is acceptance-bearing, not a nicety.

OPEN QUESTIONS for architect, flag them, do not decide them in the REQ:
  Q1 Log destination + git-tracked vs git-ignored. PO PREFERENCE, overridable only with written rationale: docs/data/telemetry/tick-usage.jsonl, GIT-IGNORED. Rationale: ~500+ lines/day of churn on a tracked file collides with the documented commit-sweep hazards (feedback_shared_main_peer_push_sweeps_held_data_commits, feedback_coldevict_bare_commit_sweeps_worker_staged_index) and buys nothing — the analysis step reads it locally. Precedent for gitignored docs/data files exists: docs/data/cycle-snapshot-*.json. Note the existing tracked precedents (code-janitor-tick-preflight-last-verdict.json, db-integrity-probe-last-snapshot.json) are single-row SNAPSHOTS, not append-only growth — they are not precedent for this.
  Q2 One shared JSONL for all scripts, or one file per script? Affects rotation fairness — a chatty script could rotate away a quiet one's history.
  Q3 WU-3's choke-point extraction shape, and how the tier-2/3 wrapper is represented without double-counting.

Size M. Chain: BA (this row) -> PO spec approval -> architect (Q1-Q3 + WU-3 design) -> PM decomposition into WU-0..WU-3 -> developer -> QA. WU-0 gates WU-1/2; WU-3 gates on WU-0/1/2 green.

WHY IT MATTERS (not cosmetic): the path is declared `fail_loud: true` in docs/agents/news-scout/init.md:60 always_load, so KLFL (.claude/skills/cowork-boundary/SKILL.md §Knowledge Load Failure Protocol) correctly aborts the cycle. news-scout's notebook confirms the loss: newest entry is `## c249 · 2026-08-11T12:07:40Z`; there is NO c250. The 16:09Z cowork slot produced zero signals. A false ENOENT therefore costs a whole production cycle, every time it fires.

NEGATIVE CONTROL ALREADY IN HAND (this is what makes it a real defect and not an environment-wide outage): cowork-fire 2026-08-11T16:09:37Z dispatched 4 slots in ONE batch — news-scout-offhours, market-watcher-offhours, market-watcher-eod, alert-commander-critical. market-watcher loads the SAME path (docs/agents/market-watcher/init.md:64) and COMPLETED, writing docs/agent-memory/notebooks/market-watcher.md at 16:11 UTC. Same batch, same working dir, same file, opposite outcome.

WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN (the actual spike question): why this agent, this invocation. Grants are NOT the answer — .claude/agents/news-scout.md frontmatter grants `Read` explicitly (`tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, mcp__gateway__call_tool`), so this is not the `limitation=structural / check the tool grant` class. Leading hypotheses to discriminate, in order: (1) per-invocation CWD differs for this slot, making the leading-dot RELATIVE path unresolvable — testable by having the spawn log its resolved cwd; (2) a transient read failure got surfaced with a wrong errno label, i.e. the ENOENT string is manufactured by the error path rather than returned by the syscall; (3) news-scout is model:haiku (the only haiku agent in that batch) and mis-narrated a different failure as ENOENT — this would make it an instance of the known analysis-only/false-report pattern already seen on this same agent, NOT a filesystem bug. Hypothesis (3) must be actively ruled in or out; if it holds, the fix is an agent-instruction fix (hence next_agent=agent-father / zone docs/agents/ per the ARTIFACT-CLASS ROUTING RULING), not a code fix.

RAW transcript for the actual 16:09:37Z news-scout-offhours spawn (agentId ae474a5c3e7df83b0, session 0454e9d8-b475-4230-95c9-8b7d943aa8b3) recovered from ~/.claude/projects/<project>/0454e9d8-.../subagents/agent-ae474a5c3e7df83b0.jsonl. Line 31 tool_result: "File does not exist. Note: your current working directory is /Users/admin/Documents/Hung/__works__/__PROJET/__labo/VN-Market-Intelligence-MCP." -- a genuine, accurate result for the WRONG absolute path the agent itself constructed; the literal string "ENOENT" never appears anywhere in the real tool output -- the agent invented that errno label when composing its KLFL telegram message (line 34, message_id 5087). The SAME misresolution fired earlier in the SAME transcript at line 11 on .claude/skills/gateway-availability-gate/SKILL.md (non-fatal there, not fail_loud, so it silently fell through to a different gateway probe).

NEGATIVE CONTROL: sibling market-watcher-offhours transcript (agentId a5164712412638478, same batch/session/tick/cwd, meta.json-confirmed slot identity) -- line 20 issued Read(file_path="/Users/admin/Documents/Hung/__works__/__PROJET/__labo/VN-Market-Intelligence-MCP/.claude/skills/step-0-cowork/SKILL.md") -- correctly project-root-anchored, loaded successfully at line 21.

H1 (per-invocation CWD differs) RULED OUT: the failing spawn's own Read-tool error message proves its cwd was IDENTICAL and correct (/Users/admin/Documents/Hung/__works__/__PROJET/__labo/VN-Market-Intelligence-MCP); the defect is in how the agent constructed the absolute file_path, not in its cwd -- no per-slot cwd override mechanism exists anywhere in the spawn path either (spawn-fanout.md Step 5.2's Agent-tool call takes only subagent_type/prompt/description/run_in_background, no cwd parameter).

H2 (transient read failure mislabeled) RULED OUT in its literal form: the Read call never had a chance to succeed -- its target path was wrong from the start, and the tool truthfully reported that wrong path does not exist. Not a syscall/errno mislabel on the RIGHT path.

So this is not simply "haiku agents confabulate."

ACTUAL MECHANISM (new, precise, narrower than H3): a per-invocation stochastic LLM path-construction slip -- the model defaulted to the well-known ~/.claude/ home-directory convention (a real, common path in this very operating environment -- e.g. this project's own CLAUDE.md is literally read from /Users/admin/.claude/CLAUDE.md for every agent) instead of grounding the .claude/-prefixed relative reference in its own already-established project cwd, on ONE spawn -- while a textually byte-identical always_load YAML entry in both news-scout's and market-watcher's init.md succeeded on a sibling spawn seconds later, and succeeded on news-scout's own prior 249 recorded cycles. Not a filesystem bug, not a cwd bug, not an agent-doc-text bug, not deterministically tied to model class -- inference-time stochasticity that happens to collide with a highly primed alternate path convention. The "ENOENT" label itself is a narration/embellishment layered on top of a real (if wrongly-targeted) tool result, distinct from (but adjacent in flavor to) the already-tracked leaf-agent narration-fabrication pattern (feedback_leaf_agent_analysis_only_exit_recurring_pattern_20260806.md) -- this is a fabricated ERROR DETAIL on a real failure, not a fabricated SUCCESS on a real skip.

Mirrors the proven execute-not-narrate in-prompt mitigation pattern for a structurally similar stochastic-LLM-slip class (3/3 clean when an explicit grounding directive is present, per the same memory file).

MINTED 2026-07-25T16:49:30Z by po from a coordinator finding during refine-worker verification. The reporter explicitly asked PO to settle the period-provenance question before sizing, and correctly declined to size it themselves. SETTLED BELOW AT SOURCE.

THE DECISIVE QUESTION WAS POSED AS A BINARY. THE ANSWER IS NEITHER, AND THAT IS WORSE THAN EITHER BRANCH.
The reporter asked: do financial_reports.period_year / period_quarter derive FROM the filename (severe) or from parsed content (cosmetic)? Traced end to end, they derive from NEITHER — and neither does the filename. Both come from the SAME caller-supplied ingest key, so they are structurally incapable of disagreeing with each other, and neither is ever compared to the document.
  - apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:183-184 — periodYear/periodQuarter are read out of multipart form fields: fields.get("period_year"), fields.get("period_quarter"). Purely caller-supplied by the VPS pusher.
  - :194-201 — the ONLY validation is on SHAPE: year rejected unless 2000..2099, quarter rejected unless in {Q1,Q2,Q3,Q4}. The pair (2025, Q4) is perfectly well-formed and passes. Nothing checks correspondence to the PDF.
  - :224 — normaliseFilename(sourceUrl || actionCode+".pdf", actionCode, periodYear, periodQuarter). THE FILENAME IS DERIVED FROM THE PERIOD KEY, not the reverse.
  - apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/resolvePdfText.ts:45-61 — canonical = ACTIONCODE_YEAR_QUARTER.pdf; the source URL's own basename is used ONLY if it ends in .pdf AND already contains the action code. "DPM_2025_Q4.pdf" is exactly the canonical form, so it is a RENDERING of the stored key.
  - apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/parseBctcReport.ts:77-82 — ParseBctcReportParams.period is a PARAMETER of type FiscalPeriod. The parser is TOLD the period; it never reads it out of rawText.
  - :465-470 — $periodYear: report.period.year, $periodQuarter: report.period.quarter, $sortKey: report.period.sortKey written straight through to the INSERT at :354.
CONCLUSION: the filename is NOT cosmetic and is NOT independent evidence. It is the same value as the DB period columns, from the same unvalidated source. The reporter's "if from the filename" severity branch is the one that applies — for a different reason than they expected.

SEVERITY IS HIGHER THAN EITHER BRANCH THE REPORTER OFFERED, BECAUSE OF SLOT OCCUPANCY.
sort_key is year-quarter, built from the same key, and the row identity/conflict key is (action_code, sort_key) — see parseBctcReport.ts:316 (.get(report.actionCode, report.period.sortKey)) and the ON CONFLICT clause at :393. A document mislabelled 2025-Q4 does not merely carry a wrong label: IT OCCUPIES THE SLOT THE REAL DPM Q4-2025 REPORT WOULD LAND IN. The correct Q4-2025 filing can never be ingested into that slot while this row holds it. That is a durable data-loss condition, not a display bug.
Second consequence, as the reporter predicted: apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/financial-reports/bctcFullTools.ts:461 sets deltaType = latest.period_year !== priorRow.period_year ? "YoY" : "QoQ". Q1-2026 financials stored as 2025-Q4 will be diffed against DPM 2025-Q3 and labelled QoQ. Every DPM QoQ/YoY series is then wrong, and wrong in a way that looks well-formed.

TIME PRESSURE IS REAL BUT THE REPORTER'S URGENCY MODEL IS WRONG, AND ACTING ON IT WOULD WASTE WORK.
The report reasons that "the remaining 31 windows keep accreting under whatever period identity is stored", so each daily fire deepens the mislabel. IT DOES NOT. The period identity is a SINGLE key already fixed on the row at ingest; the 31 remaining windows all inherit that one key and cannot make it more wrong. Nothing degrades per fire.
WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES STATE IS FINALIZE. Live probe this tick through the mcp-server runtime: get_bctc_report_id(code="DPM") returns {report_id: null, report_ids: [], count: 0, existing_refine_status: "PENDING"}. That tool filters on refine_status='DONE' (getBctcReportIdTool.ts:131), so RIGHT NOW nothing is served and no consumer can reach the mislabelled document. Finalize flips refine_status to DONE and ARMS it.
THEREFORE: do NOT halt the refine slot — that discards the 15 completed windows for no safety gain, since the mislabel neither grows nor becomes reachable while status is PENDING. The correct intervention is to correct or remove the period identity on this one row BEFORE finalize. That is an ops/data action, is AC 1 below, and is deliberately separated from the code fix so it can run on a different clock.

CONCRETE INSTANCE (reporter's evidence, accepted — five independent pages, internally consistent, correctly reasoned): report_id 5b0dad71-3b05-4455-9823-c2072442777d, stored as DPM_2025_Q4.pdf, content unambiguously Q1-2026 — unit-0005 "Cho ky hoat dong tu ngay 01 thang 01 nam 2026 den ngay 31 thang 03 nam 2026"; unit-0007 "Tu 01/01/2026 den 31/03/2026" with a "Tu 01/01/2025 den 31/03/2025" comparative; unit-0009 "Quy I Nam 2026" + "Tai ngay 31 thang 03 nam 2026"; unit-0010 "Tai ngay 31 thang 03 nam 2026"; unit-0011 "Quy I Nam 2026". The reporter pre-emptively excluded the OCR-year-misread hypothesis (2025 appears correctly throughout as the comparative column, "Nam 2025 (Trinh bay lai)") — po concurs, and Q4-2025 covers Oct-Dec 2025 while this document covers Jan-Mar 2026, which are disjoint periods, not an off-by-one.

BLAST-RADIUS QUESTION ANSWERED — DPM IS NOT IMPLICATED IN THE 07-19 REPARSE CORRUPTION. The reporter asked whether DPM fell inside FIX-BCTC-REPARSE-BATCH-CORRUPTION-NGAYNOP-FLIP. It did not: that incident's decision record names CTG, DBC, DGC, DXG, FRT, GEX, KDC, KDH, MSN, PDR, SAB, SHB, VCB, VJC, VND — no DPM. Different defect (that one flipped ngay_nop and zeroed total_assets), different mechanism, no shared cause. Do not bundle them.

CLASS PARALLEL — THIS IS THE UC-CDC-P1 MECHANISM IN A SECOND SUBSYSTEM, AND THE REPAIR SHAPE IS ALREADY RATIFIED THERE. UC-CDC-P1: calendar_status is caller-supplied, the tool's Zod schema is a bare z.string().optional() with no enum gate, the server never computes it, and a correct producer (vnTradingCalendar) already existed unwired. Here: period identity is caller-supplied, validation is shape-only, the server never derives it, and a correct producer already exists — THE DOCUMENT ITSELF, which states its period unambiguously on five separate pages. Both are instances of memory lesson feedback_pressure_state_caller_supplied_fields_dead_server_computed_live. The ratified remedy shape there was: compute server-side at the boundary AND gate the caller override. Apply that shape; do not invent a new one.

REMEDY — DIRECTION SETTLED, ONE GENUINELY OPEN CHOICE.
Add a period-vs-content check at the ingest/parse boundary so a document whose stated period contradicts its supplied key cannot be silently stored under that key. Honest options, NOT chosen by po:
  [a] VALIDATE ONLY — extract the period from the PDF text, compare to the supplied key, and on mismatch reject-or-quarantine rather than writing. Conservative; keeps the caller as source of truth and only refuses contradictions.
  [b] DERIVE FROM CONTENT — treat the caller key as a hint and take the period from the document.
  [c] BOTH — derive, and gate the caller override the way UC-CDC-P1 gates calendar_status.
STRONG CAUTION AGAINST NAIVE [b], from this very document: the reporter also found units 0002/0003 carrying OCR_quality_critical at confidence 0.45-0.50. Text quality is NOT guaranteed, so a content-derived period would itself be unreliable on exactly the poor-OCR filings that most need checking. Whatever is chosen must FAIL LOUD (quarantine) rather than fall back to the unvalidated key, or it re-creates this defect with extra steps. A mismatch must never resolve silently in either direction.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. DATA, AND IT IS TIME-ORDERED FIRST: report_id 5b0dad71-3b05-4455-9823-c2072442777d is corrected or removed BEFORE its refine finalizes, so it never occupies (DPM, 2025-Q4) in a DONE state. Verify via get_bctc_report_id(code="DPM", year=2025, quarter="Q4") returning either nothing or a document whose content is genuinely Oct-Dec 2025.
  2. CODE: a document whose text states a period contradicting the supplied (year, quarter) key is NOT written under that key — it is rejected or quarantined, with a loud signal naming both periods.
  3. NEGATIVE CONTROL (mandatory — without it the fix degrades into blanket rejection): a correctly-labelled filing, AND a filing whose text is too poor to extract a period at all, must BOTH still ingest normally. Do not let "cannot determine period" become "reject".
  4. The real DPM Q4-2025 report can subsequently be ingested into the freed slot — proving the fix restored capacity, not merely removed a bad row.
  5. Regression test asserting the (action_code, sort_key) slot cannot be occupied by a document of a different period.

SECONDARY, EVIDENCE ONLY — DO NOT MINT, DO NOT EXPAND SCOPE INTO IT. The reporter also flagged unit-0003's "I. No dai han" total 215.286.231.782 against listed sub-items 132.540.000.000 + 78.521.573.782 = 211.061.573.782, a ~4.2bn gap consistent with a dropped line, at confidence 0.45-0.50. That is ESC-5 deep-dive territory per the existing low-confidence handling path, and is recorded here only because it is the same document and is the direct evidence for the [b] caution above. It is NOT part of this row's acceptance.

DO NOT ROUTE THIS THROUGH FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES — see the warning annotation added to that row this tick. Fixing filename derivation alone would make the filename stop reflecting the stored period, removing the only visible symptom while the corruption persists. That is active harm, not a partial fix.

ready.title: Ready-Lane Consumer has no severity/incident expedite path: inside one priority class the tiebreak is the ready[] array index, so a P0 minted for a LIVE production incident lands at the back of a 78-deep queue and is unreachable in incident time
ready.desc: MEASURED, not inferred. Replaying scripts/devteam-backlog-claim-ready-lane-consumer.jq 14 successive times against a live copy of the board on 2026-08-12T05:36Z put FIX-RAG-EMBEDDER-IDLE-UNLOAD-ALLOCATOR-PAGES-NOT-RETURNED-TO-OS — a P0 for a service that was OOM-cycling every ~50 minutes and had taken 3 emergency ops restarts in 90 minutes — at pick #8. It sits at ready[] index 76 of 78 and is the LAST of 26 P0 rows in the lane. RLC's documented selection is 'ordered by priority_rank ascending, tiebreak by ready[] array index (FIFO proxy)'; a row minted today is always appended, so recency and severity are anti-correlated with dispatch order inside a priority class. Compounding factors, both live-verified: RLC claims exactly ONE row per invocation (its own header: 'single row per invocation'), and it only runs when it wins the 6-way idle-chain rotation (.dev_team_idle_chain.rotation shows all 6 candidates served ~30min apart, i.e. ~3h per lane, against cron `7,37 * * * *`). Every pick must additionally satisfy wip_in_progress < 2. Floor-bound expected latency for the tail of the P0 class is ~24h and realistically days. PO had to hand-dispatch out of band, which is a producer-with-no-mechanism escape hatch, not a designed path.
ready.scope: Design an expedite/severity dimension for ready-lane selection that does NOT simply add a 4th priority tier (P0 is already saturated at 26 rows — a new tier saturates the same way). Candidate shapes for the architect to adjudicate, none pre-selected: (a) an explicit, PO-settable `expedite_at` / `incident_ref` field that sorts ahead of priority_rank and is bounded to N rows so it cannot itself saturate; (b) age-weighted or arrival-inverted tiebreak inside a priority class so a fresh incident row is not structurally last; (c) a separate low-cardinality incident lane with its own budget, outside the shared WIP<=2 slot and outside the 6-way rotation, mirroring how QA-Drain already carries an independent qa[] budget for structurally different work. Any design MUST keep the existing single-linear head-writer collision-freedom proof intact (docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-29-qadrain-head-slot-decouple.md).

ready.title: PUBLISHED-MARKER KEY AGREEMENT — derive the dedup key from the scheduled UTC fire-window, never from a wall-clock date read (P0: chef-evening double-published 2026-07-22 19:56Z + 20:00Z on keys :2026-07-22 vs :2026-07-23 derived from ONE instant; the same defect will FALSELY SUPPRESS the 2026-07-23 19:45Z dish)
ready.note:
ROOT CAUSE (RAW-verified 2026-07-22T20:00-20:10Z, router + po). chef-evening cron is `45 19 * * *` = 19:45 UTC = 02:45 VN of D+1 — cowork-schedule.json chef-evening.vn_description literally reads '02:45 VN next day (GMT+7)'. chef.md Step 0.5 L48 computes WORK_DATE = TZ="Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh" date +%Y-%m-%d and L70 builds MARKER_KEY = published:<slot>:<WORK_DATE>. Because this slot fires AFTER VN midnight, the key straddles a date boundary: two peers reading the SAME wall-clock instant derive DIFFERENT keys. EVIDENCE — task_list_held(task_kind=cowork-slot) shows BOTH published:chef-evening:2026-07-22 (owner_client_session 9f4a6bfc-b001-4349-8a44-545f24c1b0ac, claimed_at 1784750141 = 19:55:41Z) AND published:chef-evening:2026-07-23 (owner_client_session ab870ed6-0502-4e49-811a-8e7c90aff1ef, claimed_at 1784750490 = 20:01:30Z) HELD SIMULTANEOUSLY, ttl_seconds 100800 each. Both runs therefore claimed successfully, both passed the gate, both published. Artifacts on disk, both dish_type=evening + quality_verdict=degraded, overlapping conviction VHM+VIC: docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-22-evening.json (date_vn 2026-07-22, timestamp_utc 19:56:15Z, EIB/VIC/VHM/VJC, regime risk-off) and docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-23-evening.json (date_vn 2026-07-23, timestamp_utc 20:00:37Z, VHM/VIC/VCB, regime carry-unwind-risk-off). NOTE the historical convention was the UTC/trading-day label — published:chef-evening:2026-07-21 was claimed 2026-07-21T19:51:10Z i.e. VN 07-22 — so the 19:55Z run followed PRECEDENT while the 20:01Z run followed the SPEC AS WRITTEN. Neither agent misbehaved. The spec is ambiguous exactly at the boundary it is supposed to defend.

WHY THIS IS **NOT** UC-CCA-P3 — DO NOT FOLD AND CLOSE. UC-CCA-P3 fixes marker LIFECYCLE (claim timing + release immunity). Its design recommendation (early read-only probe + late task_claim immediately before send_telegram + never release) would NOT have prevented this incident: both peers would still compute DIFFERENT keys, both probes would read free, both late claims would succeed, both would publish. Key AGREEMENT is orthogonal to key LIFECYCLE. A mutex whose key depends on which timezone the reader happens to consult is not a mutex. If UC-CCA-P3 ships alone, this defect survives and the umbrella closes green — the recurring-detection-vs-recurring-FAILED-FIX class (feedback_recurring_detection_vs_recurring_failed_fix).

PO RULING (product decision, po-owned, decided 2026-07-22 — DO NOT re-litigate; architect/ba own the HOW, not the WHAT). The dedup key and the human-readable date label are TWO DIFFERENT VALUES and MUST NOT be derived from one expression. chef.md L654 (CYCLE_DATE = WORK_DATE verbatim) deliberately couples them; that coupling IS the defect, not the fix — it was introduced by GAP-CHEF-SYNTHESIS-A-FLOW-PERSIST to make the FILENAME deterministic and it silently made the MUTEX KEY timezone-dependent. (1) MUTEX KEY = window-anchored and timezone-free: derived from the scheduled cron fire-window expressed in UTC (shape e.g. published:<slot_id>:2026-07-22T19:45Z), NOT from any `date` call made by the executing agent. Two peers executing the same scheduled window MUST derive byte-identical keys with zero shared state beyond the cron expression. This is invariant to timezone, to VN/UTC midnight straddle, to DST, to host clock skew, and to run-start jitter within the window (19:55 vs 20:01). It needs NO trading-calendar lookup. NEVER put a trading-calendar / holiday lookup on the mutex path. (2) DISPLAY LABEL (metadata.date_vn, synthesis filename, prose) = the VN trading session the dish INFORMS. chef-evening fires after the prior VN close (08:00Z) and before the next VN open (02:00Z of D+1) and gates on macroIndicatorRefreshJob US macro data — it is a FORWARD preview; the slot's own dish_type is literally `evening_preview`. Therefore the correct label for a 19:45Z fire is the NEXT VN session = the VN wall date at fire time. Tonight's correct label is 2026-07-23; the 19:55Z run's date_vn=2026-07-22 is WRONG. Weekend/holiday note for ba: the cron is daily including weekends, so 'next VN session' is not the next calendar day on Fri/Sat/Sun fires — the LABEL MAY remain the plain VN wall date (simple, calendar-free); if a true session label is ever wanted it belongs in a SEPARATE display-only field and never in the key.

CAUTION for architect/ba: metadata.cycle_id is NOT a ready-made substitute — today's two runs emitted cycle_id evening-2026-07-22T19:56:00Z and evening-2026-07-22T20:00:37Z, i.e. cycle_id is keyed to RUN-START and diverges exactly like WORK_DATE does. RECOMMENDED PLUMBING (non-binding): the cowork dispatcher ALREADY holds the canonical window value — the fire-election lock cron:cowork:2026-07-22T20:00Z carries payload.tick — so pass the tick DOWN to the spawned agent instead of having the agent re-derive it; DESIGN-COWORK-FANOUT-T1-TICK-SNAPSHOT-WON-SLOTS (tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7, already in ready[]) is the natural carrier. Deriving-at-the-leaf is what created this bug class.

LIVE FORWARD HAZARD (self-healing — do NOT 'fix' it with lock surgery): published:chef-evening:2026-07-23 expires 2026-07-24T00:01:30Z, which is AFTER tomorrow's 2026-07-23T19:45Z fire. If tomorrow's run uses the UTC-date convention it derives :2026-07-23, finds it HELD, and SILENTLY SKIPS — a MISSED evening dish. If it uses the VN convention it derives :2026-07-24 and publishes. Tomorrow's outcome is a coin flip on which convention the spawned agent picks. So this ONE defect produces BOTH double-publish AND missed-publish. Both markers are deliberately LEFT IN PLACE: they are the evidence, and releasing published: markers is the known-wrong direction (feedback_chef_releases_published_marker_enables_peer_double_publish). Hazard self-clears 2026-07-24T00:01:30Z.

AC: (1) two peers spawned for the SAME scheduled window derive byte-identical MARKER_KEY regardless of host timezone, of VN-vs-UTC midnight straddle, and of run-start offset within the window; (2) the key contains NO value obtained from a `date` call made by the executing agent; (3) mutex key and display label are SEPARATE named values with separate derivations, and no later step re-derives either; (4) chef-evening's synthesis date_vn + filename carry the NEXT-VN-session label per the PO ruling above; (5) the fix applies to ALL cowork published: gates (chef-morning/intraday/eod/evening, digest-daily, digest-sunday, fb, market-watcher, news-scout, tnb-audit) — not chef-evening alone; the same straddle hits ANY slot whose UTC fire hour maps across VN midnight, and single-fire slots carry a 100800s TTL that outlives the next window; (6) RAW-verify by executing two same-window runs: exactly ONE claim succeeds, exactly ONE synthesis artifact exists for the window, exactly ONE MARKET post is emitted.

SEQUENCING: ships WITH UC-CCA-P3, not before and not after — lifecycle-without-key-agreement is defeated by divergent keys, key-agreement-without-lifecycle is defeated by leaked or released markers. architect should treat UC-CCA-P3 + this row as ONE design.

RECURRENCE LEDGER (marker-gate cluster): 2026-07-02 x2 (chef-morning + chef-evening, release-after-publish), 07-03 (release-on-no-post remediation -> leak-on-silent-exit), 07-14 (chef-evening dup + date mislabel), 07-15 (MARKET ids 932+933; the dup published a FALSE ~29% index move), 07-16 (chef-eod abort-after-claim false tombstone), 07-17 (chef-eod 2nd false tombstone), 07-22 (THIS — key divergence, NEW root cause). 8th event, 3rd distinct root cause. Recurring-bug-escalation applies (feedback_recurring_bug_escalation): no further point-patches to Step 0.5 until this + UC-CCA-P3 land as one design.

ready.desc:
RECURRENCE 2026-08-06 (PO triage, 3rd+ confirmed instance of this key-derivation class). This row's own 2026-07-22 title predicted today verbatim: "the same defect will FALSELY SUPPRESS the [next day's] 19:45Z dish". It did, 15 days later, while the row sat in BACKLOG.

SEQUENCE (every step RAW-verified, not agent self-report):
(1) 2026-08-05T19:51:57Z the scheduled chef-evening fired (cowork-schedule.json .slots[chef-evening].last_fired) and the session died mid-composition AFTER claiming published:chef-evening:2026-08-05 and BEFORE send_telegram. Router released that marker and re-dispatched a retry at ~19:52Z.
(2) The retry did not begin executing until 2026-08-06T06:34Z. THE 10h42m GAP IS NOT AN AUTH OUTAGE AND NOT A SCHEDULER STALL -- that was the initial triage hypothesis and it is wrong. It is macOS host sleep: `pmset -g log` shows a MAGICWAKE at 2026-08-06 08:34 CEST = 06:34Z, matching the retry's start instant exactly, and the agent's own runtime was only 175909ms (~2m56s). Do not design against a phantom auth/scheduler bug.
(3) On wake, chef.md Step 0.5 recomputed CYCLE_DATE_UTC = `date -u +%Y-%m-%d` = 2026-08-06, so the retry keyed published:chef-evening:2026-08-06 and published a degraded dish to MARKET at 06:37:25Z (msg id 1129, headline "Thi truong 5-6 thang 8"). docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-06-evening.json records quality_verdict="degraded", 0 clusters, gaps [gap:L2_US_macro_absent_no_gap_token] [gap:L3_VN_macro_incomplete] [gap:business_context_unavailable]. It landed 13h before its real 19:45Z window and while the VN session was still OPEN (06:37Z = 13:37 ICT, close is 15:00 ICT) -- an "evening" dish published mid-session.
(4) That marker then tombstoned tonight's legitimate 19:45Z fire (28h TTL, expiry 2026-08-07T10:37:25Z). PO manually released published:chef-evening:2026-08-06 at 2026-08-06T06:53Z to unblock it, RAW-verified absent from task_list_held afterwards. THAT MANUAL RELEASE IS THE THING THIS ROW MUST MAKE UNNECESSARY.

DECISIVE DESIGN INPUT -- THE CORRECT KEY IS ALREADY COMPUTED AND SITTING UNUSED. scripts/agents-flow/cowork-catchup-predicate.js (shipped under TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-1/-2) already emits per slot exactly the fields this row needs: scheduled_utc_time, scheduled_key_part, expected_publish_task_id. Executed live 2026-08-06T06:52Z it returned for chef-evening: scheduled_utc_time=2026-08-05T19:45:00.000Z, expected_publish_task_id=published:chef-evening:2026-08-05 -- i.e. the predicate ALREADY identifies the missed window as 08-05, which is precisely the key the retry should have used and did not. So the fix is not new date logic. It is:
  (a) propagate the nominal scheduled tick into the slot trigger_prompt (e.g. `slot=<id> scheduled_utc=<ISO8601>`), sourced from the values the predicate already produces;
  (b) make chef.md Step 0.5 derive CYCLE_DATE_UTC from that scheduled_utc when present, falling back to wall-clock ONLY for genuine ad-hoc runs. Because CYCLE_DATE_UTC is already the single canonical date-derivation point (chef.md:73 -- pinned once, reused verbatim at Step 7.6 synthesis filepath + metadata.date_vn and Step 8b notebook header), this lands in ONE place and simultaneously fixes the marker key, the synthesis filename and the dish's own date label;
  (c) add a lateness guard: when now - scheduled_utc exceeds the slot's freshness window, the run must publish under an explicit backfill label or abort -- never silently retarget to the current day. The predicate ALREADY implements this notion (catchup_eligible:false with reason "rolled_past_vn_date" / "freshness_window_exceeded"); reuse it, do not reinvent it.

GENERALITY -- DO NOT SCOPE THIS TO CHEF. Every guaranteed slot derives its published-marker key the same wall-clock way, so any delayed, retried or post-sleep execution of digest-daily, tnb-audit, fb-daily, digest-sunday has the identical failure. On this host (laptop, France) sleep is a routine nightly condition, so "execution delayed hours past the nominal tick" is the NORMAL case, not an edge case. Any fix that assumes prompt execution is already wrong.

THE INSTANCE. Notebook size is governed by two caps on the same files. The LINE cap (200) has both a detector and an automatic actuator: scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh is a PostToolUse hook that drops the oldest "## " section in a loop until the file is back under cap. There is no byte actuator anywhere. The pruner's early-exit (:135) and loop-break (:174) are both line-only and it never calls wc -c. Sub-class 5 (instance 10, cold-evict) is a trigger whose ACTION IS INCAPABLE of moving the trigger's input: the trigger counted done rows, the action required count AND age, so n_evict was structurally 0 and the gate was unclearable. Safe-haven demand reflects caution amid margin debt expansion."  -> Fed funds ONLY. NO PMI. NO EFFR-IORB spread. Both are mandatory Layer-2 content per tnb-methodology.md / the main.md Layer table.
- known_gaps = ["[gap:business_context_sparse] ...", "[gap:gold_4300_active] ..."] -> ZERO L2 gap token.
So the dish certifies 6/6 layers walked while its own persisted payload shows Layer 2 is not walked, and emits no gap token to compensate. The quality signal is not merely wrong, it is confidently wrong — downstream consumers that trust quality_verdict to gate use have no way to detect this.

*** CORRECTION TO TNB'S EVIDENCE (PO re-verified; do not carry TNB's version forward) ***
TNB's finding argues the self-scoring gate CAN work by contrasting the SAME-DAY eod dish, which it says "explicitly tokens [gap:L2_US_macro_absent]". That contrast is NOT RAW-verifiable: docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-eod.json DOES NOT EXIST (PO ls-confirmed; TNB's OWN other finding, GAP-CHEF-SYNTHESIS-A-FLOW-PERSIST, states the same file is Glob-confirmed absent). TNB therefore cited the eod NOTEBOOK claim as if it were persisted-JSON evidence, in the same handoff where it correctly reports that JSON never landed — an internal contradiction.
The proof leg SURVIVES, but must be re-anchored to the EVENING dish, which PO verified RAW: unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-evening.json has metadata.quality_verdict="degraded" AND tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer="EFFR-IORB spread 1.64pp NEUTRAL. Brent +2.31% ... Gold +1.97% ..." — i.e. genuine L2 content and an honest verdict, same agent, same day. That is a sound same-day control and it establishes the same point: the defect is isolated to the morning cycle, not universal.
CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS: do not build the fix around a comparison with the eod JSON. It is not there.

OCCURRENCE COUNT = 1 (first live-verified). Below the 3-cycle auto-cure threshold, and PO agrees auto-cure is the WRONG instrument here regardless of count — see the sibling row below.

FIX SHAPE (PO directive): the verdict gate must be a DETERMINISTIC ASSERTION, not a narrative self-judgement. Before writing metadata.quality_verdict="full", the agent must assert per-layer that the layer's own payload field is non-empty AND contains its mandatory tokens (L2: PMI and/or EFFR-IORB). If an assertion fails, "full" is not writable — the verdict must downgrade to "degraded" and a [gap:L<N>_...] token must be appended to known_gaps. Verdict and gap-token must be derived from ONE evaluation so they cannot disagree.

AC: (1) quality_verdict="full" is unwritable when any mandatory layer field lacks its required tokens; (2) verdict and known_gaps are computed from a single pass (no independent second judgement); (3) negative control — a synthetic dish with L2 stripped must produce degraded + an L2 gap token, proving the assertion fires (without this the fix is indistinguishable from always writing degraded); (4) RAW-verify on the next morning fire by reading metadata.quality_verdict + tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer from the persisted JSON — an agent self-report or notebook line is NOT acceptable evidence (the 07-21 morning notebook line matched the false "full" verbatim, so the notebook faithfully reproduces the bad verdict and cannot detect it).

THIS row = no token was ever generated AND the verdict was affirmatively certified "full". Different mechanism, opposite end of the pipeline. ready.title: Every subagent shares ONE git working directory + ONE HEAD: any agent that honours a `branch:` field (e.g. a PM handoff) checks out that branch in the shared checkout, and every concurrent peer's commits silently land on it. 4 independent hits on 2026-07-31 alone; zero board rows existed.
ready.root_cause: STRUCTURAL, not behavioural. There is no worktree/checkout isolation between agents — all agents (router, dev-team, pm, po, developer, architect, agents-architect, qa) operate on the same `$PROJECT_ROOT` and therefore the same `.git/HEAD`. `git checkout <branch>` is a process-global mutation of shared state with no lock, no claim and no TTL, so it is not serialisable against peers the way the index is (the index at least has `index.lock` + the Layer-0 sweep guard). CLAUDE.md's `NO branches — all work stays on main` invariant is the only thing holding the system together, and it is enforced by prose alone: nothing structurally prevents a `branch:` field from appearing in a PM handoff / task row and being obeyed. Note this is the SIBLING hazard to the shared-INDEX sweep (FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD family, 6 rows, Layer-0 hook shipped): same shared-working-dir root, different shared resource (HEAD vs index), and the sweep-guard hook is structurally blind to it because it only inspects $GIT_INDEX_FILE shape, never HEAD.
ready.evidence: dev-team signal `dev-20260731T020908` (signal_queue, status READ, minted by commit 3b20fc8c9): '4x today: subagents share dev-team's git checkout (no worktree isolation); a branch checkout (e.g. PM handoff's branch: field) hijacks peer commits.' ready.ac: (AC-1) Name the enforcement layer and make it STRUCTURAL, not prose. The prose invariant already exists in CLAUDE.md and did not prevent 4 hits — a 5th doc sentence is a rejection. Candidate layers to evaluate explicitly, choosing and justifying one: (a) a `pre-checkout`-equivalent guard (git has no pre-checkout hook — say so if rejecting, do not silently assume one exists) e.g. a wrapper/alias or a `post-checkout` hook that hard-reverts + fail-louds any move off `main`; (b) real per-agent `git worktree` isolation; (c) a schema-level ban on the `branch:` field in task rows / PM handoffs so the trigger can never be authored. po 2026-07-25T16:25:39Z — EVIDENCE FOLDED IN, NO NEW ROW MINTED. This annotation changes what "done" means for this row; read it before implementing.

THIS ROW'S OWN IMPACT ASSESSMENT IS NOW OBSOLETE AND MUST NOT BE ACTED ON AS WRITTEN. The note above says "at the live rate 26110 all three currently agree on direction, which is exactly why this has stayed invisible — the divergence only bites between 25000 and 26500." That framing treats the defect as a LATENT disagreement. It is no longer latent, and the more serious problem is not the disagreement at all.

MEASURED THIS TICK, AT SOURCE: apps/macro-indicators/pkg/primitive/macro_usdvnd_direction_classifier/macro_usdvnd_direction_classifier.go:34 BearishThreshold = 25000.0, line 37 BullishThreshold = 23000.0, so the NEUTRAL band is 23000-25000 and BULLISH requires < 23000. Live rate 26130. The rate has not been under 25000 in a long time and is not trending back. BEARISH IS THEREFORE THE ONLY REACHABLE OUTPUT OF THIS CLASSIFIER — it is SATURATED, not merely divergent. A three-valued direction classifier has silently become a constant that still reports a verdict on every call, and consumers cannot distinguish "the model assessed the rate and found it bearish" from "the model can only say bearish". news-scout emitted "USDVND 26130 bearish >25000 threshold" from it in both c199 and c200 today.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — THE STATED GOAL IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. "Pick one SSOT" does not fix saturation if the value picked is 25000, and 25000 is the most likely pick precisely because it is the one with a named exported constant in Go. Shipping a single-SSOT refactor on 25000 would close this row while leaving the classifier constant — and would additionally propagate the saturated threshold to the two planes (25500 in macroTools.ts / macroAdjustments.ts) that are currently, by accident, slightly less wrong. AC ADDITION, mandatory: whatever value is chosen, add a test asserting that BOTH the bullish and bearish branches remain reachable at the CURRENT live rate, not at a fixture rate. A classifier whose test suite only exercises synthetic inputs cannot detect that its live input has left the discriminating range.

THE DURABLE FIX IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE OF THRESHOLD, AND THAT DECISION BELONGS TO WHOEVER WORKS THIS ROW. A fixed absolute threshold on a drifting nominal exchange rate saturates eventually by construction — this is not a mis-set constant, it is a design that has a shelf life. Honest options: [a] make the threshold relative (z-score or percent deviation against a trailing window, so the discriminating range travels with the series); [b] keep absolute levels but bind them to a real policy anchor (e.g. the SBV reference-rate band) that is itself revised, and add a staleness alarm on the anchor; [c] keep 25000 as a deliberate permanent red-line and DELETE the NEUTRAL/BULLISH branches plus the "direction classifier" framing, so the output honestly reads as a single boolean threshold breach rather than an assessment. What is NOT acceptable is shipping one SSOT and leaving three branches of which two are unreachable. po did not choose among these.

KEY BROWNFIELD FINDING: scripts/orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs (Stage 1.5) ALREADY computes, per row id, `changed = !liveRow || !deepEqual(omit(candidateRow,'updated_at'), omit(liveRow,'updated_at'))` for every row in the candidate (source: flattenRows()/deepEqual()/omitField(), lines ~150-257) — exactly the primitive needed to detect "selector missed its target." Nothing currently consumes that per-id result beyond the stamp-or-not decision. Fix reuses this machinery instead of duplicating it (HARD CONSTRAINT in orch-apply.sh's own header: never duplicate validation logic).

FIX SHAPE — chosen: (a) opt-in per-id companion assertion, env-var-plumbed exactly like the existing ORCH_APPLY_ALLOW_SHRINK / ORCH_APPLY_DECLARED_SIGNAL_EVICTIONS precedent (inherited via subprocess env, zero new orch-apply.sh plumbing). Blind escalation manufactures a false-positive storm on the majority of routine writes, not a targeted fix.
  - (c) jq-transform-string parsing — REJECTED: fragile against arbitrary jq syntax (nested selects, alternate predicates, first()/limit()), reverse-engineers intent from source text instead of trusting a structural caller-supplied fact. Opt-in declarative env var matches the file's own existing idiom.

MECHANISM (scripts/orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs, extend the existing stamping loop — do not add a new script/stage):
1. New env var `ORCH_APPLY_EXPECT_MUTATED_IDS=<comma-separated task ids>` — optional, read directly from process.env (no CLI-arg change, mirrors ORCH_APPLY_ALLOW_SHRINK's "no special plumbing" note).
2. In the existing `for (const [id, candidateRow] of candidateRows)` loop, additionally push `id` into a `changedIds` Set whenever `changed` is true (already computed — one extra Set.add per iteration).
3. After both stamping passes (rows + head), BEFORE `writeFileSync`: if the env var is non-empty, for each declared id check `changedIds.has(id)`. This single predicate unifies all 3 failure shapes with zero extra branching: (i) id present in both live+candidate with identical content [[exact PO incident — row relocated to another lane, content byte-identical]]; (ii) id present in live only [row removed from candidate entirely]; (iii) id present in neither [typo / already-evicted] — none of these ever enter changedIds, since the loop only adds ids where `changed===true`.
4. Any unsatisfied id -> print every failing id to stderr, `process.exit(4)` BEFORE the write (TMP stays at its pre-stamp, already-schema-valid state; orch-apply.sh's cleanup trap removes it since the rename never happens — live file untouched, per the file's own "Live file is SACRED" hard constraint).
5. scripts/orch-apply.sh Stage 1.5 error-handling: one new branch — `stamp_exit -eq 4` -> propagate a NEW distinct exit code 4 (documented in the top-of-file EXIT CODES comment + new ORCH_APPLY_EXPECT_MUTATED_IDS env-var doc block, styled like the existing ORCH_APPLY_ALLOW_SHRINK block) instead of collapsing into the current generic `exit 1`. Rationale for a distinct code: remediation is "re-read live file, recompute filter, retry" — identical to exit 2's CAS-mtime remediation, NOT exit 1's "malformed candidate, retry fails the same way." Lets any retry-wrapper safely auto-retry on {2,4} but never blindly retry on 1.
REGRESSION SAFETY: exit 4 only fires when the new opt-in var is set. None of the ~290 existing orch-apply.sh call sites set it today -> zero behavior change for all of them, verified by design (additive-only code path).

COMPANION FIX — docs/agents/po/flow/main.md AC-3 (explicitly required by the board row): current AC-3 only checks file-PRESENCE in HEAD (`git show --stat $SHA | grep -q orch-state.json`) — provably insufficient, it passed on this exact incident because OTHER rows changed in the same commit. (2) belt-and-suspenders — extend AC-3's post-commit self-verification to re-read the SPECIFIC target row from the just-committed HEAD (`git show $SHA:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json | jq --arg id "$TARGET_ID" '.. | objects | select(.id?==$id)'`) and assert the intended field(s) are actually present, not merely that the file is in HEAD. This generalizes the rule already adopted fleet-wide in docs/protocols/fail-loud-protocol.md's Analysis-Only Exit Guard ("re-read the persistence layer before claiming it — never trust the write call's own exit code") from file-level to row-level.

ready.po_evidence_20260808T1600Z:
MECHANISM, read at source — NOT inferred from the signal prose.

(1) WINDOW LENGTH. scripts/audits/verify-a30-mcp-memory-reclamation.sh:124-125 `PROBES="${1:-12}"` / `INTERVAL="${2:-25}"` => default window 12 x 25s = 300s = 5 minutes. Auditor cycle c373 recorded a 6-sample window (~2.5 min). The ESCALATE branch that actually fired is :326-328 `elif awk "BEGIN{exit !($MINP > 93)}"` -> REASON "all samples >93% sustained high - loss of reclamation". Note the VmHWM branch (:325) did NOT fire — c373 itself records VmHWM 'NOT advancing in window' — so the verdict rests entirely on MINP>93 over that <=5-minute window.

(2) EVENT PERIOD. apps/rag-service/app_factory.py:87 `idle_unload_minutes = getattr(cfg, "embedder_idle_unload_minutes", 15)`; :46 `_IDLE_UNLOAD_CHECK_INTERVAL_S = 60.0`; :108-109 the loop is armed with `idle_threshold_s=idle_unload_minutes * 60.0`. So rag-service's only reclamation event has a MINIMUM period of 15 minutes and is polled once a minute. A <=5-minute window is 3x too short to contain one. Whenever the probe lands in a pre-unload plateau, MINP>93 holds by construction and the verdict is guaranteed ESCALATE regardless of whether reclamation is healthy. The predicate cannot return false for this container — it is not measuring what it claims to measure.

(3) LIVE FALSIFICATION (the OTHER plane, not the auditor's own numbers — feedback_internal_consistency_is_not_corroboration_check_the_other_plane). Auditor c373 sampled rag-service-1 at 94.69% baseline / 6-sample median 94.71% (min 94.69, max 94.71) across 15:34-15:39Z and emitted sys-20260808T153848-7fac WARN 'loss of reclamation, zero reclamation dips'. `docker stats --no-stream` at 15:58Z: vn-market-intelligence-mcp-rag-service-1 = 839.7MiB / 1GiB = 82.00%. 94.69% of 1GiB = 969.6MiB -> 839.7MiB is ~130MiB reclaimed INSIDE the very interval the probe declared reclamation-free. The idle-unload fired; the probe's window simply ended before it could see it.

(4) CONTRAST CONTROL — same probe, same tick, opposite verdict correctness. mcp-server-1 was sampled at 95.29% baseline / median 94.50% (min 94.36, max 94.93) and emitted sys-20260808T153859-7b4c. `docker stats` at 15:58Z: 2.891GiB / 3GiB = 96.37% — HIGHER than every sample, i.e. still climbing. `docker exec ... /proc/1/status`: bun VmRSS=3015024kB (2.875GiB), VmHWM=3034944kB (2.894GiB) — current RSS is sitting AT its own all-time peak. mcp-server has no unload cycle at all, so MINP>93 is a correct TRUE POSITIVE there. This pair is the whole point: the predicate is not wrong, the window is not calibrated to the target. A fix that weakens the threshold would break the mcp-server arm; a fix that lengthens the window uniformly would make every Tier-1 cycle >15 min. The correct shape is a per-container window (or an explicit per-container reclaimer-period declaration) — that is why this is minted as its own row rather than folded into any existing A-30 row.

(5) SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FOUND WHILE VERIFYING (folded elsewhere, NOT minted here): c373 states 'rag-service-1 VmHWM: pinned at cap (1.5GiB)'. `docker inspect vn-market-intelligence-mcp-rag-service-1 --format '{{.HostConfig.Memory}}'` = 1073741824 = 1.0GiB, and the last compose change on this service is 2f835ec63 'raise memory cap 768m->1g'. The live VmHWM is 1568064kB = 1.495GiB — i.e. the notebook reported VmHWM's OWN value as if it were the cap. The SCRIPT is innocent: :262-268 derives MEMLIMIT_KB from the real cgroup limit. This is a prose-transcription fabrication and is folded onto FIX-AUDITOR-VERDICT-TRANSCRIPTION-PROSE-OVERRIDES-MACHINE-VERDICT. Recorded here only because it is the reason the '1.5GiB/1.5GiB pinned at cap' premise in the dispatch brief must not be trusted. Side-observation for the implementer, deliberately NOT adjudicated by PO: VmHWM (1.495GiB) EXCEEDS the live cgroup limit (1.0GiB) with no OOMKilled — worth understanding before writing the per-container calibration, but it is not this row's deliverable.

ready.title: notebook-auto-prune charges the ENTIRE byte-cap overage to dated journal sections: rolling headings (## Archive, ## Known patterns) carry the MAX sentinel key so they can never be the drop candidate, yet they contribute their full bytes to the overage — every breach is paid for by deleting real cycle history while the actual bloat is retained
ready.desc: REPORTED BY ba (signal ba-2026-08-06T18:53:30Z-gateway-blind), 2x reproduced live on docs/agent-memory/notebooks/ba.md during the TE-T05 cycle (section FIX-VNINDEX-CROSS-PLANE-PLAUSIBILITY-GATE dropped twice, once after an Edit, once after a full Write; recovered from git HEAD 8732d0854/2b55a01b1). PO READ THE SCRIPT AND THE REPORTER'S STATED ROOT CAUSE IS WRONG — do not implement against it. ba claimed the hook 'counts ALL ## headings toward its 3-section cap instead of scoping to DATED headings only per notebook-write AC-2a'. There is NO 3-section cap anywhere in scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh: the drop loop is `while true` and breaks the instant BOTH line_count<=LINE_CAP AND byte_count<=BYTE_CAP hold (L389-395). Section count is only consulted for the SECTION_COUNT<=1 safe-fail. The true mechanism is the INVERSE of what was reported: rolling headings are not over-counted as droppable, they are structurally EXEMPT from being dropped while still being fully counted in the byte total.
ready.root_cause: Two independently-correct mechanisms compose into a data-loss ratchet. (1) SELECTION plane: nso_sections_with_ts assigns the 17-char MAX sentinel key ($NSO_SENTINEL_KEY) to any '## ' heading with no parseable timestamp. The drop candidate is always MIN_KEY. So a rolling heading — '## Archive', '## Known patterns / preferences', '## Identity', the exact stable-ROLLING-heading convention .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md itself prescribes — sorts to MAX and can NEVER be the drop candidate as long as one dated section survives. That exemption is deliberate and correct in isolation. (2) MEASUREMENT plane: BYTE_CAP = LINE_CAP * 60 is computed over the WHOLE FILE (L347-352, L387-388), rolling sections included. Compose them and the invariant becomes: 100% of any byte overage is repaid by deleting dated cycle history, 0% by the rolling sections, REGARDLESS of which sections actually hold the bytes. On ba.md the binding axis is bytes, not lines: 45L/10252B against cap 200L/12000B — i.e. it prunes at 22% of the line cap because 2 of its 4 headings are permanently-retained rolling sections. Worse, it is a RATCHET: ba's documented recovery action (re-document the lost content into the Known-patterns section) grows the undroppable share, which makes the NEXT dated section get dropped sooner. Any notebook following the prescribed convention converges to rolling-sections-only.
ready.corroboration: Signal notebook-direction-defaulted-docs-agent-memory-notebooks-ba-md-2026-08-06T185213Z fired on the SAME file the SAME day and is the second half of the proof: ba.md's dated headings are date-only ('## TE-T05 · 2026-08-06', '## UC-CRITIC-HOOKS-ENFORCEMENT · 2026-08-06') so they normalize to an IDENTICAL key and tie; the only non-tied sections are the two sentinels, which nso_vote_direction excludes from the direction vote by construction — so direction is UNRESOLVABLE, DIRECTION_SOURCE=default, and the drop falls to the newest_first default (drop physically-LAST of the tie group). The tiebreak signal was filed action_required=informational_no_action_needed; it is not informational, it is the corroborating half of this row.
ready.fix_spec: Make the two planes agree. Preferred: make the MEASUREMENT plane match the SELECTION plane — compute the cap predicate over the DROPPABLE (non-sentinel) section bytes only, so the pruner stops deleting history to pay for bytes it is structurally forbidden to reclaim, and instead emits an honest signal when the undroppable remainder alone exceeds cap (the same honest-signal contract L400-425 already uses for the single-section case). Alternative: keep whole-file measurement but make rolling sections droppable-of-last-resort once every dated section is exhausted. Either way the rule must be stated in .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md so the prescribed Archive/Known-patterns convention and the pruner stop contradicting each other.
ready.ac: AC-1 REGRESSION (must FAIL before, PASS after): fixture notebook, 3 dated sections + '## Archive' + '## Known patterns', total bytes over cap, where the two rolling sections alone hold MORE than the overage. Current code deletes a dated section and still leaves the file over cap on the next write; fixed code must retain all 3 dated sections and emit the honest over-cap signal instead. AC-2 NEGATIVE (must not regress): fixture whose bloat genuinely IS in the dated sections and whose rolling sections are small — the true-oldest dated section must still be dropped exactly as today. AC-3 RATCHET: replay the same fixture through 3 consecutive over-cap writes; assert the retained dated-section count is non-decreasing (today it strictly decreases to zero). AC-4: no live notebook is written by the test. AC-5 MIXED-CONVENTION INVERSION (new, from occurrence 5 — must FAIL before, PASS after): fixture notebook over the BYTE cap only, containing exactly 2 undated `## Keep (maintenance) 12:58 - ...` headings plus 1 dated `## EDIT <full-ISO> - ...` heading placed LAST/newest. Current code drops the dated EDIT section (verify by asserting the fixture's dated section is ABSENT after a HEAD-version run). Fixed code MUST retain the dated section. Generalize the invariant under test: when the set of non-sentinel ts_keys in a file has cardinality 1 and at least one sentinel section exists, that single dated section MUST NOT be the drop candidate — one real timestamp is not a chronological ordering, it is a sample size of one, and ranking it against MAX-sentinels manufactures a false 'oldest'. review.title: sla-monitor's bctc threshold is NOT a policy constant — it rises 60min/hour in lockstep with the measured staleness, holding a fixed 5439-minute margin. The gate can therefore never clear and never escalates, and the 'threshold' value printed in every CRITICAL alert is meaningless.
review.status_note:
MECHANICALLY PROVEN, not inferred. PO extracted every bctc sla-monitor alert from list_unresolved_reports() over a 21-hour window (2026-07-24T17:00Z -> 2026-07-25T14:00Z, 12 samples) and differenced the two numbers in each message:
  stale=5950 thr=511 | 6010/571 | 6070/631 | 6160/721 | 6250/811 | 6340/901 | 6400/961 | 6550/1111 | 6700/1261 | 6910/1471 | 7090/1651 | 7210/1771
The set of (stale - threshold) values across all 12 samples is EXACTLY {5439}. One element. The threshold is not a duration policy — it is a second clock running 5439 minutes behind the first.

ISOLATED TO bctc, WHICH IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL THAT MAKES THIS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT A GLOBAL MISREADING: in the same alert stream over the same window, every other metric's threshold is CONSTANT — bond_maturity 10080 (7d) in all samples, signal_quality_audit 2880 (48h) in all, news 30, sbv_fx 30. Only the bctc threshold moves. So this is a bctc-specific threshold computation, not a shared formatter bug and not an artifact of how the message is rendered.

HYPOTHESIS FOR THE ROOT CAUSE, stated as a hypothesis and NOT verified at source (PO did not read the sla-monitor implementation — the next agent must): a constant difference between two quantities that both grow with wall-clock time means BOTH are ages measured from `now` against FIXED timestamps, 5439 minutes apart. That is, the code is almost certainly comparing `now - T_data` against `now - T_other` — an AGE-vs-AGE comparison — where a correct SLA compares an AGE against a DURATION. Whoever picks this up should first confirm or refute that shape before changing anything; if it is refuted, the 5439 constant still has to be explained.

OPERATIONAL COST: the bctc breach re-fires roughly hourly and has done so continuously for at least 21 hours (almost certainly far longer — 3 samples/hour of bond_maturity + signal_quality_audit + bctc dominate the 100-row unresolved-report backlog). Because the margin is fixed, the alert carries zero information about whether the situation is improving or worsening: it will print CRITICAL with a larger pair of numbers forever.

review.title: orch-state `blocks` AND `co_edit` are write-only — read by NO script, so any sequencing or atomic-ship guard expressed in them is decorative. PO authored one of each on 2026-07-25 believing both bound; neither did. 7 rows carry `blocks` (1 holds a prose paragraph instead of task ids), 2 rows carry `co_edit`
review.source: dev-team 16:37Z tick caught PO's own decorative guard on FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES; mechanism + full-repo reader grep + 7-row population + positive control independently re-verified at source by po
review.note:
MINTED 2026-07-25T17:00:10Z by po. Surfaced by the dev-team 16:37Z tick, which caught PO's own decorative guard; independently re-verified at source by po before minting. The reporter explicitly declined to mint and left the call to PO.

THE DEFECT. `blocks` reads as a sequencing constraint and binds NOTHING. It is write-only across the entire repo. An author who writes `blocks: ["X"]` on row A, intending "X must not start before A", has created zero enforcement — and, critically, has no way to tell the difference from a working gate by inspecting the board.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, NOT RELAYED:
  - scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq:133-141 — `effective_depends_on` unions ONLY the candidate row's own `.depends_on`, `.depends` and `.blocked_by`; inline first, then backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows. It never traverses a reverse edge from any other row.
  - :161-164 — `deps_satisfied` short-circuits `true` when the effective list is empty.
  - Full grep across scripts/lib/*.jq, scripts/devteam-*.jq, scripts/orch-*.mjs, scripts/orch-*.sh, scripts/agents-flow/*.sh: NO consumer of `blocks`. The only textual matches are unrelated test-assertion prose ("... blocks idle").

LIVE POPULATION — 7 rows carry the field, and the three states are instructive:
  - INERT-BUT-INTENDED (1): FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT -> FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES. This was PO's own guard, written 16:49Z today, believed binding, and it was not. Now repaired by writing the reciprocal `depends_on` inline on the target. THIS IS THE PROOF THE FIELD IS A TRAP: a caller whose entire job is board correctness used it wrongly on the same day, because nothing about it signals that it does not work.
  - ACCIDENTALLY-BINDING (1): RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND -> ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-REBUILD-CRON. This one DOES hold — but not because of the `blocks` edge. The target independently carries `blocked_by: ["ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-CRON-SAFETY-GATE", "RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND"]` and status BLOCKED. Positive control for the correct shape, and evidence that the correct shape is already known and used elsewhere in the same board. Verified at source rather than assumed.
  - MALFORMED (1): FIX-MCP-SUITE-HEALTH-BASELINE's `blocks` value is not a task id or a list of them — it is a prose paragraph beginning "PUSH-AUTONOMY-1. This standing red makes any literal '0 fail on the FULL suite' reading of the push gate permanently unsatisfiable...". A separate data-quality defect that only survives because nothing ever parses the field. It is IN SCOPE for this row: whichever remedy is chosen must not silently swallow a non-list value.
  - EMPTY / harmless (4): TASK_2006, TASK_2005, ALPHA-S2-SUB5-WATCHDOG-STRETCH, ALPHA-S2-FF-SUB6-BUCKETING-HELPER all carry `blocks: []`.

REMEDY — THREE HONEST OPTIONS, po did NOT choose:
  [a] MAKE THE GATE READ THE REVERSE EDGE — extend `effective_depends_on` to also scan every lane for rows whose `blocks` contains the candidate's id. Most faithful to author intent, and fixes all existing writers retroactively. Costs a full-board scan per candidate inside a hot eligibility predicate; measure before adopting.
  [b] MAKE `blocks` AN ALIAS — have scripts/orch-apply.sh mirror `A.blocks: [X]` into `X.blocked_by += [A]` at write time, so the reverse edge is normalised into the forward field the gates already read. Keeps the eligibility predicate untouched and cheap. Needs care: mirroring must be idempotent, must not fight a hand-written `blocked_by`, and must fail loud on a non-list value (see the malformed row above) rather than mirroring garbage.
  [c] DELETE THE FIELD — strip `blocks` from all 7 rows and forbid it, forcing every sequencing intent through `depends_on`/`blocked_by`. Smallest surface, but discards genuinely useful documentation-of-intent and does nothing to stop the next author reaching for an intuitive name.
WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE is leaving a field that reads as a constraint in every board dump while binding nothing. If [c] is chosen, the deletion must be paired with something that makes the mistake loud — see acceptance 3.

SCOPE ITEM DISCOVERED WHILE REPAIRING THE INSTANCE — A SECOND WAY DEP GATES CAN SILENTLY OPEN. scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh defaults `STUB_FIELDS="id,title,priority,size,type,zone,status,sprint,detail_ref"`. `depends_on`, `depends` and `blocked_by` are NOT in the keep-set, so a re-run strips inline deps out of hot rows. That is normally survivable because `effective_depends_on` falls back to backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows — BUT the strip is documented idempotent with "existing cold wins" (docs/policies/dev-standards.md), so a row whose cold entry already carries `depends_on: null` (as FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES does today) would lose the inline value while the stale cold null survives. Net effect: a dependency that was set correctly, later silently unset by an unrelated maintenance migration. Either add the three dep field names to STUB_FIELDS, or make the cold-merge non-clobbering for dep fields specifically. This belongs here because it is the same failure mode by a different route: a gate that is present in the author's mental model and absent from the machine's.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. A sequencing intent expressed the way PO expressed it at 16:49Z (reverse `blocks` edge only, target row otherwise unconstrained) either BINDS or is REJECTED AT WRITE TIME. It must not be silently accepted and ignored.
  2. The existing 7 `blocks`-carrying rows are each dispositioned — migrated, normalised, or deleted — with the malformed FIX-MCP-SUITE-HEALTH-BASELINE prose value handled explicitly rather than crashing or being swallowed.
  3. NEGATIVE CONTROL, and this is the criterion that distinguishes a real fix from a cleanup: after the change, deliberately author a new reverse-only `blocks` guard and demonstrate that it is caught — by binding, by a validation error, or by a loud warning. A remedy that only fixes today's 7 rows leaves the trap armed for the next author.
  4. STUB_FIELDS (or the cold-merge rule) preserves `depends_on`/`depends`/`blocked_by`, verified by running the stub migration over a fixture row carrying an inline dep and asserting the dep still binds afterwards.
  5. Do NOT hand-edit docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json as part of this — 761KB, outside the orch-apply validation gate.

CROSS-REF, NOT A NEW INSTANCE: this is adjacent to SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP (ready/P1) but deliberately NOT filed as an instance there. That row's class is gates whose INPUT cannot cross a threshold; here there is no gate at all — the field simply has no consumer. Filing it there would dilute a class that row has carefully bounded. The transferable lesson does belong in that SPIKE's findings doc as one line, however: A FIELD'S EXISTENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A CONSUMER — when auditing any guard expressed as data, grep for its READER before trusting it.
