Independently re-verified: the script contains ZERO occurrences of any dep field name, and combined with its documented existing-cold-wins merge, a re-run would strip an inline dep from a hot row while a stale cold null survives — silently re-opening a gate that was set correctly. One line, no cold-file surgery. EXPLICITLY REJECTED as the remedy here: hand-editing docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json (761KB, outside the orch-apply validation gate) — the cure is worse than the risk, and it would fix one row rather than the class. po 2026-07-25T17:37Z — SECOND INSTANCE FOLDED IN: `co_edit`. NO NEW ROW MINTED (grep-for-prior-art ruling; the reporter recommended folding and po agrees — this row's scope and its AC 3 negative control extend to it without modification).

THE INSTANCE. On 2026-07-25 at ~17:2xZ po wrote a `co_edit` binding onto BOTH Step 0b sibling rows (FIX-DEVTEAM-BACKGROUND-SPAWN-LOCK-RELEASED-AT-SPAWN-NOT-COMPLETION and FIX-DEVTEAM-STEP0B-RESUME-SUPERVISED-HOLD-GATE), intending "these two must be edited in ONE change to the Step 0b block, because shipping them separately means the second edit races the first." It binds nothing.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY po THIS TICK, WITH A WIDER NET THAN THE REPORT USED. The report grepped `scripts/ apps/` for .jq/.js/.sh/.ts and got 0 files. po re-ran it across the ENTIRE repo with no path or extension restriction (`grep -rl "co_edit" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .`) — 3 files total, and every one of them is a WRITER or a record of a write, never a reader:

  docs/agent-memory/notebooks/po.md   (po's own record of writing it)
  docs/agent-memory/decisions/po-decisions.md (ditto)
Zero code consumers anywhere in the repository. Confirmed independently rather than relayed, and the wider net matters: a scripts/-and-apps/-only grep could have missed a reader in tooling/, .claude/, or a workflow file. It did not — there is none.

WHY THIS BELONGS HERE AND NOT IN A NEW ROW. Identical mechanism, identical failure mode, identical author-trap: a field whose NAME reads as a binding constraint, written in good faith by the agent whose entire job is board correctness, consumed by nothing, and indistinguishable from a working gate by inspecting the board. `blocks` and `co_edit` are the same defect wearing two names. This row's AC 3 — "deliberately author a new reverse-only guard and demonstrate that it is caught, by binding, by a validation error, or by a loud warning" — already covers it verbatim; only the field name changes.

SCOPE ADDITION (small, explicit): whichever remedy this row adopts must dispose of `co_edit` too, and the disposition should be the SAME one chosen for `blocks` — do not fix one and leave the other. Note the asymmetry when choosing: `blocks` has a natural forward-field normalisation target (`blocked_by`/`depends_on`, remedy [b]), whereas `co_edit` has NO existing forward equivalent — there is no "must ship atomically with" primitive in the schema at all. So for `co_edit` the honest menu is narrower: either (i) introduce a real co-edit/atomic-ship primitive that something reads, or (ii) delete the field and force the intent into prose on both rows plus a `depends_on` edge that at least serialises them, or (iii) reject unknown/unread top-level task fields at write time in scripts/orch-apply.sh, which kills this whole class permanently instead of playing whack-a-mole with field names. po's preference, stated as input to ba/architect and NOT as a decision: (iii) is the only option that stops the NEXT invented field, and it is cheap — orch-apply.sh already validates; a known-key allowlist with a loud rejection on unknown keys is a natural extension of the Zod stage. But (iii) has a real migration cost across 658 live rows with many ad-hoc annotation fields (this note's own key included), so it needs measuring before adoption, not assuming.

INTERIM MITIGATION ALREADY APPLIED — DO NOT ASSUME THE BINDING IS UNPROTECTED TODAY. The router, on dispatching FIX-DEVTEAM-BACKGROUND-SPAWN-LOCK-RELEASED-AT-SPAWN-NOT-COMPLETION to architect, passed the co-edit requirement as an explicit MANDATORY instruction in the spawn prompt, including the fact that nothing enforces it. So that specific instance is human-relayed and covered for this dispatch only. It is NOT covered for any future dispatch, re-dispatch, or resume — which is exactly the residual this row exists to close.

TRANSFERABLE LESSON, one line, for this row's eventual findings and for the SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP cross-ref already recorded above: THE COUNT OF DECORATIVE FIELDS IS NOW TWO AND WAS DISCOVERED TWICE IN ONE DAY BY ACCIDENT, BOTH TIMES AUTHORED BY PO. That is evidence the trap is structural and frequently sprung, not a one-off lapse — which raises the value of a class remedy (iii) over per-field cleanup, and is the strongest argument in this row for not settling on remedy [c] (delete-and-forbid) alone.

review.title: apps/pdf-extractor/infrastructure/extraction_engine.py:177-178 swallows an OCR failure (`except Exception: return ""`) and returns the empty string as if extraction had succeeded -- a failed, timed-out, or deadline-aborted OCR page is stored/served as a low-quality SUCCESS, byte-indistinguishable at read time from a genuinely sparse-but-real extraction
review.root_cause: Confirmed unchanged by the concurrency fix. dev-pdf-extractor's own close-out: 'Flagged, explicitly NOT addressed ... extraction_engine.py:177-178's except Exception: return "" still swallows OCR failure into a low-quality-success shape'. qa's independent re-verification: 'Gap-3 ... confirmed unchanged, correctly left open, needs its own row'. The new ocr_gateway.py deadline mechanism (PDFX_OCR_PAGE_TIMEOUT_S) now GUARANTEES a bounded failure on a hung/abandoned OCR call instead of an unbounded hang -- which makes this swallow MORE likely to fire in practice (a deadline exceeded is exactly the kind of exception this catch block converts into a silent empty string) at the same time as it makes hangs rarer. The two changes compose: bounded-failure-more-often + failure-swallowed-into-success is a worse combination than either alone.
acceptance: AC1: an OCR failure (tesseract error, deadline/timeout, capacity-exceeded passed through as an exception) at this call site is NOT returned as a plain empty string masquerading as success -- it is raised, tagged, or otherwise made distinguishable from a legitimate empty/sparse extraction result all the way to whatever stores or serves the page.

AC2: negative control -- a genuinely blank or near-blank scanned page (legitimate sparse text, no OCR failure) is NOT reclassified as a failure by this change; both directions must have a passing test.
AC3: regression floor -- existing extraction_engine.py tests plus the concurrency-fix's own test_ocr_concurrency_invariant.py suite still pass unmodified.
review.scope_out: Do NOT touch the OCR concurrency/gateway mechanism itself (ocr_gateway.py, the semaphore, the deadline) -- that is DONE_VERIFIED on FIX-PDFX-TESSERACT-CONCURRENCY-VIOLATES-SINGLE-WORKER-INVARIANT; this row only changes what happens to the RESULT of a failure at this one call site.

review.title: bctcReparseJob: double-wrap recordJobRun + ungated restart catch-up defeat the T4 cadence guard's evidentiary trail
review.detail: Found during SPIKE-BCTC-REPARSE-CADENCE-GUARD-ROOTCAUSE-VERIFY AC-2 (findings docs/spikes/SPIKE-BCTC-REPARSE-CADENCE-GUARD-ROOTCAUSE-VERIFY.md). runBctcReparseWithDb (apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/startupHelpers.ts:361-366) wraps recordJobRun(db,'bctcReparseJob',fn) where fn discards runBctcReparseJob()'s real ReparseRunResult (Promise<void> arrow fn) -- so cron_job_runs.rows_written is ALWAYS NULL for this job (RAW-confirmed live: 100% of ~90 sampled rows across 11 days, 2026-07-29). Worse: recordJobRun marks the row 'success' whenever fn() resolves without throwing, REGARDLESS of whether runBctcReparseJob()'s OWN shouldSkipRecoveryReplay guard (bctcReparseJob.ts:718) early-returned a no-op -- so a guard-SKIPPED invocation still writes a fresh 'success' row, silently re-arming its own 21.6h dedup window. This is the SAME double-wrap class already found+fixed for runBaseRateComputationWithDb (FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD, 2026-07-23) and runEvidenceAccumulatorWithDb (EVIDENCE-ACCUM-SILENT-CRON) -- bctcReparseJob was never patched. It uniquely compounds with a SECOND defect: the startup catch-up in startScheduler.ts:169-182 fires runBctcReparseWithDb(db) UNCONDITIONALLY 30s after every container boot/restart with NO staleness gate -- its own introducing commit (75b729183, 2026-04-12) claimed to mirror runDailyAuditIfStale's pattern (dataAuditJob.ts:292-311, which correctly checks last_daily_audit_at age before running) but never implemented an equivalent check. Net effect, RAW-confirmed live (docker exec, market.db, last 30 days): 2-7 cron_job_runs rows per calendar day for bctcReparseJob (vs. the intended 1x/day), overwhelmingly 0-3ms duration (guard-skip echoes) with occasional real multi-hour runs, plus status='crashed' zombie rows on restart-cluster days (2026-07-19, 2026-07-28) -- the table's 'last success' signal is contaminated by boot-time noise unrelated to real reparse activity, and is the best-supported explanation for the 2026-07-10 incident this SPIKE investigated (ops' pre-edit probe showed clean, then a subsequent restart re-armed the guard within 30s, before ops resorted to falsifying 25 rows instead of using the job's own nowMsFn override).
review.ac: (1) runBctcReparseWithDb gains its own shouldSkipRecoveryReplay(db,'bctcReparseJob',DAILY_CADENCE_MS) check BEFORE calling recordJobRun (mirrors the FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD fix pattern exactly) so a guard-skip never reaches recordJobRun and never writes a fresh row. (2) fn's default implementation captures runBctcReparseJob()'s real ReparseRunResult and maps resolved+failed to rowsWritten (or an equivalent field) so cron_job_runs.rows_written is no longer always NULL for this job. (3) startScheduler.ts's bctcReparseJob startup catch-up (currently unconditional, :169-182) gains a staleness gate consistent with its own stated intent to mirror runDailyAuditIfStale -- either reuse shouldRunCatchup() (matching the other 5 hardened catchups in the same file) or an equivalent last-run-age check, so a restart does not unconditionally fire the job every single boot. (4) new unit tests proving both fixes through the real default code paths (mirror FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD.test.ts's approach) -- specifically a test that 2 back-to-back invocations within the cadence window produce exactly 1 cron_job_runs row, not 2. (5) RAW-verify post-fix: cron_job_runs rows-per-day for bctcReparseJob drops to <=1 on days without a genuine multi-file reparse, and rows_written is populated (non-NULL) on real runs.

review.detail:
PO triage 2026-07-30T19:07Z (report-queue pass). NOT a false-positive — the alarm was sanity-checked first and PASSED three independent ways: (a) 40 alert samples spanning 2026-07-28T16:00Z..07-30T19:30Z back out to ONE fixed epoch, 2026-06-05T20:13Z, agreeing to within 6 seconds between the oldest and newest sample — a broken baseline drifts, this one is a fixed anchor with a monotonic clock; (b) the threshold is CONSTANT across every sample (2880, then 43200 after the fix landed 07-30T09:00Z), unlike the known-broken sibling metric FIX-SLA-BCTC-THRESHOLD-TRACKS-STALENESS-NOT-CONSTANT where (stale - threshold) was a fixed 5439 constant proving an age-vs-age comparison — here the margin grows, so the comparison is well-formed; (c) dev-mcp-server independently queried the live named-volume market.db for the sibling row and reported 'zero rows since 2026-06-05T20:12:12Z', matching the arithmetic to the minute by a different method.

WHY IT IS DEAD, read at source (not inferred). The table's only writer is insertSignalQualityAudit() (infrastructure/db/signalQualityAuditStore.ts), reached from exactly one call site: post_agent_signal's handler at interface/mcp/tools/news-analysis/agentSignalTools.ts:455-500. Three preconditions must ALL hold: (1) the signal was not dedup-suppressed — note the `if (id <= 0) { ... return }` early-return sits ABOVE the audit block, so every dedup-suppressed post skips the audit silently; (2) signal_type is price_confirmation or urgent_news; (3) typeof finding_data.confidence === 'number'.

The suspected structural break is (3) against the emitter contract. domain/signals/signalTypes.ts makes confidence REQUIRED for price_confirmation (:159 z.number().min(0).max(1)) but OPTIONAL for urgent_news (:217 .optional()), and docs/agents/tools/package/news-scout.md:66 documents urgent_news's required finding_data as headline/source/severity — confidence is NOT in the documented required set. So a fully-compliant news-scout urgent_news post never trips the audit write. docs/agents/tools/list/get_signal_effectiveness.md shows urgent_news at 58 recorded signals; the audit table has 6 rows LIFETIME. price_confirmation, the one type that does mandate confidence, does not appear in that effectiveness sample at all.

BOTH failure modes are silent by construction: agentSignalTools.ts:499 catches and console.warn's ('non-fatal'), and signalQualityAuditStore.ts:78 catches and console.warn's again. Two swallow layers, no counter, no alarm. The SLA monitor is the only thing that ever noticed.

WHY THIS IS NOT ALREADY OWNED — checked both adjacent rows, neither covers it: FIX-SLA-SIGNALQUALITYAUDIT-MONTHLY-CADENCE-MISCLASSIFIED-48H (REVIEW/qa) is a threshold change and its own freshnessSlaChecker.ts:209-211 comment states the current gap 'still fires under the new value' BY DESIGN; FIX-MONTHLYSIGNALQUALITYAUDITJOB-MISSED-JULY-RECOVER-GUARD (BACKLOG/P3) is about monthlySignalQualityAuditJob, which orch-state's own note at :10859 says verbatim 'never writes to the signal_quality_audit table'. So the sign-off path currently closes both neighbours while the condition persists.

OPERATIONAL COST: 39 of the 179 unresolved Telegram reports PO cleared this tick (22%) were this one alarm, arriving ~1/hour. It is the single largest cluster in the queue and it regenerates unboundedly.

CAUTION for whoever picks this up — the 30d threshold in freshnessSlaChecker.ts was sized off '6 rows total ... real gaps of >2 weeks between them even in a healthy period'. If the capability never worked, there was no healthy period and those 6 samples are noise, not a cadence. review.title: 80-page OCR cap vs 50%-completeness threshold: 3 large PDFs never finish extraction, full re-OCR every boot
review.source: architect review of FU-OCR-BOOT-LOOP-SEQUENTIAL, live-measured 2026-07-31 on vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1
review.desc:
pdfOcrWorker.ts:extractAndStorePdfPages hard-caps OCR at 80 pages (line ~261, maxPages = Math.min(totalPages, 80)) but the completeness re-extraction gate (line ~217-219, threshold = Math.max(expectedPages * 0.5, 3)) checks the CAPPED extracted-page count against the UNCAPPED expected page count. For any PDF with totalPages > 160, 80 < threshold forever — the extraction is judged perpetually incomplete, DELETED (db.run "DELETE FROM pdf_extracted_text WHERE filename = ?") and re-OCR'd from scratch, capped at 80 again, on EVERY call — i.e. every single composition-root bootstrap OCR loop run (composition-root.ts §4b), forever, with zero possibility of ever satisfying the threshold.
LIVE CONFIRMED on vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1, 2 consecutive boots (2026-07-30T22:07:03Z, 2026-07-31T00:56:46Z), identical shape both times: GVR_2026_Q1.pdf (totalPages=204, extracted pinned at 80, threshold=102), GVR_2025_Q4.pdf (totalPages=285, extracted pinned at 80, threshold=142.5), 000000013535084_20240328__MSN__Bao_cao_thuong_nien_2023compressedsigned.pdf (totalPages=255, extracted pinned at 80, threshold=127.5) — DB query (bun:sqlite against /app/data/market.db) confirms all 3 sit at exactly c=80 rows, never advancing across boots. Each re-OCR burns ~10-12 real minutes of sequential tesseract CPU (bracketed via consecutive "[pdfOcr] starting" log timestamps) on every boot; combined they are the dominant driver of the ~33min (22:07:03Z -> 22:40:10Z) bootstrap-OCR wall-time observed despite 271/279 other PDFs being fast-skip cache hits.
WORSE than pure waste: the DELETE happens BEFORE re-extraction, so any concurrent read_bctc_pdf / getCachedPdfText call against these 3 filenames during the ~10-12min re-OCR window sees ZERO cached pages (previously-available 80 pages deleted, new 80 not yet reinserted) instead of the stale-but-present partial text — a real availability regression window on every single boot, not merely CPU waste.
Found during architect review of FU-OCR-BOOT-LOOP-SEQUENTIAL (sequential-vs-parallel bootstrap loop question); root cause is unrelated to that question and would reproduce identically whether the loop is sequential or parallel.

AC1: for any PDF whose true page count exceeds the 80-page OCR cap, the completeness gate must not judge the capped result as permanently incomplete — e.g. compute threshold against Math.min(expectedPages, 80) instead of raw expectedPages (or another design the implementer justifies), so a full 80-page capped extraction reaches a terminal cached state and is never re-attempted.
AC2: fix must not create a delete-before-reinsert availability gap for the 3 already-affected files on the FIRST post-fix boot (e.g. write new pages before deleting stale ones, or UPSERT per-page rather than blanket DELETE-then-loop).
AC3: regression test reproducing the live defect (synthetic fixture, expectedPages > 160, cap = 80) — assert a SECOND extraction call does not re-trigger "[pdfOcr] starting" / does not re-DELETE existing rows. Falsification: run the test against unfixed code first, paste RED output before the fix.
AC4: verify live against the 3 named files (GVR_2026_Q1.pdf, GVR_2025_Q4.pdf, 000000013535084_20240328__MSN__Bao_cao_thuong_nien_2023compressedsigned.pdf) on the next mcp-server restart — confirm pdf_extracted_text row count for each stabilizes and the 2nd boot after the fix skips full OCR for all three (only "[pdfOcr] already extracted" fast-path fires).

review.title: [BCTC-1345b] alert hard-codes 'Check for OCR corruption (VNM/VEA pattern: assets<equity or margin>100%)' but financial=0.10 is emitted ONLY by the unit-mismatch short-circuit that bypasses those rules entirely — 65 live rows (23 tickers) each send the triager to a rule family that provably cannot return 0.10
review.source: telegram_reports id=4273 (from_agent=analysis-agent, 2026-08-01T05:52:16Z, NVL 2026-Q2 composite=0.10 financial=0.10)
review.desc:
MEASURED, not inferred.

ROOT CAUSE. parseBctcReport.ts:737-741 computes confidence_financial as a ternary: when detectUnitMismatch(totalAssets, netRevenue) (cross-statement, >1000x) OR detectBsIntraStmtUnitMismatch(totalAssets, totalLiabilities) (intra-BS, >100x) fires, it SHORT-CIRCUITS to the literal 0.1 and validateFinancialFigures() is never called. The alert built at parseBctcReport.ts:275-279 then tells the reader to check the VNM/VEA patterns -- but those are BCTC-VAL-01 (assets<equity) and BCTC-VAL-03 (margin>100%), both implemented INSIDE the validateFinancialFigures() call that was just skipped.

PROOF THE HINT IS UNREACHABLE FOR THIS VALUE. Brute-forced validateFinancialFigures over 160,000 input combinations (totalAssets/totalEquity/totalLiabilities/netRevenue x 10 values each, operatingMargin x 16): the ONLY outputs it can ever return are {0, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0}. It returns 0.1 ZERO times. Documented VNM pattern (assets 957 << equity 18829, revenue 63645) -> 0.8; same without the >30x-revenue escape -> 0.0; documented VEA pattern (margin 3.3 = 330%) -> 0.8. None is 0.10. Therefore financial=0.10 is a UNIQUE, unambiguous fingerprint of the unit-mismatch branch and NEVER of the two patterns the alert names.

SECOND DEFECT -- DEAD FLOOR. financialFiguresValidator.ts:306 'return Math.max(confidence, 0.1)' and its docstrings at :28 and :177 ('soft violations stack, floor at 0.1') describe a floor that cannot be reached: max stacked soft penalty is 0.6, because BCTC-VAL-01's guard requires totalEquity>0 while BCTC-VAL-06 requires totalEquity<0, so those two can never both fire. Minimum non-hard-fail output is 0.4. The 0.1 in the docstring is what makes the collision with the unit-mismatch sentinel invisible on reading.

LIVE BLAST RADIUS (market.db via runtime container, 2026-08-01T06:2xZ). confidence_financial distribution over 221 non-null rows: 1.0 -> 121, 0.1 -> 65, 0.8 -> 18, 0.0 -> 17. Note 0.4 and 0.6 have ZERO rows, and 0.1 is the 2nd most common value at 29.4%. All 65 came through the unit-mismatch branch (independently corroborates the brute-force). 23 distinct tickers. Sub-detector split over those 65: cross-statement only 44, intra-BS only 11, both 7, neither-now 3.

TRIGGERING INSTANCE. NVL 2026-Q2, parsed_at 2026-08-01T05:52:14.418Z: total_assets=420322071420, total_liabilities=0, equity_total=0, net_revenue=31, extraction_confidence=0.375, confidence_financial=0.1, validation_status=low_confidence. assets/revenue ratio = 1.4e10 -> detectUnitMismatch fires (raw VND vs trieu VND). assets>equity, so the VNM signature the alert names is ABSENT; the VEA margin rule was never evaluated. Contained at serve time only INCIDENTALLY: get_bctc_full returns 'Chua co du lieu BCTC' via PUB-1 (refine_status=PENDING, not DONE/PARTIAL) -- NOT via any corruption guard. checkBctcIdentityGuard's predicate (total_assets<=0 OR total_assets<equity_total) passes this row, since equity_total=0 makes assets>=equity trivially true.

AC-1: the [BCTC-1345b] message must name the detector that ACTUALLY fired -- cross-statement unit mismatch (assets/revenue ratio R), intra-BS unit mismatch (assets/liabilities ratio R), or the specific BCTC-VAL-NN rule -- with the offending figures. No hard-coded ticker-pattern hint.
AC-2: the VNM/VEA hint may only appear on values that rule family can actually return (0.0/0.8).
AC-3: resolve financialFiguresValidator.ts:306. Either delete the unreachable floor and correct the :28/:177 docstrings, or keep it and move the unit-mismatch sentinel off 0.1 so the two stop colliding. Do NOT silently leave both.
AC-4: regression test asserting the unit-mismatch alert text does NOT contain the VNM/VEA string, and that a genuine BCTC-VAL-01/03 alert does.
AC-5: NON-GOAL -- this row does NOT fix the underlying unit normalisation (no open row owns that; the 2026-06-07 commit 06c65978c added the DETECTOR only) and does NOT repair the 65 existing rows. Scope is alert truthfulness + the dead floor.

PRIOR ART CHECKED. FIX-BCTC-1345B-REPORT-BATCH (review[], next_agent=qa) touches the same emission block but is about VOLUME/dedup, not text correctness -- its verdict must not be read as making this alert accurate. FIX-BCTC-VALIDATION-GATE-NONBANK-ZERO-SCALE (backlog, architect) is the serve-time validation_status label, not the alert. SPIKE-BCTC-CONVICTION-COMPOSITE-DRAG-PERFECT-FINANCIAL is the inverse case (financial=1.00 dragged by extraction). 48 open BCTC rows scanned; none covers this.

FOUR FIRES IN ~50 MINUTES, previously untracked (no board row matched AUDIT-OUTPUT-CONTRACT or SIGNAL-QUEUE-ROWS-WRITTEN in any lane):

  4415 06:52:40Z  marker-parsed=2, independent re-read=1
  4420 07:42:17Z  marker-parsed=1, independent re-read=2   <- re-read HIGHER than marker
Recurrence is established (4 fires, 2 audit cycles), so this is past the single-fire observation threshold.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN AN OBSERVATION: the mismatch runs in BOTH directions. 4412 and 4415 have the marker above the re-read; 4420 has the re-read above the marker. The emitted resolution — "Trusting the higher (real-artifact) value" — is therefore not a conservative fallback, it is arbitrary: it picks a different source on different cycles, so the number the auditor finally reports is not attributable to any one plane. An agent self-report whose reconciliation rule is direction-dependent is exactly the class flagged in feedback_agent_selfreport_metalayer_confabulation, and it is being used to attest that signal rows were written.

LIKELY BENIGN EXPLANATION TO RULE OUT FIRST (cheap, do this before any code change): .signal_queue.rows[] is a live hot structure that peer agents write to concurrently, so a marker parsed at time T and a re-read at time T+delta can legitimately differ if another agent appended or if a drain removed rows in between. If that is the whole story the fix is to snapshot once and compare within the snapshot, not to pick the larger number. Confirm or refute by timestamping both reads.

TWO INDEPENDENT STRUCTURAL BUGS, one per direction, both inside scripts/audit-output-contract.sh's V1 check (line 194-216):
BUG A (explains 4412/4415, marker HIGHER): every tier's FIRE_TICK (main.md Step 0d, lines 140/147/152/165) is minute-precision ("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"); every signal_queue row .ts (emit-audit-signal.sh:529) is second-precision ("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"). V1's raw jq string ".ts >= $cycle_start_ts" silently drops any row written in the SAME clock-minute as the tick (":" 0x3A sorts below "Z" 0x5A right after HH:MM) — the common case since Tier-2's wall-time target is <300s. Confirmed empirically: jq -n '"2026-08-05T06:00:03Z" >= "2026-08-05T06:00Z"' => false. NOT a new defect class: emit-audit-signal.sh::_ledger_prune_and_lookup() (lines 472-478) already carries a `to_epoch` helper solving this exact minute-vs-second mismatch for the dedup ledger; audit-output-contract.sh's V1 check never adopted it. BUG B (explains 4420, independent HIGHER): zero call sites (grep-confirmed, all 6 emit-audit-signal.sh sites + tier1-probe.md's 2) ever pass --from-agent — every tier/session shares the identical default FROM_AGENT="system-auditor". V1's independent query `.from==$from and .ts>=$ts` therefore counts ANY row from ANY concurrently-running tier/session sharing that string within the window, not just what THIS cycle's own $MARKERS_FILE recorded. Tier-1 fires far more frequently than Tier-2/3/5 so cross-tier overlap during a longer cycle is routine. Reproduced: a cycle whose own markers file lists exactly 1 verified row, cross-checked against an orch-state containing that row plus one UNRELATED row sharing from="system-auditor", falsely inflates the FINAL reported signal_queue_rows_written from 1 to 2 — silently crediting the cycle with a write it never made. RECONCILIATION RULE VERDICT (answers AC-2): JUSTIFY "trust the higher value", do not replace it with a direction-locked rule. Once both bugs are fixed, the only remaining legitimate divergence sources both genuinely favor the higher operand: independent<marker means a verified write was drained/pruned after this cycle wrote it (cannot un-write a real append — marker, already the write-time read-back-verified value, correctly wins, no code-path change needed there); independent>marker (now exact-cycle-tag-scoped, so no longer explainable by cross-tier collision) means this cycle's OWN markers file is missing a row that legitimately carries its tag (dropped marker line / bypassed-script write) — real self-report undercount, the scoped ground truth correctly wins. review.title: Foreign-flow pipeline outage renders NO bulletin section at all — the canonical "Du lieu khong kha dung (pipeline tam dung)" copy sits behind a branch the production SQL can never reach
review.root_cause: Verified at CODE level, not from comments. assembleEveningSummary.ts:571-580 selects foreign flow with `WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM daily_ohlcv) AND foreign_net_vol IS NOT NULL AND foreign_net_vol <> 0`. Zero rows is therefore the ONLY shape a real outage (or a genuine all-zero session) can produce — and the surrounding try/catch also leaves foreignFlowMovers=[] on any DB error. foreignFlowSection.ts:21 answers that shape with `if (movers.length === 0) return []`, and eveningSummaryJob.ts:191 splats the result unguarded (`lines.push(...formatForeignFlowSection(...))`), so the entire "Khoi ngoai" section vanishes silently with no notice. The canonical unavailable copy lives one branch lower, at foreignFlowSection.ts:26-29, gated on movers.length > 0 AND every entry netVol === 0 — a set the `<> 0` SQL predicate cannot emit. franceSummaryJob.ts:434 is worse: it wraps the call in `if (foreignFlowMovers.length > 0)`, so even a future empty-path message would be suppressed there. INVERTS THE CLOSED ROW'S RESIDUAL FLAG: FIX-FOREIGN-FLOW-BULLETIN-UNAVAIL-STRING's router_note worried the unavailable copy could MISLABEL a genuine zero-net-flow day as an outage. Reading the query shows the opposite is what actually ships — a genuine outage is labelled as nothing at all, and the misleading branch is unreachable. LIVE CORROBORATION, not hypothetical: the board's own user-escalated FFLOW-STALE-0723-A-VPS-FIX records foreign flow stalled 2026-07-21 to 2026-07-23 (Vinahost VPS suspended). Throughout that window every evening bulletin would have omitted the section in silence rather than saying the pipeline was down.
review.fix_spec: Make the empty case the one that speaks. Emit the canonical "Khoi ngoai: Du lieu khong kha dung (pipeline tam dung)" line on movers.length === 0, and drop or invert the unreachable all-zero branch (keep it only if a caller can still supply raw unfiltered rows via the injected getForeignFlowMoversFn path — decide from the call sites, do not guess). Remove the redundant `foreignFlowMovers.length > 0` outer guard at franceSummaryJob.ts:434 so both jobs share one policy. DISTINGUISH THE TWO CAUSES IF CHEAP: pipeline stale/absent vs. a real all-flat session are different user messages; if the freshness of daily_foreign_flow is already available at the call site, say which one it is rather than asserting "pipeline tam dung" unconditionally — asserting an infra cause from a data-shape observation is the same misattribution class this row exists to fix. review.note:
MINTED 2026-07-25T16:25:39Z by po (router triage input, RAW-verified at source by po before minting — every number below was measured this tick, none relayed).

THE DEFECT IS NOT INACCURATE BOOKKEEPING — IT IS A TRIGGER THE WRITER MAKES UNSATISFIABLE.
Read contract, docs/agents/news-scout/flow/stage-sentiment.md:16-21 — STALE_TICKERS = watchlist tickers where last_covered_news_scout == null OR (now - last_covered) > 48h, sorted oldest-first, take <=3 per cycle. Write contract, docs/agents/news-scout/flow/stage-log-notify.md:62-63 — "for each ticker analyzed this cycle (both event-driven AND sweep-forced): set .tickers[t].last_covered_news_scout = now". The write contract is CORRECT AS WRITTEN. The execution is not: every cycle stamps ALL tickers, so no ticker can ever age past 48h, STALE_TICKERS is permanently empty, and the <=3-per-cycle rotation can never fire. The sweep is the only mechanism guaranteeing periodic coverage of low-news watchlist tickers; it has been the equivalent of disabled.

MEASURED (docs/data/coverage-state.json, .tickers has 57 entries):
  - after the 16:14Z tick: all 57 carry the byte-identical stamp 2026-07-25T16:14:39Z (jq group_by -> ONE group, n=57).
  - previous committed version: all 57 carry the byte-identical stamp 2026-07-25T12:10:42Z (ONE group, n=57).
  - the 16:14Z cycle (c200) analyzed 2 tickers by its own evidence trail: fragments #584 VNM and #585 MARKET. Not 57.
  - COVERAGE COST, the reason this is P1: ~2 of 57 tickers get event-driven coverage per cycle. The other ~55 are reachable ONLY via the sweep. With the sweep alive (<=3/cycle, ~6 cycles/day) full rotation completes in ~3.2 days; with it dead the long tail gets zero scheduled coverage indefinitely.

SCOPE IS DOUBLE WHAT THE INPUT REPORTED — MARKET-WATCHER HAS THE IDENTICAL DEFECT, LIVE.
The triage input named only news-scout. po checked the sibling field in the same file and it is equally saturated: all 57 tickers carry byte-identical last_covered_market_watcher = 2026-07-25T08:10:06Z. market-watcher's flow carries the same pair of contracts in the same shape — read at docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/cycle.md:60-73, write at :240-250 ("for each ticker priced this cycle (both anomaly-driven AND sweep-forced)"). Any fix that touches only news-scout leaves half the defect live. BOTH agents are in scope; this is stated here because a narrow reading of the originating report would miss it.

THE BEHAVIOUR IS INTERMITTENT, NOT A CLEAN REGRESSION — DO NOT CHASE A BREAKING COMMIT.
po walked 25 historical revisions of the file. Distinct-stamp counts for last_covered_news_scout: 3/4/7 on 06-30, then 1 across 07-02..07-21, then 5 at 819fff993 (07-23, correct shape: a 38-ticker fossil group at 07-21T16:14 plus small 2/2/4/11 groups from later cycles), then 1/1 on 07-25. last_covered_market_watcher: 8,9,10,10,10,6,7,11 through 07-23, then 1,1 on 07-25. So BOTH agents have produced correct per-ticker stamping at some points and blanket stamping at others, with no code change in between. THAT IS THE ROOT CAUSE AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: the write is a prose instruction executed by an LLM against a 57-entry JSON blob, so faithfulness is non-deterministic per cycle. Editing the prose to say it more emphatically is NOT a fix — the prose is already correct. The fix must move the write to a deterministic scripted surgical patch.

INDEPENDENT PROOF THE WRITE IS A FULL-DOC OVERWRITE, NOT A MERGE — A TOP-LEVEL CONFIG KEY WAS SILENTLY DELETED.
coverage-state.json had a top-level sweep_config block ({max_staleness_hours: 48, sweep_batch_size: 3}) — present at 0866c35b6 (2026-07-21), ABSENT from 819fff993 (2026-07-23) onward, and absent live today. Nothing deleted it deliberately; a hand-rewrite of the blob dropped it. Corroborated by docs/handoffs/2026-07-16-coverage-state-cross-agent-lost-update-and-three-premise-corrections.md:16, which enumerates the then-current top-level keys including sweep_config, and by docs/data/.trash/2026-07-20/docs/archive/coverage-state.json.tmp:67 which still carries it. CONSEQUENCE, fold into this fix: BOTH flow docs still cite "sweep_config.sweep_batch_size" (stage-sentiment.md:21, cycle.md:73) against a key that no longer exists — a dangling config reference. It is currently harmless only because the prose also hardcodes "<=3" next to it, and max_staleness_hours=48 now survives solely as prose in two files. Restore the block (or relocate the two constants to a real config surface) as part of this row; do NOT mint a separate row for it.

CO-SHIP — THIS ROW AND FIX-COVERAGE-STATE-CROSS-AGENT-LOST-UPDATE ARE ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO.
That row (backlog/P2/M/plan_only, minted 2026-07-16) records the same file being clobbered on the _ssot blob across agents, and its candidate direction (i) reads "serialize the two writers behind a shared coverage-state write helper that does read-modify-merge (not full-doc overwrite)". This row is direct corroboration that (i) is correct and that the live write IS a full-doc overwrite — the vanished sweep_config key is the proof that row was missing. One helper satisfies both ACs; shipping them separately means editing the same write step in the same two flow files twice, with the second edit racing the first. Sequence: this row leads (P1, live coverage loss), the lost-update row closes with it and its AC 1 becomes AC 3 below.

ROUTED DIRECT TO developer, NOT ba, DELIBERATELY. The sibling row was minted plan_only/next_agent=ba on 2026-07-16 because its direction was genuinely open between three candidates. That question is now CLOSED by the sweep_config deletion evidence above, which is the discriminating observation that row lacked. What remains is one shell script, its test, and two flow-doc edits against a fully specified AC — that is a direct FIX, and holding a P1 live-coverage-loss behind a planning hop for a settled design would be disproportionate. The implementer MUST NOT re-open the direction; if implementation reveals the direction is wrong after all, bounce the row back to po with the contradicting evidence rather than re-scoping in place.

REMEDY SHAPE (direction settled, details open to ba/architect):
Replace the prose read-modify-write in BOTH flow files with one deterministic script — proposed scripts/agents-flow/coverage-stamp.sh, invoked as `coverage-stamp.sh --agent <news-scout|market-watcher> --tickers VNM,FPT` — that does a surgical jq patch of ONLY the named tickers, preserves every other key byte-for-byte, and holds a short mutex (task_claim "coverage-state:main", TTL ~30s) around the read-modify-write. This is exactly the shape already proposed and left unbuilt as cowork-cycle-agents-P10 in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-12-ultracode-workflow-improvement-audit.md:982-986 — that proposal is UNVERIFIED-status there and is hereby superseded by this row, which carries the live evidence it lacked. Genuinely open for the implementer, and the only open question on this row: whether the script also emits the STALE_TICKERS list (so the read side becomes deterministic too, closing the same class on the read path) or only owns the write.

ACCEPTANCE (biconditional — a one-directional test cannot distinguish this fix from the current behaviour):
  1. POSITIVE: after a cycle that analyses N tickers, EXACTLY those N carry the new stamp; `jq '[.tickers|to_entries[]|.value.last_covered_news_scout]|group_by(.)|length'` returns > 1 whenever N < 57. Same assertion for last_covered_market_watcher.
  2. NEGATIVE (this is the one that actually proves the trigger is alive): seed a ticker with a stamp older than 48h, run a cycle, and assert it appears in STALE_TICKERS and is force-included. A test that only checks "the right tickers got stamped" passes today for a 57-ticker cycle and proves nothing.
  3. PRESERVATION: after the write, every top-level key present before the write is still present (regression test for the sweep_config deletion class) and the peer agent's last_covered_* field is unchanged (this is the lost-update row's AC 1).
  4. Both agents covered. A fix landing on news-scout only does not close this row.

SECONDARY OBSERVATION, ONE LINE FOR WHOEVER WORKS THIS — DO NOT EXPAND SCOPE: three unreconciled ticker counts. coverage-state.json has 57 entries; news-scout's c200 notebook asserts "all 58 watchlist sweep"; docs/data/system-map.json's watchlist node has 34. The sweep iterates WATCHLIST (from the get_watchlist tool) but stamps and reads the FILE, so a ticker present in one and not the other is either never swept or never stamped. po did NOT determine which count is authoritative — flag it in the fix's findings, do not silently pick one.

review.title: news-chain BCTC fallback writes an all-zeros balance sheet into financial_reports — the authoritative table — where it is byte-indistinguishable from OCR corruption at serve time; decide whether it should write there AT ALL before guarding arm (b2)
review.origin: QA found this sibling writer while approving arm (b2) on parseBctcReport.ts::storeReport(), and explicitly DECLINED to mint or to expand that row (correctly — PO had a scope-hold on it). Router sharpened the finding at source and also declined to mint. Minting is PO's; this is that mint.
review.mechanism: newsChainFallback.ts (apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/newsChainFallback.ts) is a SECOND, independently-implemented writer to the same financial_reports (action_code, sort_key) row as storeReport(). It already has arm (b1): lines 264-274 block the write when existingReportRow.total_assets > 0, preserving a previously-good row and logging BLOCKED. What it LACKS is arm (b2): with NO prior row it proceeds to INSERT a brand-new row whose totalAssets is a hardcoded 0 (line 307, bound into the INSERT at line 535), inside an entire all-zeros balance sheet at lines 304-313. Identical defect shape to the one just fixed in storeReport(): refuses to overwrite a good row, but freely CREATES a fresh zero-total row that bctcIdentityGuard.ts then reads at serve time as the OCR-corruption fingerprint. The file's own comment at lines 254-263 already says it 'carried the same two defects' and 'mirrors the identical guard' — the mirror was completed for only one of the two arms.
review.po_verified_at_source_20260721T1811: PO RE-READ THE FILE THIS TICK rather than accepting QA's or router's description, and the single decisive fact checks out: `totalAssets: 0` at line 307 is a hardcoded LITERAL and is the ONLY assignment to that field in the whole file (grep: refs at 73, 255, 307, 425, 535 — 307 is the sole write, 535 binds it to the INSERT, 425 is the SQL column list, 255 is the comment, 73 is the summary formatter). There is NO code path in this function that can produce a non-zero balance sheet. The surrounding lines 304-313 are likewise all-zero literals across currentAssets, nonCurrentAssets, liabilities, equity and totalLiabilitiesAndEquity.
review.product_question_decide_before_scoping: ANSWER THIS FIRST — the fix does not follow from the defect. Question as router framed it: if a news-inference fallback only ever produces directional hints and never real balance-sheet figures, is writing it into financial_reports — the table bctcIdentityGuard treats as authoritative at serve time — the actual design error, such that guarding arm (b2) alone merely relocates the problem? PO'S STRONG STEER, WITH THE PROOF: YES, IT IS THE DESIGN ERROR, and here is the reductio that settles it. Arm (b1) already blocks every write where a good row exists. Arm (b2), applied literally, blocks every write where NO row exists AND totalAssets<=0. Since totalAssets is hardcoded 0 on EVERY call (verified above — no path produces otherwise), the two arms together block 100% of this function's writes. Adding arm (b2) does not fix the function; it silently converts it into a total no-op while leaving ~600 lines of live, tested, maintained code in place pretending to be a working fallback. A guard that makes its own subject unreachable is not a guard — it is proof that the write target is wrong. CORROBORATING, AND THE PART THAT MAKES THIS USER-FACING RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY: (i) the code's OWN comment at lines 254-259 already concedes the whole argument — 'this fallback ALWAYS writes totalAssets=0 ... it reconstructs directional hints from news signals, never real balance-sheet figures — i.e. every call is, by construction, the exact OCR-corruption fingerprint bctcIdentityGuard.ts checks for at serve time.' The codebase has already diagnosed itself; nobody drew the conclusion. (ii) The write is strictly WORSE than not writing, because it destroys an honest signal: an absent row serves 'Chua co du lieu BCTC' ('we do not have this'), whereas a zeros row serves '[CORRUPT DATA - SKIP] total_assets=0 (OCR extraction failure)' — a false claim that we HAVE the filing and it is broken, which misattributes a defect to the filer. This is the same family of harm as the ngay_nop flip on the parent row: fabricating a state that defames a real-world filing. (iii) buildAnalysisSummary() at line 73 formats this into Vietnamese RAG-retrievable prose — 'Tong tai san: 0 trieu dong.' — a flat factual assertion that the company has zero total assets, written into the retrieval corpus. That is fabricated financial data in a served surface, and it engages feedback_no_fake_data_real_fetch directly. THEREFORE the design target to evaluate is: directional news-inference hints belong in a hints/signals surface, NOT in financial_reports. BA must still evaluate the alternatives honestly (a separate table/column; a nullable-financials sentinel row explicitly marked non-authoritative that bctcIdentityGuard excludes; or deleting the write path entirely and keeping the function as a pure read-side hint producer) — my steer is not a pre-selected implementation, and if BA finds a consumer that genuinely needs these rows in financial_reports, say so and I will revisit.
review.six_tests_encode_the_defect: THE HARD PART, AND WHY THIS IS A PO/BA ROW AND NOT A FIXER TICKET. SIX existing tests assert the first-ever zero-total write SUCCEEDING, i.e. they encode the defect as intended behaviour: 1294b-bctc-fallback RED-1 / RED-6 / RED-7 / RED-8-first-call (VCB/VIC/BSR/VJC first-call, all no-prior-row first-ever writes asserting fallback:true + row-exists), and BOTH cases in FIX-BCTC-NEWS-CHAIN-FALLBACK-ID-ORPHAN (run#1 explicitly commented first-ever-write, asserting fallback:true + row-exists for Q1 and Q2 sort_keys). QA adjudicated these individually and confirmed they are genuine intent-assertions, not incidental fixture inconvenience — that adjudication is accepted and must NOT be re-derived. These six are IN SCOPE to be rewritten by this row, and rewriting them is the deliverable that encodes whatever product answer is chosen. They are also the reason a quiet patch is impossible: any honest fix turns six green tests red, and a developer without this row's authority would reasonably read that as 'my change is wrong' and revert — which is EXACTLY what happened once already (see prior_attempt_reverted).
review.prior_attempt_reverted: dev-mcp-server ALREADY TRIED the naive fix during the parent row's arm-(b2) work: applied the storeReport guard pattern to tryNewsChainFallback(), broke those 6 tests, and reverted cleanly — documenting it as an open gap in usecases.md rather than folding it in. That was the RIGHT call under a scope-hold and is not a failure; it is corroboration that the naive patch is blocked by design intent, not by a fixable test bug. Do not re-attempt the naive guard.
review.containment_do_not_downgrade: BLAST RADIUS IS BOUNDED — THIS IS LATENT, NOT BLEEDING, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HIGH AND NOT P0. Router grep-confirmed the containment independently of QA: enableBctcFallback is declared optional at bctc/types.ts:59, DEFAULTS TO false at fetchParseAndStoreBctc.ts:50 (destructured `enableBctcFallback = false`), and resolvePdfText.ts:228 gates the fallback call behind `if (!enableBctcFallback)`. No non-test caller passes it true. THE FLAG IS THE CONTAINMENT AND MUST BE RECORDED AS SUCH — two failure modes to pre-empt: (1) nobody may downgrade this row on the grounds that 'the flag is false so it is safe' — the flag being false is WHY this is HIGH rather than P0, it is already priced in, and re-applying it is double-counting; (2) NOBODY MAY ENABLE enableBctcFallback ANYWHERE — test, staging or production — UNTIL THIS ROW IS CLOSED. Flipping that flag with arm (b2) open turns a latent hole into live manufacture of corrupt authoritative financial rows, on the exact mechanism the parent row was minted to stop. If a future task needs the fallback enabled, it depends on this row.
review.acceptance: (1) A written product decision on where news-chain fallback output belongs, stated on this row before any code is scoped — either 'not in financial_reports' (PO's steer) with the replacement surface named, or a reasoned rebuttal naming the consumer that requires those rows in financial_reports. (2) The chosen design implemented such that no all-zeros row is ever CREATED in financial_reports by this path. (3) The six tests named in six_tests_encode_the_defect rewritten to assert the CHOSEN behaviour, with each rewrite's intent stated — not deleted, not skipped, not left asserting the old contract. (4) get_bctc_full for a ticker with no real filing serves honest absence ('Chua co du lieu BCTC'), never '[CORRUPT DATA - SKIP] total_assets=0' manufactured by this path. (5) Arm (b1) behaviour is preserved unchanged — a previously-good stored report is still never overwritten. (6) If the write path is removed entirely, buildAnalysisSummary()'s zero-valued Vietnamese output (line 73) must not reach any served or RAG-retrievable surface either — check that plane explicitly, do not assume removing the INSERT covers it.
review.verification_gate: MECHANISM-SCOPED AND FULLY CODE-LEVEL — deliberately carries NO ingest, deploy-window or multi-day dependency, unlike the parent row (this is why it can converge in one pass). (a) A forced/simulated news-chain fallback invocation for a ticker with NO prior financial_reports row creates NO row — asserted against the live serving path via get_bctc_full returning 'Chua co du lieu BCTC', not by reading the DB plane directly (parent-row precedent: the DB plane and the serving plane diverged and only the serving plane matters here). (b) Same invocation for a ticker WITH a good stored row leaves it untouched and still serving non-zero total_assets (arm b1 regression). (c) grep proves no remaining code path can bind a hardcoded zero balance sheet into a financial_reports INSERT. (d) RED-before demonstrated by git-stash A/B with the test changes kept, same technique dev-mcp-server used on the parent row's arm (b2). (e) Full suite run and every failure file-attributed, not name-grepped — 1405b-bctc-vps-fixes.test.ts is a known decoy (has 'bctc' in the filename, its failures are in the unrelated logVpsPush group and are a test-order flake).
review.scope_boundaries: DOES NOT own re-extraction or remediation of any already-corrupt or absent report — that stays with OPS-BCTC-REFINE-REPASS-NONBANK-5T, W5-FU-CTG-REFINE-96e36139 and SPIKE-BCTC-Q1-2026-SERVABILITY-CENSUS. review.title: dev-team head-pin auto-reset is 24h while the tick cadence is ~30min — ONE silently-failed spawn takes all four dispatch lanes offline for up to 24h
review.mechanism: docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md L492 gates the ENTIRE dispatch chain (BOUNDED-1 -> SLS -> RLC -> QA-Drain) on head.status being idle/done/missing/v1. L491 is the only self-heal: 'head.status == in_progress AND head.updated_at >= 24h -> stale crash, reset to idle'. Between those two lines, any head that pins without progressing takes every dispatch lane offline until the 24h timer expires. The Pipeline Resume path at L470-489 does re-spawn head.next_agent each tick, but it stamps nothing on .head, so a spawn that dies before writing anything leaves updated_at frozen and the resume silently repeats — burning one spawn per tick with no forward progress and no alert.
review.instance: 2026-07-25T05:18:14Z BOUNDED-1 claimed P2 FIX-VNINDEX-CACHE-STARTUP-PURGE and pinned the head. At 09:48Z (4h25m later) PO verified: no commit references the task id; no working-tree change under apps/mcp-server/; no dev-mcp-server notebook entry (its last three 2026-07-25 entries are all pre-05:18Z work from session 4ae45b71); and task_list_held returned 14 locks with NO lock on task:FIX-VNINDEX-CACHE-STARTUP-PURGE — so Pipeline Resume was never blocked by a peer holder and was free to re-spawn every tick. Prior BOUNDED-1 cadence was one claim+closeout every ~30min (7 claims 02:17Z-05:18Z), i.e. a healthy task closes in ~13-30min; the 24h threshold is roughly 48x the observed p100. Blast radius during the pin: 18 P0 rows in ready[], 73 qa-eligible rows in review[], 390 backlog rows — none dispatchable. Auto-reset would not have fired until 2026-07-26T05:18Z. PO unpinned by hand at 09:48Z.
review.why_p1: Single point of failure with a ~24h outage window on the whole dev pipeline, triggered by any one silent spawn failure, with no alert on the way in. The hand-unpin PO performed this tick is not a fix and does not survive the next occurrence.
review.acceptance: (1) A head pinned in_progress with no .head movement AND no commit referencing active_task_id for a bounded interval proportionate to the observed tick cadence (NOT 24h) is detected and reset; PO does not ratify a specific number — architect picks it from the measured cadence and states the basis. (2) Detection emits a BUG-channel signal naming the pinned task id and the pin duration, so a silent spawn failure becomes loud rather than being inferred 4h later from a missing commit. (3) Pipeline Resume records evidence of each re-spawn attempt (e.g. an attempt counter or last_resume_at on .head) so a repeated no-op resume is distinguishable from a task that is genuinely still running — the current state is indistinguishable from the outside, which is why this went unnoticed. (4) Repeated resume of the SAME active_task_id past a small attempt bound stops re-spawning and escalates instead of burning one spawn per tick.
review.scope_out: Do NOT fix by raising WIP or by removing the head gate — the WIP<=1 BOUNDED-1 bound is user-gated (2026-07-04) and out of scope. Do NOT diagnose why dev-mcp-server specifically produced nothing on FIX-VNINDEX-CACHE-STARTUP-PURGE; that row is back in backlog[] and, if it stalls the head a second time, becomes a separate reproducible per-row dispatch failure.

  1. CLAUDE.md instructs EVERY agent: "All structural data (services, agents, zones, channels, sources, watchlist) lives in docs/data/system-map.json. Query with jq — never hardcode values." Candidates: (i) GENERATE `.project.watchlist` from the `watchlist` table so the file is derived and cannot drift, with the frontend constant regenerated from it in the same step; (ii) keep the file authored but add a CI/audit check asserting `.project.watchlist` set-equals the runtime `get_watchlist` set, failing loud on divergence; (iii) delete `.project.watchlist` outright and repoint CLAUDE.md, the system-map-query skill, fb-market-poster's flow and the frontend at the runtime tool — smallest surface, but the frontend needs a build-time or runtime fetch it does not have today, so cost is real. A remedy that only reconciles today's 24 leaves the drift mechanism armed and SPIKE_1946 will recur a third time.

review.title: pdf-extractor's uvicorn PARENT process (PID 1) -- not tesseract concurrency, which is already fixed and proven bounded -- is the dominant memory driver, and the row's OOM-risk business case remains open: VmHWM=2,541,184kB (~2.42 GiB, ~97% of the 2.5 GiB cap) was recorded inside this container's post-fix life, which would leave the just-shipped AC-4 bar (<=80% of cap) violated at peak even though it is satisfied at trough
review.root_cause: MECHANISM (qa+router corroborated, both read-only): a load-correlated SAWTOOTH in the parent uvicorn process, released at job boundaries -- NOT accumulation/climbing; that framing was explicitly refuted by direct observation and must not be carried forward. (1) VmHWM (all-time high-water mark since container start 2026-07-28T16:45:08Z, RestartCount=0) = 2,541,184 kB -- a real peak reached ~97% of the 2.5 GiB cap at least once in this container's post-fix life, proving the ceiling is reachable. (2) qa's own re-sample ~23min after the concurrency-fix rebuild, under ordinary (non-burst) traffic: MemPerc 78-83%, PID1 (uvicorn) alone RSS ~2.0-2.1 GiB (~83-84% of the container BY ITSELF) while tesseract stayed bounded at 0-1 (~90-95 MiB each) -- the now-fixed tesseract concurrency is not the term driving the container back toward the cap. (3) auditor samples 45.18% (17:10:56Z) and 44.74% (17:16:32Z) -- stable/declining in that window, consistent with a trough. (4) router's own 10-sample series 17:18:46Z-17:21:47Z: PID1 RSS held 1.08-1.11 GiB with tesseract=1 in-flight; at 17:21:06Z tesseract dropped to 0 and MemPerc fell to 40.44%; at 17:21:26Z tesseract returned to 1 and RSS jumped 1.24->1.39 GiB in one sample -- RSS moving WITH an OCR job starting/stopping, not monotonically, by a magnitude (100s of MiB per job) that dwarfs a single tesseract child's own footprint. (5) parent dominance: PID1 RSS ~2.0-2.1 GiB at peak vs tesseract child ~90-95 MiB -- the child term was already proven bounded by FIX-PDFX-TESSERACT-CONCURRENCY-VIOLATES-SINGLE-WORKER-INVARIANT; this row is specifically the PARENT term, a different mechanism in a different process from that row's fix.  ||  EVIDENCE ADDENDUM 2026-08-01T06:08Z-06:17Z (po/triage-auditor-findings-20260801, read-only: docker inspect + docker stats + docker exec cat /proc/1/status + /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.* + docker logs). THIS ADDENDUM FALSIFIES THIS ROW OWN PRIOR root_cause ON ONE POINT -- read it before planning. (1) THE BURST IS NOT RELEASED AT THE JOB BOUNDARY. A 47-page PekEngineAdapter job ran to successful completion at 06:09:53.913Z ("_run_pek_extract: DONE report_id=486980a8-2b61-4e02-8bf1-65166542670c push_echo_units=47 push_echo_pages=47"). From 06:10:01Z to 06:16:59Z -- 40 consecutive samples at 8-15s spacing, entirely AFTER that completion, with tesseract child count 0 in every sample -- PID1 (uvicorn/python3) VmRSS was BYTE-IDENTICAL at 2521008 kB in all 40 samples, VmHWM constant at 2641368 kB, and cgroup memory.current oscillated only 2609258496-2610274304 B (+/-0.04%). At 06:17Z ps inside the container showed PID1 python3 RSS 2521008 kB as the ONLY non-transient process. 2521008 kB = 2.404 GiB = 96.2% of the 2.5 GiB cap HELD AT IDLE, with zero work in flight. The prior root_cause clause "a load-correlated SAWTOOTH ... released at job boundaries -- NOT accumulation/climbing" does NOT hold for this container life: the down-stroke of the sawtooth did not occur. (2) RESTING STATE IS AT THE WALL. 06:08:34Z docker stats: 2.468GiB / 2.5GiB = 98.70%, PIDs=29. cgroup v2 at the same moment: memory.current=2675834880 of memory.max=2684354560 = 99.68%, memory.peak=2684391424 (i.e. peak has touched/exceeded the limit), anon=2564096000, file=52416512, slab=17084624. Container: RestartCount=2, StartedAt=2026-08-01T02:46:16.989733302Z, State.ExitCode=0, OOMKilled=false, RestartPolicy=unless-stopped, HostConfig.Memory=2684354560. Free headroom at 06:08Z was ~8.5 MB of cgroup budget -- not enough for one more page raster, let alone one more job. (3) THE FAILURE MODE IS A CLEAN EXIT, NOT AN OOM KILL. ExitCode=0 / OOMKilled=false with RestartPolicy=unless-stopped means this service silently self-terminates and is restarted by Docker rather than being OOM-killed, so NOTHING in the OOM-detection plane (A-30 state.oom_killed, dmesg OOM-killer) will ever witness it. Any acceptance criterion that keys on OOMKilled will pass while the service is dying. (4) LOAD CONTROL FOR THE TRAJECTORY -- CORRECTS THE BRIEF THAT PROMPTED THIS ADDENDUM. The auditor brief reported the 53%->80-82% climb as occurring at "0 extracts/30m" (i.e. an idle leak). docker logs --since 2026-08-01T02:46:00Z contradicts that: 52 POST /extract in this container life, 51 of them inside 03:27:22-03:35:38Z and 1 in hour 05. The climb window was NOT idle -- it contained a 51-job burst. So the correct reading is neither "idle leak" nor "released sawtooth": memory is acquired during jobs and RETAINED ACROSS job boundaries, producing a monotonically rising FLOOR (53% at 03:06Z -> 96.2% floor at 06:17Z after ~52 jobs). (5) QUEUE PRESSURE IS REAL: bctc_vps_queue live at 06:17Z = deferred_infra 328, enrich_failed 128, done 98, url_not_found 42, pending 13, pek_triggered 5 -- there is queued work that will re-enter this service. PRECISION CORRECTION 2026-08-01T06:23Z (same triage, extended sampler completed after the addendum was first written): the post-completion retention series is larger than stated above -- 54 consecutive samples spanning 06:10:01Z to 06:22:26Z (12min25s, two independent sampler runs, 8-15s spacing), tesseract child count 0 in every sample, PID1 VmRSS BYTE-IDENTICAL at 2521008 kB in all 54 and VmHWM constant at 2641368 kB in all 54. docker stats at 06:23:08Z: 2.406GiB / 2.5GiB = 96.25%, RestartCount still 2, StartedAt unchanged 2026-08-01T02:46:16Z. Read the "40 samples / 06:10:01Z-06:16:59Z" figure above as a subset of this series, not a second observation. LATE PARTIAL RELEASE, RECORDED FOR HONESTY AND BECAUSE IT IS DIAGNOSTIC (2026-08-01T06:25:29Z, same triage): PID1 VmRSS finally moved off the 2521008 kB plateau to 2407444 kB -- a release of 113564 kB (~111 MiB) occurring somewhere between 06:22:26Z and 06:25:29Z, i.e. roughly 12-15 MINUTES AFTER the 06:09:53Z job completion, with ZERO POST /extract in the whole 06:10Z-06:25Z interval (docker logs --since 2026-08-01T06:10:00Z | grep -c "POST /extract" = 0). VmHWM unchanged at 2641368 kB. docker stats 06:25:29Z = 92.95%. So the correct statement is NOT "memory is never released" -- it is that release is LATE, PARTIAL and DECOUPLED FROM THE JOB BOUNDARY: ~111 MiB of ~1.5 GiB acquired since the 03:06Z 53% baseline came back, out-of-band, a quarter-hour after the work finished, leaving a 2407444 kB = 91.9%-of-cap resting floor. This is the signature of deferred/opportunistic reclamation (glibc malloc arena trim, or a GC generation collected on a timer) rather than of scope-exit deallocation at the request boundary, and it is why a snapshot taken at any single moment can read as either "sawtooth" or "plateau" depending on where in this slow cycle it lands. It reinforces AC5: the three candidate mechanisms must be discriminated with an artifact, and AC6: the idle floor must be measured at least 5 minutes -- preferably 20 -- after the last job, not at the boundary.
review.deliverable: Diagnose what in the uvicorn PARENT process holds 100s of MiB-to-~1GiB per job and releases it at job boundaries (candidates, not a prescription: PDF page rasterization/image buffers held in the request-handling coroutine before/after handing a page to OCR, pdfplumber/PyMuPDF page-object retention across a multi-page document, response-body buffering, GC-deferred large objects between requests) -- name the mechanism with a captured artifact, not prose. Then size a bound so peak MemPerc stays <=80% under the SAME caller shape used to verify the concurrency fix (a 15-wide POST /extract burst), OR make an explicit, evidenced recommendation that the cap itself needs revisiting (user/ops-gated infra decision -- do not decide the cap here).
acceptance: AC1: mechanism named with a captured artifact (not prose) explaining which parent-process code path drives RSS by 100s of MiB to ~1 GiB+ per OCR job and releases it at job end.

AC2: peak docker stats MemPerc for pdf-extractor during and shortly after a 15-wide POST /extract burst (the same trigger shape already used to verify the concurrency fix) is measured and reported with raw output + date -u timestamps -- whatever the number is, report it honestly.

AC3: EITHER a change lands that keeps peak MemPerc <=80% of the 2.5 GiB cap under that burst, OR an explicit evidence-backed recommendation is written that 80%-of-cap is not achievable at the current cap for the largest real observed document, routed to ops/user for a capacity decision.
AC4: regression floor -- BCTC extraction still succeeds end-to-end on at least one real scanned PDF after any change.

AC5 (added 2026-08-01): explicitly discriminate unreleased-Python-heap vs malloc-arena-fragmentation vs deliberate-cache as the cause of the retained idle floor, with an artifact (e.g. tracemalloc/gc totals vs RSS, or a malloc_trim/jemalloc A-B) -- a fix aimed at the wrong one of these three will not move RSS.

AC6 (added 2026-08-01): the accepted bound must hold at IDLE, not only at peak -- measure PID1 VmRSS at least 5 minutes after the last job completes with tesseract child count 0, and report it. The 2026-08-01 idle floor was 2521008 kB = 96.2% of cap.

AC7 (added 2026-08-01): do NOT use OOMKilled as a success signal -- the observed failure mode is State.ExitCode=0 / OOMKilled=false under RestartPolicy=unless-stopped. Any regression gate must key on MemPerc/VmRSS or on RestartCount growth, never on the OOM flag.

review.title: A-29 Cron Fire Check is UNEXECUTABLE as specified against its own named data source, so the implementing agent silently substituted a success-rate predicate that is structurally blind to a stopped cron - and the same defect silently drops systemAuditTier1/2/3, which is why the frozen auditor tier heartbeats were invisible
review.root_cause: docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:174-182 specifies a FIRE-GAP predicate: call get_cron_health, iterate system-map.json microservices[0].crons, compute expected last-fire from the schedule expression, flag if gap > 2x cadence. FOUR independent reasons that predicate cannot execute as written, all PO-verified 2026-07-29T02:14-02:25Z. (1) WRONG PATH: the literal jq path .microservices[0].crons resolves to null; the real path is .project.microservices[0].crons (70 entries). Navigable by a human, but wrong as written. (2) SCHEDULE GRAMMAR IS NOT UNIFORM: of the 70 schedules only 32 are parseable 5-field cron expressions. The other 38 (54%) are prose: */15 min, */6h, 08:00 VN M-F, 23:00 VN Sunday, 1st monthly 06:00 VN, 19:00 UTC daily (02:00 VN), plus the two non-schedules startup and helper. Compute-expected-last-fire-from-schedule-expression is undefined for 54% of the inventory. (3) THE NAME JOIN IS BROKEN: get_cron_health returns 87 runtime jobs; system-map lists 70 crons; after aggressive normalization (lowercase, strip trailing Job, strip non-alphanumerics) only 48 join. 39 runtime jobs have NO system-map entry and therefore no schedule and are uncheckable by this predicate at all, including pollNews, pollNews_all_sources_dark, bondMaturityPoller, publicContracts, vnstockFundamentalsRefresh, deepFetchMain, deepFetchVps, schedulerWatchdog, restartCadenceAlert and diskUsageAlert. 22 system-map crons have NO runtime record. Runtime names carry a Job suffix and :variant suffixes (dataAuditJob:daily, marketScanJob:open) that the SSOT names do not; no mapping contract exists. (4) NO DATA SOURCE FOR CLAUDE-CODE CRONS: systemAuditTier1/2/3 ARE present in .project.microservices[0].crons with clean parseable schedules (*/30 * * * *, 0 */4 * * *, 0 2 * * *) but are ABSENT from get_cron_health because they are Claude Code CronCreate crons, not mcp-server node-cron jobs. They land in the 22-cron no-runtime-record bucket and are silently skipped. WHAT THE CYCLE ACTUALLY RAN INSTEAD: Cron Health (A-29): 127+ jobs tracked; all success_rate >=80%, majority >=99% - PASS. The strings success_rate and 80% appear NOWHERE in docs/agents/system-auditor/ (PO re-ran the grep and confirms zero hits) - the bar is agent-invented and re-chosen per cycle, so A-29 is also non-reproducible. WHY THE SUBSTITUTE IS WORSE THAN NOTHING: success_rate is a ratio over runs that HAPPENED. A cron that stopped firing retains its historical ratio forever - a dead cron reports ~99% and PASSES. The substitute cannot detect a stopped cron under any circumstance, which is precisely and only the failure mode A-29 exists to catch.
review.po_ruling: MINTED AS ONE ROW, NOT TWO. The router submitted the A-29 predicate substitution and the three frozen tier heartbeats as separate findings. They are one defect: reason (4) is the mechanism by which the first causes the second to be undetectable. Splitting them would produce two rows that each fix half a join. CORRECTION TO THE DISPATCH BRIEF, recorded because it changes the fix: the brief states Tier-2/Tier-3 are Claude Code CronCreate crons and NOT entries in system-map microservices[0].crons, and concludes even a correct A-29 would not cover them. That is factually wrong - all three ARE in the inventory with clean cron schedules. The gap is on the DATA-SOURCE side, not the inventory side, so the fix is NOT to add them to system-map; it is to give A-29 a second source for Claude-Code-side fire state and to make a join miss loud. THE GENERALIZABLE DEFECT IS SILENT-DROP-ON-JOIN-MISS: today, adding a cron to the SSOT creates the ILLUSION of coverage because an entry with no matching runtime record is skipped without a word. That is a coverage-reporting lie and is the part most likely to recur in other detectors. ROUTED TO ARCHITECT NOT DEVELOPER because none of the four blockers is an implementation bug - each needs a contract decision: a canonical schedule grammar or a normalization pass over 38 prose entries, a name-mapping contract between two divergent namespaces, a fire-state source for Claude-Code crons where NO tool exists today (structural gap, not laziness), and a fail-loud-on-join-miss policy. NOT BATCHED into the auditor detector-correctness epic minted alongside this row: that epic is a triage pass over 18 stalled rows, and A-29 has demonstrated LIVE blindness on a P1 detector - it must not queue behind a housekeeping sweep.
review.acceptance: (1) A-29 in docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md is rewritten so its stated predicate is executable against sources that actually exist, or is explicitly narrowed to the subset it can cover with the uncovered remainder named in the spec text. (2) The corrected inventory path .project.microservices[0].crons appears in the spec. (3) A recorded decision for the 38 prose schedules: a canonical grammar they migrate to, or a documented parser contract handling them, or explicit exclusion with the exclusion visible in A-29 output. (4) A name-mapping contract between get_cron_health job names and system-map cron names is defined and recorded; the 48/87/70 join counts are re-derived after it. (5) FAIL-LOUD ON JOIN MISS: any system-map cron with no resolvable runtime record is REPORTED as unobservable, never silently skipped; a cycle that can only observe N of M spec'd crons must state N and M. (6) A disposition for Claude-Code-side cron fire state (systemAuditTier1/2/3 today) - either a new source, or an explicit out-of-scope statement in the spec plus a named detector that does cover them. (7) NO success-rate bar is reintroduced as a fire-gap proxy; if success_rate is checked at all it is a SEPARATE, separately-labelled check with a bar written in the spec rather than chosen per cycle.
review.note: Fire-gap blindness is CURRENTLY LIVE, but PO found no confirmed stopped mcp-server cron while verifying: every long-gap candidate cleared against its real schedule (devTeamHeartbeat=07:00 UTC Sunday, patternWatch=22:30 VN Sunday, integrityCheck=0 2 * * 0 all last fired Sunday 2026-07-26 as scheduled). Reported as MISSING rather than asserted: pollNews_all_sources_dark last fired 2026-07-22T15:00:11Z with total_runs=1 and has no system-map entry, so no schedule ground truth exists to judge it - it may be a one-shot dark-launch probe or a dead cron, and A-29 cannot currently tell the difference. That ambiguity is itself an instance of gap (3).

The remaining 6 already carry owners: DOCAUDIT-MEMORY-PATH-PREDICATE=architect, D4-WHITELIST-DATA-QUALITY-ANOMALY-PREFIX=dev-mcp-server, C04-PARSEDAT-RECENCY-PREDICATE=architect, A30-VMHWM-VETO-TAUTOLOGY-FALSE-NEGATIVE=architect, EMIT-SEVERITY-LABEL-FLAT-ESCALATION-BYPASS-NEVER-FIRES=developer, T1-PREGATE-MEMCREEP-SINGLE-POINT-SAMPLE=developer. The lane is not slow, it is stalled by construction: an unowned row is invisible to pickup, so backlog depth grows monotonically with every audit cycle that mints rather than drains.
review.po_ruling: The router asked whether to batch these into one consolidated epic or continue minting individual rows, flagging possible churn-without-convergence. Ruling: NEITHER a 19th loose row NOR a merge of 18 distinct defects into one undifferentiated blob. The 18 rows describe genuinely different detectors and merging their content would destroy the diagnostic work already in them. What is actually broken is not their granularity, it is that 12 have no owner. So this epic is a TRIAGE PASS, not a container: its deliverable is a disposition per row, and it deliberately does NOT absorb their scope. Bounded on purpose - it mints NO new rows, so it cannot itself become the churn it exists to stop. Assigned to architect rather than PO doing the assignment inline: choosing an owner requires reading each row's technical content to judge whether it is a spec defect (architect), an implementation defect (developer/dev-mcp-server), or already obsolete - and PO assigning 12 owners without that read would reproduce the mint-without-understanding failure this epic exists to correct. FIX-AUDITOR-A29-UNEXECUTABLE-SPEC-SILENT-JOIN-DROP is explicitly EXCLUDED from this epic and routed independently at P1: it has demonstrated live detector blindness and must not queue behind a housekeeping sweep.
review.acceptance: (1) Each of the 18 listed rows ends this epic in exactly one of two terminal states: next_agent set to a real agent that can act on it, or status CLOSED with a one-line reason (superseded-by-<id>, obsolete, or duplicate-of-<id>). No row may remain with next_agent unset. (2) Any row closed as duplicate/superseded names the surviving row id. (3) This epic mints NO new task rows - if triage uncovers genuinely new work, it is recorded in the epic note for PO to mint separately, never self-minted, so the epic cannot grow the lane it is draining. (4) A stale-check is run first per the known stale-backlog hazard: for each row, git log --since=<its created_at> over the file it names, to catch rows already fixed by later unrelated commits before spending any triage effort on them. (5) Final state reported as a count: N assigned, M closed, N+M=18.
review.note: Deliberately scoped to disposition-only. Do not fix any detector inside this epic - the point is to make the lane drainable, not to drain it in one pass.

review.title: 34 of 40 sprint ids referenced by task rows / sprint_goal have NO active_sprints[] or closed_sprints[] object — PO sign-off, cold-eviction and decision-journal archival are all structurally unreachable for them
review.desc:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-07-30T09:3xZ on docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, not inferred. Every `.task_board.<lane>[].sprint` value and every `.sprint_goal.entries[].sprint_id` was resolved against the union of `.task_board.active_sprints[].id` (8 ids) and `.task_board.closed_sprints[].id` (19 ids) plus the cold-archive closed-id universe (`docs/data/orch/archive/*.json`: .closed_sprints[].id, .closed_sprint_goals sprint ids, [.done_tasks[].sprint]). Result: 40 distinct referenced sprint ids, of which 34 resolve to NOTHING. Top offenders by reference count: TOKEN-ECONOMY-AUDIT (28 refs), ULTRACODE-AUDIT-FIXALL (24), COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP (11), FLOW-PRICE-ALPHA-LOOP (9). Only 6 ids resolve (MARKET-INDICATOR-DEPTH-P0, COWORK-RELIABILITY, BCTC-ANALYTICS-LAYER, FLEET-HOST-SAFETY, OHLCV-UNIT-CONTAM-WHOLEROW-LT1000, VN-MACRO-TOOLING).

THREE CONSEQUENCES, each verified against the executable and not the prose:
(1) PO SIGN-OFF IS IMPOSSIBLE for those 34. `docs/agents/po/flow/main.md:126` makes the Approve path MUST-set `active_sprints[sprint_id].status = "DONE"`. There is no such key to set, so the canonical sign-off write cannot be performed at all — the failure mode is not a wrong token (the documented hazard) but a missing object.
(2) DECISION-JOURNAL ARCHIVAL IS UNREACHABLE. `scripts/agents-flow/decision-journal-archive.sh` selects STATUS-based (header :9 'Selection is STATUS-based (closed sprint id vs still-active), NOT mtime-based'), building a closed-id universe (:120-127) and an active-id set (:116) and longest-prefix-matching each `sprint-<id>[-<agent>].md`. An id in NEITHER set is a THIRD, unhandled state: it is silently skipped forever, on both stdin and --all backfill paths. Live cost: `docs/agent-memory/decisions/` holds 513 sprint-*.md journals / 5.5MB, and the largest over-cap files all belong to dangling ids — sprint-CI-RED-RECONCILE-po.md 331592B (9.2x the 36000B cap), sprint-SYSTEMIC-REMAKE-P1-qa.md 225553B, sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-developer.md 128381B.
(3) THE BREACH DETECTOR THEREFORE NEVER CONVERGES. context-bloat-backstop re-emits on whichever journal a live agent happens to write: 138 context-bloat signals sit in docs/signals/processed/, ~34 of them for the 3 COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP journals alone over 07-25..07-30, every one marked processed with the condition untouched. Same never-converging-detector family as FIX-NOTEBOOK-PRUNER-LINE-ONLY-SETPOINT-BYTE-CAP-NEVER-CONVERGES.

ORIGIN: triaged from the 2026-07-30T09:07Z drain's context_bloat_breach on sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-architect.md (46429B vs 36000B cap, 191L/600L — byte-axis only). That signal was DEFERRED as a prune (live sprint, file uncommitted-modified at triage time, content is load-bearing design rationale) — but the standard 'defer until the sprint closes' disposition is a FALSE PREMISE here: COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP exists only as `.sprint_goal.entries[15].sprint_id` plus 11 task-row refs (TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-2 DONE, -3/-4/-5/-10 READY, -6..-9 BACKLOG), so it can never close and the deferral can never expire.

SUPERVISED + PLAN_ONLY ON PURPOSE — the naive fix bricks the board, and this was measured, not guessed. The obvious fix is a referential-integrity rule in `scripts/orch-validate.mjs` (Stage 1 already does dangling-ref checks and is the validator every `scripts/orch-apply.sh` write must pass). Arming it fail-loud TODAY rejects EVERY subsequent board write, because 34 ids are already dangling. Sequencing is therefore mandatory, and is the design question for architect:
AC-1 RECONCILE FIRST: decide per dangling id whether it is genuinely live (register an `active_sprints[]` object), genuinely finished (register in `closed_sprints[]` so the journal archiver can sweep it), or never was a sprint (rename/strip the `.sprint` field). 'BACKLOG' appearing as a 5-ref sprint id is evidence the field is also being used as a non-sprint sentinel — classify that separately.
AC-2 THEN arm the guard, WARN-first with an env-var escalation to reject, mirroring the notebook-immutability gate disposition (`.claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md` AC-2a: GIT_NOTEBOOK_IMMUTABILITY_MODE defaults to warn). Do not arm reject until a corpus replay reads 0.
AC-3 the guard must cover BOTH reference planes (`task_board.*[].sprint` and `sprint_goal.entries[].sprint_id`) — a check on one plane leaves the other silently broken.
AC-4 give `decision-journal-archive.sh` an explicit third-state branch: an id in neither set must FAIL LOUD (or emit one deduped signal), never be silently skipped. Today's silent skip is what made a 5.5MB/513-file accumulation invisible.
AC-5 verification gate is timestamped and measured, not prose: re-run the resolver and show `dangling == 0`, and show `decision-journal-archive.sh --all` moving a previously-unreachable journal, with a before/after byte count.
AC-6 do NOT fix this by prune/split of any live journal — that is the deferred, separate action and it races live editors (feedback_ctxbloat_breach_on_live_sprint_file_defer).
