review.title: system-auditor predicate errors — mutation-timestamp + window class, 3 checks. (C-04) counts bulk-reparse re-stamps as new low-confidence extractions (parsed_at is a mutation timestamp, not arrival) AND counts never-extracted rows (conf=0, status=pending) as low-confidence -> recurring WARN false-positive. (C-01/C-02 — added 2026-07-31 by PO, verified live) their window is `date >= date("now","-1 day")` = TWO calendar dates: at 2026-07-31T09:12Z C-01 returned 947 and C-02 returned 1070 while date=2026-07-31 held only 129 distinct codes. The checks cannot measure same-day coverage at ANY threshold — the window is the defect, not the >=25 / >0 bar. Also write down the invariant that cost a router a full session on a phantom "86% coverage collapse": daily_ohlcv same-day coverage is ~130 BY DESIGN (live intraday tick universe = 117-119 codes EVERY session per intraday_ohlcv_5m 07-20..07-31 and market_prices_history); the full ~940-code universe lands ONLY via the nightly history backfill 00:00-02:20Z, which UPSERTs ~750k rows (97% of the 774k-row table, dates 2014-2026) and thereby CLOBBERS daily_ohlcv.updated_at — the exact same "mutation timestamp is not arrival" root cause as C-04. Every historical date shows 0-2 same-day writes vs 900-1000 next-day writes. Do NOT add a same-day-coverage-vs-trailing-median alarm: it would fire every single day.
review.root_cause: C-04 (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:572) = SELECT count(*) FROM financial_reports WHERE parsed_at > datetime('now','-7 days') AND extraction_confidence < 0.2, threshold <=5. TWO independent predicate defects, both RAW-probed by PO against live market.db in the mcp-server runtime. D1 RECENCY: parsed_at is a MUTATION timestamp bumped by any reparse, not an arrival timestamp. All 11 flagged rows have parsed_at in {2026-07-19, 2026-07-20} and NONE since; that 2-day window parsed 182 rows total against a historical baseline of 1-23 rows/WEEK — i.e. a bulk historical reparse batch re-stamped a legacy cohort into the 7-day window. Periods flagged are 2024-Q1..2025-Q4, not current filings. The 11 are 6.0% of the 182-row batch — a HEALTHY rate, not an extractor regression. D2 POPULATION: extraction_confidence < 0.2 sweeps in rows that were never extracted at all — 5 of the 11 (HUT 2024-Q1, HUT 2024-Q3, HUT 2025-Q3, BSR 2024-Q3, HUT 2025-Q4) — leaving only 6 rows that are genuinely low_confidence — carry conf=0.0 with validation_status in {pending, pending_extraction}. 'Not yet extracted' is not 'low-confidence extraction'; 45% of the alert population is mislabelled. An absolute count threshold (<=5) with no volume normalisation guarantees re-fire on every future bulk reparse.
review.deliverable: Re-specify C-04: (a) normalise to a RATE with a minimum-volume floor (e.g. lowconf/total > 15% AND total >= 20) instead of an absolute count, so healthy large batches do not trip it; (b) restrict the population to rows that actually completed extraction — exclude validation_status in ('pending','pending_extraction') and/or require extraction_confidence IS NOT NULL AND > 0; (c) decide whether recency should key off an immutable arrival column (published_at) rather than parsed_at, or whether the reparse path should stop re-stamping parsed_at. Fold into scripts/auditor-db-checks.sh as predicate SSOT per UC-ASL-P3 rather than leaving raw SQL in the flow doc.
review.acceptance: Replaying the live 2026-07-19/20 reparse batch through the new predicate emits ZERO C-04 signal. Negative control: a synthetic cohort where >15% of a >=20-row genuinely-extracted batch lands under 0.2 confidence STILL trips C-04. No never-extracted (pending*) row appears in the counted population.

review.title: RECURRING DATA LOSS: the notebook-write compose step silently REWRITES the content of RETAINED prior sections to pay for an over-cap current section, instead of trimming its own section first - and the skill has no immutability invariant, so a diff reviewer cannot tell authorized pruning from unauthorized rewriting
review.premise_correction_read_first: The incoming report framed this as 'zero deletions were required, it dropped 82 lines anyway', arithmetic from the commit's NET +43/-82 diffstat. THAT PREMISE IS WRONG and an implementer who chases it will fix nothing. The new section is 71L, not 43L; 152 + 71 = 223 > 200, so cap pressure was REAL and deletions WERE required. The defect is not that it deleted - it is WHICH bytes it deleted and that no rule forbids them.
review.measured_evidence: PO measured per-section line counts on both sides of 9b27e9723 (7 sections/152L -> 6 sections/113L). BEFORE -> AFTER: 05:08:58Z 81L -> 10L REWRITTEN; d4-auto 03:00 3L -> 3L intact; x1b5c2a9 02:33 25L -> 10L REWRITTEN; d986065c 00:42 10L -> DROPPED; 88ec89d6 00:36 14L -> 10L REWRITTEN; a1f7k9x5 23:39 10L -> 9L REWRITTEN; 60d26f9b 23:10 9L -> DROPPED; new section 06:09:36Z = 71L. So FOUR retained sections had their content silently rewritten, on top of two whole-section drops. The immediately-prior cycle's own audit record was compressed 81L -> 10L.
review.defect: THREE findings. (1) LADDER ORDER INVERTED: the new section is 71L against the AC-6 cap of <=60L per section. AC-3 Step 1f prescribes an ordered remedy whose FIRST step is 'If current-cycle section > 60L: trim to 60L first'. The agent skipped its own trim and paid the cap out of other sections' content. The spec-compliant outcome was reachable: trim 71->60 (212L), drop oldest 60d26f9b (203L), drop next-oldest a1f7k9x5 (193L) -> 5 sections, ~193L, every retained section BYTE-IDENTICAL. Actual outcome: 6 sections, 113L, four retained sections mutated. (2) NO IMMUTABILITY INVARIANT: nothing in AC-1..AC-6 of .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md states that retained sections are immutable. Steps 1c and 1f authorise DROPPING whole oldest blocks; no clause authorises editing a retained block's content, and no clause forbids it. Because AC-3 lands the result as ONE whole-file Write/Edit, both authorized pruning and unauthorized rewriting appear in the commit diff as plain deletions - they are indistinguishable to any reviewer. That is why this ran for multiple cycles unnoticed. (3) SPEC SELF-CONTRADICTION: AC-2 says 'Keep: current cycle + 2 prior sections = last 3 total', but AC-3 Step 1c says drop ONE oldest per cycle. Under Step 1c the section count is INVARIANT (add one, drop one), so AC-2's steady state of 3 is unreachable from above - this notebook sat at 7 sections, which AC-2 forbids and Step 1c permits indefinitely. Whichever is normative, the other is wrong.
review.acceptance: (1) The skill states an explicit IMMUTABILITY INVARIANT: sections retained across a cycle are byte-identical before and after. The ONLY authorized mutations are dropping a whole oldest block, the AC-2b intra-prune of a named permanent accumulator, and trimming the CURRENT cycle's own section. (2) AC-2 and AC-3 Step 1c are reconciled into one rule and the doc states which is normative. (3) The cap-pressure ladder ordering is made explicit and mandatory: trim own section to <=60L FIRST, then drop oldest whole blocks, NEVER mutate a retained section to make room. (4) A MECHANICAL check - runnable by the agent or a hook - that compares retained-section bytes before and after the settled write and fails if any surviving section changed. This is the AC that makes the class detectable at all; do not drop it for being harder than the prose ACs. (5) SCOPE FENCE: do NOT fix this in scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh. That is a DIFFERENT actuator (a PostToolUse hook running AFTER the write) and already carries its own 4-row REVIEW cluster: FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-REGEX-HEADING-MISMATCH, FIX-NOTEBOOK-PRUNER-LINE-ONLY-SETPOINT-BYTE-CAP-NEVER-CONVERGES, FIX-NOTEBOOK-LINECAP-SWEEP-BYTE-BLIND-BACKSTOP, FIX-ALERT-COMMANDER-NOTEBOOK-SINGLE-BLOB-UNPRUNABLE. This row is the agent's IN-MEMORY compose step, AC-3 Step 1, which runs BEFORE the hook ever sees the file. (6) The fix applies to the shared skill and therefore to all 37 APPEND-class agents in AC-6, not to system-auditor alone.

review.title: windowPartitioner maxWindowPages truncation creates a headless tail window that continuation-stitch.md's contract never anticipated -- resolveColumnLayout() defaults to code-first, silently swapping code/label on label-first (bank) continuation tables split by the cap
review.source: SPIKE-BCTC-REFINE-MAXWINDOW-TRUNCATION findings, docs/spikes/SPIKE-BCTC-REFINE-MAXWINDOW-TRUNCATION.md
review.root_cause: windowPartitioner.ts's maxWindowPages cap (windowPartitioner.ts:92-101) does NOT fold an over-cap continuation table into its current window -- it starts a brand-new window (i=j) at the very next page, which is itself a mid-table continuation page with no header of its own (that's why it matched CONTINUATION_MARKER in the first place). This 'tail window' gets page_type='continuation' (getBctcPendingRefineTool.ts:319-335) and is dispatched to the SAME sub-flow as a genuine first-page window (docs/agents/refine_bctc_md/flow/continuation-stitch.md), whose contract (Steps 2-3) unconditionally treats the window's first page as carrying the table's real header -- a rule that was never updated to anticipate a truncation-created headless tail. Downstream, refinedMarkdownParser.ts::resolveColumnLayout() (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:386-393) decides code-first vs label-first column order by reading the CAPTURED header row's own cell text, but headerCells is a per-call local re-initialized to null on every parseRefinedMarkdown invocation (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:439) -- unlike statement_section, which IS explicitly threaded window-to-window via initialSection/finalSection (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:404-419, finalizeBctcRefine.ts:162,174-175). A tail window with no header of its own (the expected shape) falls back to the DEFAULT code-first layout (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:387,391), silently swapping code<->label for every 4-column row of a label-first (bank Meu B02a/TCTDHN) continuation table whose true header only existed in the truncated head window. This corrupts (not drops) code/label text; value_current/value_prior are read from the same cell indices in both layouts so numeric values are unaffected. bctcScalarAggregator.ts resolves headline scalars (total_assets, equity_total, net_revenue, ...) via LABEL-CANONICAL matching preferred over code (bctcScalarAggregator.ts:20-21,396-399) and also uses row code/label shape for isBankFormFromRows bank-vs-corporate detection -- a swap can silently degrade or null the headline figures this pipeline exists to produce, with no error and no gate that catches it (checkSectionCompleteness/BEQ-7 only checks statement_section PRESENCE, never code/label correctness -- bctcSectionCompleteness.ts:27-60). Same root mechanism as the already-shipped FIX-BCTC-BANK-BS-COLUMN-ORDER (single-window, no-captured-header case) -- that fix added within-window header capture but never cross-window threading, so the maxWindowPages truncation path re-opens the identical hazard through a side door the original fix did not anticipate. Live-confirmed trigger frequency: 5 truncation WARNs within the same second of a single run (docs/agent-memory/health/team-tool-recheck-2026-06-21-1605.md:195-196) -- not a theoretical edge case. NOT independently reproduced within the spike's 120-min timebox: an actual corrupted bctc_table_rows row instance from a live truncation-tail window (would need pulling a real bctc_refined_units row past a report's first truncated unit_id and diffing against a known label-first bank filing).
review.deliverable: Architect decision (not a blind copy-paste) among 3 non-exclusive candidate mitigations, then implement the chosen combination: (1) raise maxWindowPages default / make it PDF-adaptive so real long bank continuation tables stop splitting; (2) thread a headerCells/column-layout hint forward across windows in parseDoneUnitsToRows the same way carrySection/statement_section already is, so a headless tail window inherits the correct layout from its head window; (3) have windowPartitioner mark truncation-tail windows explicitly (make the already-claimed but nonexistent truncated_continuation flag real -- windowPartitioner.ts:50 docstring vs 0 grep hits) so continuation-stitch.md's live agent-flow contract can fetch the head window's page-N header context on demand instead of silently assuming it is absent. Whichever combination is chosen, add a regression fixture that exercises the actual >maxWindowPages split-across-two-windows path end to end (partition -> refine markdown -> finalize) with a label-first (bank-form) 4+-column continuation table -- no existing test does this (grep -rn maxWindowPages apps/mcp-server/src/__tests__ only covers inputs that never exceed the cap: AR-refined-units-idempotency.test.ts:346,369; FIX-REFINE-WINDOW-DB-PAGELIST.test.ts:128 tests a different bug -- DB-driven page-list construction, not the continuation cap).
review.acceptance: A synthetic label-first (bank Meu B02a/TCTDHN-shaped) continuation table spanning > maxWindowPages pages, run through partitionIntoWindows -> parseRefinedMarkdown (per-window, threading whatever new cross-window state the chosen fix adds) -> finalizeBctcRefine's parseDoneUnitsToRows, produces rows in the tail window with code/label in the CORRECT (non-swapped) order -- not just non-empty. Negative control: an existing code-first (corporate) continuation table fixture is unaffected (0-diff). The health-recheck WARN's severity/wording is corrected in the SAME change (or a follow-up doc-only PR) to stop attributing it to intelligence-cycle/news signal-drop -- see SPIKE-BCTC-REFINE-MAXWINDOW-TRUNCATION Finding 0.

review.desc: Branch B of the OPS row's corrected AC-3 protocol (po_ac3_adjudication_20260808T0820Z, upheld by QA measurement 2026-08-08T09:03Z): unload log line 'Embedding model unloaded after 910s idle (threshold=900s)' fires correctly (embedder.py _maybe_unload_idle(), ~lines 120-150), but measured RSS only drops ~18-20pp -- pre-unload baseline 96.19-98.34% (PO, 08:17:31Z/08:19:24Z) to post-unload 77.98%/798.5MiB (system-auditor cron measurement sys-20260808T083446-4705, 08:34:46-08:35:03Z; docs/data/DASHBOARD.md:890-897), reproduced on a 2nd load/unload cycle (reload 08:49:50Z -> 97.67%/1000MiB @08:56:57Z, QA live read) -- well short of the ~35pp (~400MiB model) bar for a full OS-level reclamation, and well above the ~2pp ordinary jitter floor PO established, so this is a real but partial reclamation, not noise and not a failed unload.
review.root_cause_hypothesis: _maybe_unload_idle() calls `self._model = None` then `gc.collect()` with NO OS-level page-return call following -- classic glibc/CPython heap-retention behaviour: freed C-level allocations backing numpy/torch CPU tensors stay in the process's own free-list/arena rather than being returned to the OS via malloc_trim(0) or an equivalent allocator hook. Same allocator class already diagnosed and ratified with an empirical fix in THIS repo: FIX-PDFX-PARENT-PROCESS-MEMORY-BURST-HEADROOM (docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-07-fix-pdfx-parent-process-memory-burst-headroom.md) found malloc_trim(0) recovers ~99.7% of the per-job RSS delta for pdf-extractor's PEK pipeline after gc.collect() alone recovered 0 bytes -- directly reusable diagnostic template and fix shape.
review.scope: Confirm the allocator-retention hypothesis with the same isolated repro method as the pdf-extractor precedent (RSS before/after gc.collect() alone vs gc.collect()+malloc_trim(0)); if confirmed, add a guarded ctypes CDLL('libc.so.6').malloc_trim(0) call inside _maybe_unload_idle() immediately after gc.collect() (no-op / guarded on non-glibc platforms). Add direct test coverage matching __tests__/unit/test_embedder_idle_unload.py's existing style (mock/spy the release call fires post-unload). No config/env change expected -- this is an unconditional cleanup step, not a tunable.

WHY THIS IS A LAYER FIX, NOT N AGENT FIXES -- empirical refutation of the in-flow approach already on record: FIX-MARKET-WATCHER-NARRATE-NOT-EXECUTE-GUARD (2026-07-12) added an in-flow Step -1 'Execute-not-narrate directive' to docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/main.md:28. market-watcher narrated AGAIN on 2026-07-29T04:00Z (agentId a900dcd98a589be29) -- the in-flow guard structurally cannot fire when the agent stops before/outside the flow. DESIGN ASK (architect, plan_only -- do NOT hand-edit spawn-fanout.md on this pass):

Arm 1 (cheap, keep): positive-match markers, extended with the shapes observed here (future-tense 'Next actions (for the LLM ...)', 'would require', a STATUS token not in the slot agent's own RETURN enum). Arm 2 (LOAD-BEARING, new): a mechanical ARTIFACT-DELTA check -- for each slot, assert the declared durable artifact actually changed since spawn (git diff on a notebook/doc path, file mtime, a DB/tool row-count probe, or a new .signal_queue row) BEFORE last_fired is stamped. Arm 2 does not read the spawn's returned text at all, so no future narration shape can evade it. Precedent for the exact predicate already exists in-repo and should be reused, not reinvented: docs/agents/po/flow/main.md:161-168 AC-3 states the generic rule verbatim ('any step that writes an artifact AND asserts its own persistence must re-read the persistence layer before claiming it, never trust the write call's own exit code') and scripts/audit-output-contract.sh already does marker-parsed counting for the auditor. The novelty here is applying it at the SPAWNER boundary rather than the writer's own boundary -- which is the whole point, since the writer is the unreliable party.
(B) Decide WHERE the per-slot artifact declaration lives (candidate: a new required field on each docs/data/cowork-schedule.json slot, e.g. delivery_proof: {kind: file_delta|db_probe|signal_row, target: <path|tool>}), and how a slot with no honest proof artifact is handled (explicit opt-in allowlist ONLY -- see feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist; never a silent opt-out default).
(C) SEQUENCING -- MANDATORY, do not skip: reconcile with TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-6 (FR-7, 'Rewrite last-fired.md Step 5b as reconciliation logic', BACKLOG, next=developer) and with the standing PO ruling on FIX-COWORK-LASTFIRED-DECOUPLE-FROM-DELIVERY (po_consolidation_ruling_20260728: do not route the subsumed rows until the BA-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP epic closes). CATCHUP-6 makes last_fired a RECONCILED value (backfilled from task_list_held claimed_at); this row makes last_fired a GATED value (refused without delivery proof). Those are complementary but must not become two competing authorities over the same field -- the brief must state which one owns the write and how they compose. If architect judges this belongs INSIDE the CATCHUP epic as an added FR rather than as a standalone row, say so explicitly and route it there; that is an acceptable and expected outcome of this design pass.
(D) CRON-SPAWNED COVERAGE (the occurrence-2 half): cron-fired agents (system-auditor tiers, and any other non-cowork spawn) have NO exogenous observer at all. Note the already-designed mitigation in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-06-fix-system-auditor-cycle-notebook-persistence-lifecycle.md (3a stale-marker sweep) DOES NOT cover occurrence 2: RAW-verified there is no docs/agent-memory/.auditor-cycle-markers-2026-08-06T*.tmp on disk at all (the 6 orphans present are 07-30T16:00Z, 07-31T00:00Z, 08-01T04:00Z, 08-05T17:30Z, 08-05T18:00Z, 08-05T19:00Z) -- the 09:52Z spawn died BEFORE Step 0d ever created $MARKERS_FILE, so a sweep keyed on orphaned markers is blind to it. Whatever exogenous observer is proposed for cron-spawned agents must trigger on the ABSENCE of an expected cycle artifact for a due tick, not on the presence of an orphaned one. This sub-finding must also be relayed onto FIX-SYSTEM-AUDITOR-CYCLE-FINDINGS-NOT-SELF-PERSISTED (already READY, next=pm) so its implementation does not ship an incomplete detector.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE / DO NOT DO: (i) do not add another in-flow 'before returning, confirm you made N tool calls' self-check -- that is the exact vacuous reader-is-writer layer this row exists to route around, and it was considered and rejected in this triage; (ii) do not commission a fleet-wide agent-father sweep of all 45 docs/agents/*/flow/main.md files -- per-agent prose hardening is what already failed for market-watcher; (iii) no edits to .claude/agents/*.md (agent-father's zone, not needed for this fix).

qa.source: telegram report id 4227 — [kinh-dich] get_kinhdich_reading failed for HVN with 503 'insufficient price data ... requires at least 7 price points'
qa.root_cause: apps/stock-price/pkg/infrastructure/fetchers.go:303 (SQLitePriceHistoryRepository.GetHistory) and :240 (Tier3Fetcher) build the DSN 'file:%s?mode=ro&_journal_mode=WAL&_busy_timeout=5000'. The live market.db has PRAGMA journal_mode=delete, so the driver issuing PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL over a mode=ro connection fails with SQLITE_READONLY(8) 'attempt to write a readonly database'. The resulting db.Query error is then discarded at fetchers.go:318-320 ('return []domain.DailyOHLCV{}, nil //nolint:nilerr'), with the same swallow at :305-307 for sql.Open — so the handler emits HTTP 200 with an empty history and logs nothing. The two SIBLING repositories in this same package already fixed exactly this: foreign_flow_repository.go:33 and room_event_repository.go:32 both carry the comment 'Note: readonly mode (mode=ro) conflicts with WAL journal mode creation.' and dropped mode=ro from their DSN. The correction was applied to 2 of 4 call sites; fetchers.go:240 and :303 were missed.
qa.evidence: RAW-VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-31T00:25Z — every hop measured, not inferred. (1) The data EXISTS: sqlite3 on data/live/market.db (the bind-mount source of the container's /app/data) gives daily_ohlcv HVN = 775 rows spanning 2023-06-27..2026-07-30, and the handler's exact query (WHERE code='HVN' AND date >= date('now','-30 days')) returns 22. This is NOT the thin-ticker / new-listing data gap the alert text implies. (2) Outage reproduced: curl localhost:5005/reading/HVN -> 503 'insufficient price data ... requires at least 7 price points'; curl localhost:5005/market (VNINDEX) -> the same 503. BOTH kinh-dich routes are dead. (3) Failing hop isolated: gateway localhost:4000/stock/price/history?code=HVN&days=30 -> {code:HVN,history:[]}, identically empty for FPT/VNM/VCB and for days=30/365/3650 (universal and parameter-independent); but mcp-server's own localhost:3000/api/prices/history?code=HVN&days=30 -> count:22 with full rows. Same DB, same window, opposite result => the defect is in stock-price, not in the data. (4) stock-price direct: localhost:5010/price/history?code=HVN&days=30 -> {code:HVN,history:[]} while /health returns {status:ok} — passive health masking dead data. (5) Root cause reproduced in isolation: sqlite3 'file:data/live/market.db?mode=ro' 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;' -> 'Error: stepping, attempt to write a readonly database (8)', and a SELECT appended after that PRAGMA never executes; the same SELECT on a mode=ro connection WITHOUT the WAL pragma returns 22. PRAGMA journal_mode on the live DB = delete. (6) Alternatives ruled out at source: container clocks are exact (stock-price, mcp-server, kinh-dich and api-gateway all match the host to the second, so no date('now') drift); DB_PATH=/app/data/market.db resolves to a present 401MB file inside the container; and only 3 commits touched apps/stock-price since its image was built, none of them on the read path — so this is a live SOURCE defect, NOT a stale-image/deploy-lane problem. Rebuilding will not fix it.
qa.blast_radius: P1 — total loss of two product surfaces, not one ticker. (a) kinh-dich-service reads PRICE_HISTORY_URL -> api-gateway -> stock-price, so ComputeScores() receives nil for every code: get_kinhdich_reading 503s for ALL tickers and for the VNINDEX /market reading. (b) apps/frontend/app/lib/api/client.ts:245 calls the same /stock/price/history endpoint, so the frontend price-history chart renders empty. (c) fetchers.go:240 Tier3Fetcher carries the identical broken DSN, exposing the tier-3 price path to the same silent-empty failure.
qa.recommended_action: 1) Drop 'mode=ro&' from the DSN at fetchers.go:240 and :303 so all four call sites in this package match the already-corrected foreign_flow_repository.go:36 / room_event_repository.go:35 form ('file:%s?_journal_mode=WAL&_busy_timeout=5000'). 2) Stop swallowing: fetchers.go:305-307 and :318-320 must return the error — the HTTP layer at router.go:111-116 already has a correct 500 path with slog.Error, and the silent nilerr is precisely what let a total outage present as a per-ticker 503 for an unknown duration. 3) Regression test: assert GetHistory returns a non-empty slice against a fixture DB whose journal_mode is 'delete' — that is the exact condition that fails today and that a WAL-mode fixture would mask.
qa.misleading_alert_note: The kinh-dich 503 text is itself a defect amplifier and deserves a fix in the same pass or an immediate follow-up: price_score.go:32-41 collapses BOTH 'source fetch errored' and 'genuinely fewer than 7 points' into one nil return, which usecases.go:80/85/124/129 convert to ErrInsufficientData and router.go renders as 503 'requires at least 7 price points'. A total upstream outage is therefore reported as a thin-data condition — which is what steered this incident toward a per-ticker data-gap reading instead of a service outage.

(1) SEQUENCING PRECONDITION SATISFIED. This row deliberately gated itself on FIX-MCP-MEMORY-CODE-LEAK being DEPLOYED, not merely merged. It is deployed: running image sha256:115700a86e65 (Created 2026-08-06T23:21:36Z) post-dates fix commit 609f62800. The initDatabase() WeakSet guard IS live and working. Therefore the residual saturation measured below is NOT the initDatabase leak and this rows measurement is being taken against the correct image, exactly as its own SEQUENCING clause required.

(2) plan_only FIRST MOVE EXECUTED AND DISCHARGED. The row specified: "correlate /health sessionCount against MemPerc over several hours on the POST-deploy image before any code change". Done, on a 6h31m-old cold-started container: /health sessions = 871 -> 873 across an 84s window (~+86/h). That field is SseSessionManager.sessions.size (transport.ts:123-125, surfaced server.ts:494) = ACTIVE un-reaped entries, NOT a cumulative counter. "Sequential Market Analysis tool registered" = 4018 occurrences since boot = 4018 McpServer constructions in 6h31m, of which 873 were still resident -> roughly 78pct of sessions DO get reaped by res.on(close), the residual ~22pct never do. MemPerc 98.19-99.01pct across 22 probes in 2 independent windows. 2.974GiB / 873 sessions ~= 3.5MB per leaked session, consistent with an McpServer holding 183 registered tools. VmHWM ADVANCED 3170004 -> 3183020 kB DURING the observation window: high-water still climbing at the cap, not a stable sawtooth.

(3) TERMINAL EVENT — the correlation ended in a real death, observed live. Container FinishedAt 2026-08-07T05:57:26.041Z, StartedAt 05:57:26.416Z (375ms Docker auto-restart), RestartCount 0->1, OOMKilled=false ExitCode=0 = the fleets already-root-caused memory-death signature (identical to FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP), NOT a clean exit. Post-restart sessions=14, MemPerc 3.05->7.91pct. Time from cold start to death: 6h36m. This is the answer to "does the leak fix hold": the 609f62800 fix holds for what it targeted, and this second leak alone is sufficient to kill the container in under 7 hours.

(4) MECHANISM, source-read at apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/transport.ts — CONFIRMS the architect Finding 2 and adds WHY the existing cleanup cannot save it. handleSse() line 95 does `const mcpServer = this.createServer()`; that McpServer is a bare local, never stored on the instance and never .close()d. res.on("close") (lines 84-92) deletes ONLY the transport Map entry and the heartbeat interval. The only other eviction path is the heartbeat catch block (lines 69-78), which fires only if `res.write()` THROWS SYNCHRONOUSLY. Nodes res.write() on a broken pipe does not throw — it buffers and emits "error" on the socket. So for any client that vanishes without a clean FIN (the normal case for a killed/timed-out cowork agent or a dropped Cloudflare tunnel), NEITHER eviction path can fire and the Map entry is permanent. The documented "cleanup gated solely on res.on(close) or write-failure" is therefore, in practice, gated on res.on(close) ALONE — the write-failure branch is effectively dead code. No idle reaper, no max-age, no DELETE handler.

(5) DESIGN CONSTRAINT for architect: a reaper keyed on transport liveness alone is insufficient — it must also close the per-session McpServer (mcpServer.close()), otherwise the SDK-side registration graph for 183 tools stays reachable. Recommend: retain the McpServer alongside the transport in a single per-session record, add an idle/max-age reaper (last-activity timestamp bumped in handleMessage), and add a DELETE /sse handler. Correlate sessionCount against MemPerc post-fix to confirm.

(6) FILES[] PATH CORRECTED: this rows files[0] read apps/mcp-server/src/interface/transport.ts, which DOES NOT EXIST. Real path is apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/transport.ts. Corrected in place so architect/dev are not sent to a non-existent file.

# Improvement Proposal: coverage-stamp.sh mutex TTL below task_claim schema minimum (T1)

## Weakness

`scripts/agents-flow/coverage-stamp.sh` line 158 hardcodes `ttl_seconds:30` for its
`coverage-state:main` mutex `task_claim` call. The live `task_claim` MCP tool schema
enforces a minimum of 60. Every invocation of the script now fails input validation on
all 5 retry attempts and fail-CLOSED (no write performed) — this is not a transient
mutex-contention timeout, it is a permanent schema mismatch that cannot self-resolve by
retrying.

**Workaround applied:** flow doc `docs/agents/news-scout/flow/stage-log-notify.md` Step 7
already prescribes exactly this outcome for a genuine transport failure — SKIP the
coverage-state write for the cycle and log `[coverage-write-skipped: <reason>]` on the
WORK ping, never fall back to a full-file rewrite. news-scout followed that path this
cycle. **Non-fatal to this cycle's signal output, but the 48h staleness sweep
(`--list-stale`) that this same script also serves depends on `last_covered_news_scout`
timestamps actually landing — those timestamps have not been written by news-scout since
at least this cycle, degrading the sweep's future accuracy.**

## Evidence

**T1 Trigger — tool call returned error (task_claim input-validation failure) on all 5
retry attempts, every cycle, deterministically:**

```
[coverage-stamp] WARN: task_claim transport error (attempt 1/5): [mcp-call] ERROR: tool=task_claim isError=true: MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool task_claim: [ { "code": "too_small", "minimum": 60, "type": "number", ...
[coverage-stamp] WARN: task_claim transport error (attempt 2/5): ... (same error, attempts 2-5)
[coverage-stamp] ERROR: could not acquire coverage-state:main mutex after 5 attempts — fail-CLOSED, no write performed
```

Root cause confirmed by direct grep of the script:
`scripts/agents-flow/coverage-stamp.sh:158` — `ttl_seconds:30` literal, hardcoded, not
parameterised. This is a schema-vs-caller mismatch, not a load/contention issue — retrying
5, 50, or 500 times produces the identical validation error every time.

**Blast radius:** the script's own header comment (stage-log-notify.md Step 7, and the
matching step in `market-watcher`'s flow) states this mutex "serializ[es] against
market-watcher's own write (co-ships FIX-COVERAGE-STATE-CROSS-AGENT-LOST-UPDATE)" — i.e.
BOTH news-scout and market-watcher call this same script/mutex path, so the defect is
fleet-wide, not news-scout-specific. Flagged via `send_telegram(channel="bug")` this cycle
(message_id 5212) in addition to this DRAFT per PLAN-ONLY self-critique scope.

## Proposed Change

**What:** Raise `ttl_seconds:30` to a value ≥60 (e.g. 60, matching the schema floor
exactly, or a modest buffer such as 90) on `scripts/agents-flow/coverage-stamp.sh:158`.

**Why:** One-line literal change unblocks `coverage-state:main` mutex acquisition for
every future news-scout and market-watcher cycle, restoring `last_covered_*` staleness
tracking (currently frozen at whatever value each ticker held before the schema minimum
was raised to 60). No behavioral change beyond the TTL value itself — the mutex's
acquire/release/CAS logic is otherwise unaffected.

## Lane

**Lane A** — mechanical parameter fix in a support script; no gate/audit/success-criteria
change, no flow-logic change, no user-facing comprehensibility impact.

**Lane Rationale (C-3 answer):** Does this proposal edit gate/audit logic, loop success
criteria, an irreversible action, or user-facing comprehensibility? NO. It changes one
numeric literal in a mutex-acquisition call inside a support script; the coverage-state
write's own validation (jq surgical patch, CAS-guard) is untouched. Purely mechanical.

## Success Signal

- `coverage-stamp.sh --agent news-scout --tickers <...>` (or the market-watcher
  equivalent) exits 0 and reports a successful write instead of 5/5 `task_claim` failures.
- 2 consecutive news-scout cycles complete Step 7 without a `[coverage-write-skipped]`
  WORK-ping note.
- `docs/data/coverage-state.json` `.tickers[*].last_covered_news_scout` timestamps advance
  past 2026-08-13T12:11Z on the next successful cycle.

## Rollback

No rollback needed — single-literal value change, trivially revertible via git if it
somehow regresses (e.g. if some other caller relied on the invalid ttl_seconds=30 never
succeeding, which is not the case: the mutex acquisition is unconditionally attempted
every cycle today and unconditionally fails today).
